text.text:
An attractive brunch spot with highs and lows, tucked in to one of Belle Meade's strip malls. It's worth your time. The modern interior, with its stylish tile floor and open vibes, is very comfortable.  The food we tried was gorgeous, with the salmon toast draped in artfully sculpted watermelon radish and dill, and the quiche presented via a tall robust slice next to a mound of salad. We also tried the jiggly soufflé pancake, which was tasty, light, and fun, though a bit dry vs. the eggy-ness I expected. Big bonus points for the chai-spiced syrup though. On the downside, the egg sandwich on a "Japanese milk bun" was more basic than described. After many trips to Japan, I can safely say this is merely a decent standard brioche burger bun. You need to elevate a lot more to use the "J.M.B." title. Onion jam is always welcome though.

Service was a bit forgetful and slow, though well-intentioned. We had to re-request a coffee, ask for a refill, and for salt & pepper. It's a very young staff and they could learn to be a bit more solicitous. But they are forgiven easily. Overall, the effort to compose a refined alternative to standard west Nashville brunch options is appreciated, and I'll be back to check on their progress. Next time, for the vibes and to try the sandwich menu.

text.text:
More Than a Wine Store — It’s Family

I’ve been going to Triangle Wine in Cary for over 10 years, and I honestly don’t know why it’s taken me this long to write a review — this place is truly special.

The owners are wonderful and treat me like family every time I walk through the door. One of the most meaningful gestures was when they gifted me use of the back room to host my out-of-town friends and family the day before my baby shower. It meant so much — and it’s just one example of how kind and generous they are.

The staff is always attentive and welcoming. They know my wine preferences and never steer me wrong — their recommendations are always spot on! The wine selection is extensive, with something for every palate, and their events are not only top notch but also incredibly cost-friendly.

Triangle Wine isn’t just a place to buy wine — it’s a place where community, connection, and quality come together. Can’t say enough great things about it!

CHEERS

text.text:
I spent most of my life in this area and have been thrilled to welcome Cafe Mornings into my routine.

The drinks are stellar, the atmosphere of the dining area and patio are serene, and the food is amazing. Every detail of the business is thoughtful and intentional, and the owners and staff are always so friendly. text.text:
The place is loud with live music and a bar. You can get drinks in the attached bar or at the bar in the dance space. There is a hot dog stand outside and across the street as well.

Entry is cash only, unless you book tickets  beforehand with card. They do have an ATM at the entertance, for anyone who forgets cash cover.

Friendly bouncers and staff that are kind and helpful when needed.

There is a live DJ and during event nights and sometimes balloons and cotton candy available.

Bathrooms are generally clean but the bathrooms are fairly small, so there is often a wait as the night picks up.

Crowd doesn't usually pick up until about 10/10:30, but doors open at 9:00.

Free self-serve water is available at all times.

There is also a photo booth and a small set of couches and chairs to lounge on.

Occasional strobe lights and dim lighting can make navigation a challenge for some.

The only drawback is the place can be a bit dirty with sticky floors and rips and tears in the furniture. But...that just gives it character.

Plan to be a bit warm or dress lightly. There is a giant fan blowing, but the dance floor gets quite hot.

Overall a fun place to go, especially on theme nights. Everyone is welcome and the atmosphere is friendly.

text.text:
Three or four star butcher shop/deli but five star sandwich shop. Their sandwiches are reasonably priced and incredibly tasty especially the burger and anything they have with bacon in it.

I am forgiving a lot by giving them five stars but they seriously have one of the best burgers in NYC at any price point but especially for 15 bucks. The meat is super high quality, well seasoned and has tons of cheese. The size is impressive for the price too, it's a meaty smash burger that puts 7th Street to shame.

Not every sandwich on the menu is a knockout, the roast beef has like no meat on it for some reason but their bacon is incredible and the breakfast sandwiches like the green eggs are solid. Love the BLT with heirloom tomatoes when it's in season.

Now for the bad, the tips at the register are crazy, like 18% is the lowest tip suggestion and you get hit up for a tip for every order even charcuterie, meat, or grocery items. I gotta push back on this, it always annoys me when counter service places try to squeeze tips out of customers.

Their charcuterie is not the best and very expensive. I haven't been blown away by anything. The selection isn't great,and most things are not worth the price. Their Iberico Chorizo is solid but a lot of their charcuterie are not that interesting or curated in any way. Just a hodge podge of overpriced meats. I assume many of them are local because there would be no other reason to carry them.

A lot of the stuff they carry in the store part of the business is not worth the prices they charge but as a sandwich spot they are five stars all day. Also, be warned that the sandwiches take forever to make especially on the weekends.

It is quite pricy (each cup is $5 minimum) and there are some remarkable chocolates but bars are $10+.

I highly recommend visiting Kinka.

text.text:
Kitty’s is a charming little spot conveniently located right next to the Amtrak station in Hudson, which makes it a great stop whether you're coming into town or heading out. The location alone is a major plus.
The shop offers a wide variety of items, ranging from pantry goods to drinks and baked treats. However, when it comes to fresh food options—especially in the morning—the menu is a bit limited. In fact, the only breakfast meal on offer is an egg and cheese sandwich. That said, it’s a solid one—well-made, satisfying, and flavorful. It also comes with the option of a hash brown on the side, which I definitely recommend. Crispy, well-seasoned, and just the right portion. I do believe that they are priced on the bit of the higher end.

They also had a selection of baked goods on display. While I didn’t get the chance to try them, they looked fresh and genuinely tempting. As tasty as they look, I wasn’t willing to pay what I thought was an excessive price for baked goods that weren’t even coming from the bakery.

Overall, Kitty’s is worth a visit, especially if you're looking for a quick, tasty bite before hopping on a train or exploring Hudson. Just don’t expect a full brunch menu—come for the quality, not the quantity.

I recently had the pleasure of visiting La Mer Seafood, and I must say that I was thoroughly impressed with my experience. Under the new ownership of Sean, the fish shop has really flourished into a top-notch establishment that is definitely worth a visit.

One of the highlights of my visit was the amazing Poke Bowl which was made to order!  All of the seafood was fresh and delicious, and it was clear that a lot of care had gone into selecting only the best quality products.

Aside from the delicious seafood, the service at La Mer Seafood was also top-notch. The staff were friendly, knowledgeable, and incredibly accommodating, making for a truly enjoyable shopping experience. It's clear that Sean and his team are passionate about providing their customers with the best possible service and ensuring that they leave completely satisfied.

Overall, I would highly recommend La Mer Seafood to anyone who is looking for a high-quality fish shop with a great selection of fresh seafood and an amazing team behind it. Whether you're a seasoned seafood lover or simply looking to try something new, La Mer Seafood is definitely worth a visit.

text.text:
Popped in to LB Kitchen for lunch on a Tuesday afternoon around 12:30. I immediately loved the whole vibe of the restaurant. There is a refrigerated section with grab and go food options along with a well curated drink selection as well as a significant pantry section with healthy snack, treats, protein bars etc. We placed our order at the counter and were able to snag one of only a handful of indoor tables.

I should honestly be removing one star at this point because our salads took a full 30 minutes to come out. Tables that ordered waaaay after us were getting their food but I ended up enjoying my food so much that I don't want to deduct the star.

I had the kale caesar, add jammy egg and sweet potato, dressing on the side and my husband had the LB bowl, add chicken. The bowls are a little on the pricey side especially with the add ons but if I lived in Portland I would be ordering from here all of the time!

text.text: Sometimes… it all comes together and the magic happens. As a former NYC restaurant owner, I know how hard it is to maintain a cohesive vision that shines through the entire dining experience from first look to dessert. The building is beautiful, inside and out. The adjacent bottle shop is a charming convenience and lends a village feel to the approach. Inside the space is divided between a warm taverna style area and a soaring light, minimal industrial dinning area. Everything is tasteful and in its right place. Service was extraordinary. The entire staff moves in calm, graceful choreography attending to guests with warmth and attentiveness. Sophia, our server,  created an instant bond and made us feel like regulars and old friends as only the best of front of house staff can do. Beer list is tight and on point (don’t sleep on the Baby Kittens from Fat Orange Cat). Wine list is broad and well constructed. Cocktails list was creative and balanced with a stellar mocktail option. The menu is well put together and features the perfect meeting of new American and asian influences. Standouts were the duck bao (which after one bite, I looked at Beth and said “ooohhh! That’s MY food exactly”), the shrimp burger (slightly spicy with Vietnamese vibes) to the roasted 1/2 chicken with togarashi. Flavors were bold and inventive. Everything we ate was cooked and plated perfectly. I rarely end a meal with nothing to critique, but, well, I have nothing but superlatives here. Do note that the kitchen closes around 8:30 PM even on weekends

text.text:
Japanese café located behind a small gourmet grocer with mellow, modern drinks.

Stumbled upon this place while wandering the neighborhood in search of coffee. From the outside, it looked like just another curated grocery store, but tucked in the back was a quiet little cafe. No indoor seating in the cafe, just two small tables near the entrance and a few outside.

Between the two drinks I tried—the Brown Sugar Coffee and the Iced Black Sesame Foam Hoji—the latter was my favorite. One of the employees suggested I try the Brown Sugar Coffee as a latte, but I opted for it black. In hindsight, I probably should’ve taken their advice. It ended up tasting more like a sweetened Dunkin' coffee than a refined house special.

The hoji, though, was fantastic. An ultra-creamy hojicha latte topped with black sesame milk foam. Hojicha and black sesame flavors overlapped a bit, but overall, it was a soft, nutty echo that blended well with the roasted tea notes without any graininess.

If you’re into Japanese-style café drinks with a modern twist, this one’s worth checking out.

text.text: This Chelsea Market shop sells a variety of Asian foods, both prepared meals/snacks and pantry items. There are different stations to place your order and pick up depending on what you’re ordering. My friend and I ordered bubble tea. I got a cocoa oolong milk tea with pearls and she got the Chelsea drink which is strawberry milk. Pearl River Mart doesn’t have its own seating, but there are other general seating areas in the market.

Stock Culinary Goods is the cooking store to end all other cooking stores!

Every time I go in, the staff are incredibly helpful and knowledgeable, making every visit nothing short of delightful. Their selection is unmatched—Rancho Gordo beans (a cult favorite and nearly impossible to find in stores), beautifully designed Kinto mugs from Japan in every size and color, locally milled flours from Maine, and even Rhode Island classics like Wright’s Dairy coffee milk. text.text:
Nice Brunch in the countryside.

Got this place recommended by a colleague and came for brunch this past weekend. We arrived a little after noon, and despite being well outside any major town, the restaurant was completely packed. The only open spot was an outdoor table swarmed by wasps. We agreed to take it, but the staff kindly moved us indoors as soon as a table opened up.

The menu here leaned into that familiar farm-to-table, ingredient-driven fusion style you’d commonly find in bigger cities. The dinner menu looked more inventive and truer to their philosophy, and we wished we had time to stay in the area to try it. The upside of brunch, though, was getting to try a few items from their bakery section.

We started off with the seared banana bread, and it was the best griddled version I’ve had. Denser and less crumbly than most, with layers of honey, olive oil, salt, and espresso all working together seamlessly.
Next was the cauliflower agrodolce, which every nearby table seemed to order. The stewed beans in the agrodolce sauce were comforting and familiar, while the fioretto cauliflower (my first time trying it) maintained its crunch even after steaming.

In the Chicken & Waffle, the waffle was meh but the chicken & slaw were fantastic. They used fennel and ginger aioli to give it a more distinctive aroma, and it really worked well with the chili garlic maple glaze on the chicken.

On the side, we also tried the cod chowder, a lighter, herbier take on the usual New England style. The broth was clean and brothy, and while the cod itself was a tad rubbery, I liked the refreshing finish. Only thing we didn’t like were the pancakes. Not bad, just plain compared to everything else on the table.

Would definitely come back for dinner next time we’re in the area.

In the Chicken & Waffle, the waffle was meh but the chicken & slaw were fantastic. They used fennel and ginger aioli to give it a more distinctive aroma, and it really worked well with the chili garlic maple glaze on the chicken.

On the side, we also tried the cod chowder, a lighter, herbier take on the usual New England style. The broth was clean and brothy, and while the cod itself was a tad rubbery, I liked the refreshing finish. Only thing we didn’t like were the pancakes. Not bad, just plain compared to everything else on the table.

Would definitely come back for dinner next time we’re in the area.

The soup and salad bar is self serve. The service is mediocre, depending on the individual staff. Some are more willing to smile and engage with customers while some are just rude and can't even seem to properly take an order. When you're providing service it's very detrimental for your business if you don't train your staff properly. The bakery has really tasty pastries and cookies. I would definitely go back to try other things on the deli menu despite the mediocre service, but I have explored and discovered lots of good local delis in the area and will take my business where they have good customer service versus some where with mediocre service. I would've given a five star review if service was better, but I feel the 4 star is already quite generous. My fish and chips were okay, the salt and vinegar fries were really good, and the club sandwich was good.

text.text:
La Fermière is my favorite yogurt company. They are a family-owned French yogurt company that has been around since 1952. They recently added a line of French Desserts. The Boise Co-op in Boise, is the only place in Southern Idaho that is carrying them. They have three of the five flavors. I’ve tried all three. I started with the one that I expected to be my least favorite, CRÈME CARAMEL, because I don’t particularly care for caramel. Surprise! Surprise! It turned out to be my favorite of three flavors. The Vanilla and Chocolate flavors are good, but they don’t begin to compare to the Caramel flavor. La Fermière’s CRÈME CARAMEL is one of the best things I’ve eaten in 2024!

French Crème Caramel is a vanilla custard that’s baked on top of a layer of caramelized sugar, served upside down with a caramel sauce pouring over the sides. It’s somewhat similar to Flan in flavor, but closer to a crème brûlée in texture. La Fermière’s Crème Caramel incorporates the caramelized sugar/caramel, into the vanilla custard.

The Boise Co-op in Boise also has the most flavors of La Fermière yogurt. The second best location is the Boise Co-op in Meridian, which has yogurt, but none of the desserts.

Highly Recommended!!!

P.S. I recommend calling the Boise Co-op to make sure this product is in stock before you go to pick some up.

I asked him what info the store collects, he said I only see your information on the screen. You're not allowed to scan my ID without asking. If you ask me, I can say yes and proceed with the purchase or decide to leave without purchasing. I would have left the store. There are civil cases in Oregon regarding this matter. Liqour laws DO NOT require scanning ID. Ask first, give your customers a choice or you may get sued. I will buy liquor elsewhere. Unfortunately I will buy less groceries as a result.

LOVE Central Co-op!!! Have moved too far away now and I really miss going for my stock-up shopping. The staff are fantastic and the store is welcoming and comfortable to shop. Great bulk sections incl. herbs/spices, oils/vinegars, tea & coffee beans (w/grinder available), soap/shampoo, local eggs & regular dry bulk. Also can do special orders of large amounts like cases.

There's also a coffee & deli bar & good bread selection. You can spread out lifetime membership cost in  payments. They also graciously became a City of Seattle Fresh Bucks grocer!

I've come & gone from Seattle many times over 30+ years & shopped Central Co-op since before they moved & changed name. They're a block from the new rapid bus line & have free parking in their garage. Pretty easy spot to catch a Lyft too.

Thanks for all the great years & hope to be back soon ☺️🌈🐾

text.text:
Is there a store policy that prohibits cashiers from helping w/bagging? If so, please make it transparent.

Today I had bagged most of my stuff and had about 5 small items, such as a piece of ginger, left to bag when I had to pay. The cashier could have easily tossed those items in my bag while waiting for me to pay, but instead stared at me as I paid, very purposefully not helping.

I love Central Co-op, the produce and bulk sections are the best around, but these types of interactions really negatively impact my experience as a customer. And these type of instances have happened so many times to me at central co-op that I finally felt I should write a negative review.

Dear management, please make your bagging policies clear, since your staff doesn’t seem to help customers bag. And if your staff is so unhappy, maybe there is something wrong—are you paying them enough? Whatever is happening, it’s making me avoid shopping at a place that I would ordinarily love.

5 Stars – A Canby Gem!
Cutsforth’s Market is truly one of the best local hangouts in Canby. From the monthly car shows that bring the community together to the unbeatable half-off donuts after 5pm, there’s always something to look forward to here. The bakery is absolutely amazing—everything fresh and full of flavor—and the deli never disappoints with its quality and variety. The selection throughout the store is unique, with items you won’t find anywhere else. Whether you’re here for groceries, a treat, or just to soak in the small-town charm, Cutsforth’s always delivers.

text.text:
DPA Application to Food Supply & Security Narratives

Context

The Somali piracy/insurgency analogy has been used to frame local food security disruptions as evidence of fragility in the U.S. domestic system. In this narrative, looting, shortages, or coercion in food distribution are equated with insurgent control over shipping lanes. This frame—if left unaddressed—can destabilise confidence in both government and private supply chains.

DPA Authority
•	The Defence Production Act (DPA) empowers the federal government to prioritise and direct private industry in the interest of national defence.
•	“National defence” under the DPA is not limited to military readiness—it includes critical infrastructure, disaster response, and food security.
•	Grocers, distributors, and logistics providers can be compelled to cooperate under DPA authority to ensure steady supply, prevent hoarding, and avoid private-sector practices that create unnecessary scarcity.

Strategic Rationale
•	Prevents insurgent narrative capture: By securing grocery supply chains under DPA authority, the U.S. avoids the perception that local conditions are deteriorating into “warlord economies.”
•	Undercuts adversary analogies: When shelves remain stocked and rationing is orderly, the Somali comparison collapses.
•	Limits liability for grocers: DPA provides legal cover for grocers who comply with federal directives, reducing the risk of civil or criminal suits for perceived discrimination or negligence.

Implementation Guidance
•	Federal designation of grocers as “essential infrastructure” under the DPA.
•	Coordinated requirements for minimum reserve stocks and controlled release in emergencies.
•	Clear messaging: “This is not martial law. It is supply chain stabilisation under federal authority.”
•	Partnership with local law enforcement and National Guard to protect grocer staff, while ensuring store personnel not explicitly assigned to security are shielded from liability and danger.

Outcome
•	Reframes food supply from a “Somali piracy” metaphor into a federally protected national security function.
•	Positions the state as proactive rather than reactive, reducing adversary leverage in narrative warfare.
•	Provides continuity of access to critical resources while avoiding escalation into civil rights or labour liability traps.

Just check the photo's for yourselves. So, if your just gaga about bratwurst that's non commercial and honestly made, you know where to go now.

text.text:
A Hidden Gem for Fresh, Customizable, and Health-Conscious Eats

My Fresh Basket is a fantastic find for anyone who values fresh, organic, and health-conscious grocery options. The store is packed with organic, gluten-free, dairy-free, and other specialty items, and the produce section was especially impressive—vibrant, well-stocked, and clearly fresh.

One of my favorite features was the poke-by-the-pound bar. We picked up 1.5 pounds of fresh salmon poke, sampling three different flavor profiles, and paired it with our choice of salads and vegetables to build our own poke bowls. Compared to a typical poke restaurant, this experience felt more customizable, more generous in portion size, and surprisingly more affordable. At $20 per pound, it’s not cheap, but considering the quality, freshness, and flexibility, it felt like a smart and satisfying choice—especially for a hungry lunch.

text.text: I've been coming here for years and it's a great place if you're able bodied, independent, and already have a detailed store map embedded in your brain. If you're like me and don't know where stuff is and need some assistance bagging and carrying groceries due to a temporary disability, God help you. I've honestly started to question whether there's a CO leak wafting through the vents because every time I come in here the employees are wandering around like dazed sloths. I actually had a stocker glare at me today because I was apparently in his way; not once did he ask if I needed help finding anything, and I was too put off by his sour demeanor to ask. Also, the whole universal co-op thing around making customers bag their own groceries is beyond weird to me to begin with, but when an elderly person and a disabled person are back to back in your line and are both clearly struggling to bag their groceries, it's common decency to offer assistance. Instead, they just stare at you and act annoyed that the line is jammed up. The entitlement and snobbery here really sprinkles a nice dose of the infamous PNW freeze on the groceries. Makes everything taste better, I guess? I'm not sure what the deal is with the employees, but for a supposedly liberal, inclusive entity, I could not feel less welcome.

I always feel just a bit pretentious when I'm at this PCC. That feeling isn't the fault of PCC, it's likely because it is in Issaquah after all. ; ) I can say that ... I live in the Highlands.

The staff are very friendly, helpful and kind and this is something you should expect. When comparing prices to their competition in the area, Trader Joe's, Whole Foods via Amazon Prime Now 2 hour grocery delivery and Safeway, PCC loses in every way. PCC however wins on variety against the LOCAL brick and mortar stores. The variety I'm speaking of is for organic, vegetarian, or vegan. For example, if you want strawberries, PCC will be $6.99 for a pack, Safeway 3.99, Trader Joe's $3.99 or $2.99. However if you want Vegetarian or Vegan Lasagna, PCC will have several, whereas Safeway or Trader Joe's will have 1 to 2 options.

For me price wins Every time before variety and PCC prices are simply to high when the same times are cheaper within a 5 minute drive.

Let me preface by saying this is a great store in downtown. They have a lot of quality products including groceries, clothing, kitchenware, and a solid wine selection. BUT they have some of the most unfriendly staff, I always feel like an unwelcome burden when I'm in their grocery and deli areas.

They have the BEST sandwiches (better than Pickles in both flavor and price) but even with the simple order form, I feel like I'm bothering the deli with my order (specifically, the two older women who work there), if the sandwiches weren't so good, I wouldn't bother just to avoid the brief but always unpleasant social interaction. They once even compared my presence to a fruit fly because I was waiting in the general area for a sandwich.

This review could easily be 5 stars, but with the sour attitudes I can't give that, which is disappointing.

X Marks the Spot!

Ahoy, savvy shoppers! If you're in the mood for a retail adventure, set your sights on Star Store, the mercantile marvel that's more like a treasure hunt than a typical shopping spree.

First challenge: finding the entrance. This place is so cleverly concealed, you’ll feel like Indiana Jones deciphering clues to unearth hidden gems. Hint: follow the quirky signs, it’s all part of the adventure!

Once inside, prepare to be dazzled. The store is a labyrinth of eclectic finds, each aisle a new quest waiting to be conquered. From trinkets to artisanal crafts, you’ll discover treasures you didn’t even know you needed. It's like a Pinterest board exploded in the best way possible.

The staff? Absolute legends. They’re like your personal treasure maps, guiding you to the best finds with a wink and a smile. Got a question? They’ve got answers as golden as pirate loot.

The vibe? Think rustic charm meets whimsical wonderland. It’s cozy, quirky, and absolutely Instagram-worthy. Every corner is a new adventure, perfect for snapping pics that’ll make all your friends ask, Where on earth did you find that?!

In short, Star Store is a retail escapade that’s worth every twist and turn. So grab your treasure map (aka your sense of adventure) and dive into the mercantile magic. Trust me, the hunt is half the fun, and the finds are simply priceless. Happy hunting!

text.text:
Top of the Hill Market is the highlight of my week.  If you think shopping for produce, groceries, and meats is a chore, dread no more! The produce & meats are higher quality than I find in those massive, faceless grocery chains because Damu, Jackie, and the crew really do actually care and take pride in everything they provide.

The atmosphere of the place is even a breath of fresh air, especially when they bring out all of the produce, flowers, seedlings and starts in the spring!

It's not just customer service; they are genuinely happy to help you and know how your day is going. I look forward to seeing the gang and talk, it always leaves a smile on my face. I just wish I lived closer.

In a world where all of the grocery chains are becoming a faceless monopoly, and where food deserts are growing larger, it's nice to have this oasis of quality and friendliness.

text.text: I’ve been wanting to post this for literally years now but have felt like such a Karen but Jesus too many times. i have worked customer service, so many restaurant jobs. And I am sure that Whole Foods employees don’t want to also deal with Amazon returns. I actually really do get it, it’s gotta be an annoying part of the job. They use every opportunity to force us to use the glitchy return kiosks even when they aren’t busy assisting customers. Unfortunately that is something that is part of their job and yet the way they treat customers coming in with returns is always rude and somewhat appalling. Often dehumanizing. When trying to return an item today, there was a very long line of people standing to use the kiosk while two employees stood nearby doing nothing. I truly hate to say that but they really were not doing a single thing. Truly standing nearby and not helping or doing any other work. To make matters worse, an older woman was clearly struggling with the kiosk while the line backed up - the employees at customer service just watched her the entire time, without offering to assist her or any of the other half dozen people that standing in the doorway when they could have been helping us. When I finally stepped forward to ask if the employees could assist us, I was met with eye rolls and attitude from the employee AND the customers who assumed I was trying to cut/am just a rude person in a hurry. It’s actually my day off. In reality this is always the experience and customer service is always nonexistent for Amazon customers and returns in Whole Foods and I am tired of being treated this way every time I am forced to go in. Tired of watching older adults struggle while 20 year olds idle apathetically nearby and then probably complain about their low wages. I always always try to go to UPS because they are so, so much kinder than the  WF employees (who probably also use Amazon themselves). In reality it’s frustrating to feel dehumanized by other humans who were hired to provide customer service but would rather stand behind a counter and act like *you’re* the inconvenience for coming in to their place of employment.

text.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 5/5 — A Grocery Experience That Sets the Bar

Whole Foods Market has completely redefined what I expect from a grocery store. From the moment you walk in, you’re met with vibrant, fresh produce that looks like it was harvested that morning—and in many cases, it probably was. The layout is clean, well-organized, and inviting, making it easy to browse even when you’re not sure what you came in for.

What really sets Whole Foods Market apart is the quality of its offerings. Whether it’s their responsibly sourced meats, organic pantry staples, or their incredible prepared foods section, everything feels thoughtfully curated. I especially appreciate their commitment to transparency in labeling, which makes shopping with dietary needs (gluten-free, plant-based, etc.) so much easier.

The staff is consistently helpful and knowledgeable—ready to recommend a new product or help you find something obscure without hesitation. And let’s not forget the hot bar and bakery section, which often feels like a hidden gem of a restaurant tucked inside a grocery store.

Yes, prices are a bit higher than average, but you truly get what you pay for: quality, sustainability, and a better overall shopping experience. If you’re someone who values clean ingredients and ethical sourcing, Whole Foods Market is absolutely worth it.

I've been a WF customer for many years, and of this store for 15+. I appreciate the staff, quality, and selection (most of the time). The sales are always something I keep an eye on, and love the 50% department sales.
Things that drive me nuts:
Self-checkout as the only option at times. While I am fine using it at times, I do not like self checking a big ole order of produce and having to call someone over for sales. It feels like I am working for free and at times see mom's with littles or older folks struggling with the ordeal - because self checkout of more than a handful of items can be an ordeal.
Deli. Sometimes there are people hard at work back there, but part of their work seems to be intentionally avoiding customers. Standing there without even an acknowledgement is annoying and, frankly, rude. I especially found the time when I was diligently waiting forever then finally told the deli was close - this was around 4pm so not in the just before close time.
Stocking. Sometimes, especially in produce, there can be very slim pickings. I get it when there are storms and such to delay travel to CO, but when it seems to be regularly happening it is frustrating.

text.text:
Whole Foods is a go-to for many in Seattle looking for high quality, organic or natural foods, especially if you care about produce, specialty dietary items, or ready-to-eat meals. The stores are almost always clean, well-lit, and organized, which makes shopping there pleasant. The selection tends to be strong—fresh fruits & vegetables, vegan/plant-based items, gluten-free options, a large deli/prepared foods section, and plenty of organic groceries.  ￼

One of the highlights is their hot food / buffet / prepared meals area: convenient for grabbing lunch or dinner without having to cook, and often quite good in taste and variety. The Roosevelt Square location, for instance, earns praise for having “very good food” and “extensive salad bar and hot food buffet.”  ￼

On the downside: cost. Whole Foods tends to be pricier than many other grocery stores, particularly for more common staples. If you’re price-sensitive, you’ll notice.  ￼ Some locations have had issues with stock gaps or limited variety in certain categories (especially since staffing and supply chain changes over recent years).  ￼

Customer service is mixed but generally favorable: staff are often helpful, especially in specialty or prepared food sections. Some customers have had less positive experiences in certain stores around enforcement of store rules (e.g. pets, etc.) or during busy times.  ￼

If you shop at Whole Foods, it’s best when: you want organic/specialty items, you’re okay paying a premium, and want convenience + variety in one place. It’s less ideal for bargain-hunting or when you want the absolute lowest price for basics.

I really like this Whole Foods and shop here almost every week. The seafood and meat are always fresh, and I often buy daily essentials here as well. In the past, every staff member I met was very professional and friendly.

However, on the evening of September 11 around 8 PM in the seafood section, I had a very disappointing experience. I stood at the counter waiting for about 5 minutes. I clearly saw the staff member in front of me, but instead of acknowledging me, she turned away and walked off. She kept moving around and ignored my needs until I finally went up to her and asked for shrimp. On top of that, her packaging skills were very poor — the bag was messy and not properly packed.

This made my shopping experience very unpleasant, to the point that I don’t feel like coming back to buy seafood here again.

text.text: This is the original Whole Foods in Berkeley, I believe. It’s been here for at least 35 years, probably more. The store could use a little bit of updating, but that’s not a big deal. But a bigger deal is that the parking is limited, and there’s really no place else to go except in their small parking lot, which is often full. This is not a problem unique to Whole Foods, many places in Berkeley have the same issues. The bakery is good. The hot food bar is excellent, I wish they still had a soup that they haven’t had in a few years, the butternut squash crab bisque, which was the best. Their pizza is excellent, and their selection of fish and meat is very good considering how small the store is. And like all Whole Foods, the produce is excellent, albeit a little bit pricey. Whole Foods in general tends to be on the pricier side, but their own store brands are reasonable and good.

We were in a rush to buy a few specific items the day before Thanksgiving, so we ordered them online from Whole Foods Market and set them up for pickup on our way home. This was my first time doing this, and I had no idea what to expect. We got there, pulled over, and went into one of the special pickup spots. We let them know (on the app) that we were there. Within a couple of minutes, someone knocked on the window and handed us two bags with all the items we had ordered. Very impressed, we started to leave but realized we had forgotten a few things! You know how that goes?!

So, we parked the car and walked in. I should add that this was not my first time in Whole Foods at this location or altogether, but it had been a while since my last visit. The store was busy, as we had predicted, but things were moving fast. We had to ask an associate about one of the items, and she pointed us right to it. The store is well organized and orderly. Within a few minutes, we found everything we needed. Along the way, I passed by the hot food section and was reminded of all the times I was single and had to pick up something to eat on my way home, and this Whole Foods location came to my delicious rescue.

Anyhow, this was a very good experience, and I made a mental note to stop by here next time we need something, even though it is just a bit further from home than I would prefer. For anyone considering using Whole Foods for pickup or shopping in-store, I can say that both options are convenient, and the staff is helpful. The online ordering process is simple and efficient, and the in-store experience, even when busy, is smooth and well-organized.

In the vibrant locale of San Ramon, Whole Foods stands as a bastion of mindful consumerism, exemplifying the Stoic virtues of temperance and discernment. This emporium of organic abundance presents a veritable cornucopia of ethically-sourced produce, from crisp greens to succulent fruits, all meticulously curated to satisfy the refined palates of health-conscious patrons.

Amidst the bustling aisles, one finds not mere products, but a testament to the Stoic principle of living in harmony with nature. The shelves teem with a rich tapestry of sustainably-sourced goods, each item a testament to the interplay between humanity and the environment. From artisanal cheeses to wholesome grains, every offering resonates with the Stoic ideal of embracing simplicity and authenticity in one's consumption choices.

Moreover, Whole Foods in San Ramon serves as a beacon of community engagement, fostering connections among like-minded individuals who share a commitment to wellness and environmental stewardship. Through educational initiatives, culinary workshops, and partnerships with local growers, the store cultivates a sense of shared purpose, echoing the Stoic ethos of finding fulfillment in service to others and the greater good.

Thus, within the hallowed halls of Whole Foods, one discovers not merely a grocery store, but a sanctuary for the Stoic soul—a place where the pursuit of virtue finds expression in the choices we make, the products we select, and the communities we nourish.

The store itself is fine, it's a typical Whole Foods. The one star rating is for the overall typical experience at this particular store.

Rushing. That's what 99% of the people in there do, so very mindlessly. As if their next stop is the super duper ultra experience of a lifetime and they just can't wait to get there. And it's not just other shoppers rushing, employees rush around too. So much mindless rushing in one little store is an unbearable experience.

Whole Foods obviously can't control the type of people who enter their stores so I don't hold that against them, I've only had bad experiences at one other Whole Foods location and that was on the east coast and also due to the behavior of the other shoppers. At all other Whole Foods I've shopped at in between the east coast and west coast I've had excellent experiences.

This is basically just a warning to people who understand that life is better lived without mindless rushing and are wiser than those who do rush: avoid this store unless you're so far along in your healing journey that not even lack of spatial awareness, selfishness, and mindless rushing don't trigger you. Personally I've never felt so overwhelmed by the behavior of others as I have at this location.

text.text:
A Bay Area Gem (with a Parking Caveat!)
For anyone in the Bay Area seeking top-notch groceries and an overall pleasant shopping experience, the Fremont Whole Foods Market truly stands out as one of my absolute favorites.
Right from the moment you step in, the store exudes a sense of quality that's hard to beat. What truly sets this location apart for me is the meat and seafood counter. The staff here are consistently awesome – knowledgeable, friendly, and always ready to offer helpful advice or custom cuts. It's a genuine pleasure to shop there, knowing you're getting both high-quality products and excellent service.
Areas for Improvement
While the in-store experience is fantastic, there's one significant hurdle: the parking. It can be quite a struggle to find a spot, especially during peak hours, which can definitely detract from an otherwise enjoyable trip.
Overall Recommendation
Despite the parking challenge, the Fremont Whole Foods is a definite go-to. The superior quality of their products, especially the impressive meat and seafood selection, combined with the outstanding customer service from their dedicated staff, makes it well worth the effort. It's a true culinary destination in the Bay Area!

text.text:
I’ve always had great experiences shopping at this Whole Foods, so today felt a little out of the ordinary. When I went to check out, the cashier, Marshel, seemed a bit disengaged and not very enthusiastic. She asked what fruit I had, and I let her know it was starfruit, mentioning that they’re quite fragile on the edges. Unfortunately, they were still handled a bit roughly and ended up being dropped back into the box.

This felt especially disappointing because starfruit is very meaningful to me and my family—it’s my husband’s favorite fruit, and such a rare treat for us to find one that’s actually sweet. It’s taken us nearly a decade to come across starfruit like this, so I was hoping it would be handled with extra care.

I reminded her that I preferred to keep them carefully in the box, but she just gave a quick acknowledgment without much care. I typically prefer to give my feedback directly in the store. However, at the end of our checkout, the heavy handling of the produce and groceries was enough to wake up my baby in the stroller, so I wasn’t able to share my concerns to management in the moment.

I’m not sure if Marshel is new—she only had a sticker for a name tag—and I know starting a new job can be overwhelming. Hopefully with more time and support, she’ll feel more comfortable and engaged, since most of the staff here have always provided wonderful service.

Whole Foods has consistently been my favorite place to shop, and I trust that this was just an off day

The parking is also not swell because there's so many other restaurants, fitness places, Sephora, etc. going on here. I am sure you will manage but you may have to park outside the main parking lot right in front.

I visited Whrays Grocery Store recently and was deeply disturbed by the behavior of two employees. While shopping, I overheard them making openly racist and politically charged comments right in front of customers, myself included. It was uncomfortable and unsettling, especially since such discussions have no place in a professional setting.

As a customer, I expect to feel welcome and respected when I visit a store. It’s disheartening that Whrays allowed this kind of inappropriate behavior to occur without any intervention. I understand that people have personal views, but it’s crucial for employees, especially in public-facing roles, to maintain professionalism and avoid discussing sensitive, divisive topics in front of customers.

I sincerely hope that Whrays takes steps to ensure this doesn’t happen again.

text.text:
I’ve been a loyal customer here for nearly my entire adult life, but after my recent experience I won’t be coming back.

I purchased a 6-pack of beer, and immediately after getting home and taking it out of the bag, the bottom collapsed and beer spilled all over my garage. I went back to the store within 10 minutes, showed the employee the defective packaging and photos of the mess, but instead of speaking to me directly, the manager hid in her office and made her employee go back and forth. She then falsely claimed that “per Washington state law” they couldn’t do anything since the alcohol left the store. That is absolutely untrue.

When I later called the store manager, Steph, she was dismissive and rude, saying she couldn’t do anything but would “pass a note” to the owner. It’s now been two weeks and I’ve heard nothing.

Not only are the prices here higher than other stores, but the customer service is dishonest and unprofessional. Lying to a loyal customer to save a few bucks is the perfect example of stepping over a dollar to pick up a penny. They’ve lost a longtime customer over something that could have been easily resolved.

text.text:
I went to Erewhon to try Hailey Bieber’s limited edition Strawberry Glaze Skin Smoothie, and it was definitely an experience. The smoothie is packed with skin-loving ingredients like collagen, hyaluronic acid, sea moss gel, avocado, coconut cream, dates, and Harry’s Berries strawberries, so it feels like more than just a drink it’s almost like a beauty ritual in a cup. The presentation is beautiful and very Instagram-worthy, and you do get a sense of luxury when holding it.

That said, it comes with a high price tag, which makes sense since it’s made with all organic, premium ingredients. The taste was good, but honestly, I found it a bit too sweet for my liking. Personally, I think it would be healthier and more enjoyable without the maple syrup, since the fruit already gives plenty of natural sweetness. The portion size is generous almost like a meal replacement and I couldn’t quite finish the whole thing because it was so filling.

text.text:
Erewhon is one of those places that’s constantly talked about on social media — mostly for being pricey and celebrity-approved. So naturally, when I was in LA, I had to check it out for myself… and honestly, I get the hype.

First off, the store is absolutely beautiful and fully stocked with everything you could possibly want — and then some. From fresh produce to organic snacks, supplements, beauty products, and hot meals — it’s a wellness paradise. Everything here is organic, high quality, and thoughtfully curated. It’s not your average grocery store, and it doesn’t try to be.

Of course, I had to try the famous Hailey Bieber Smoothie, and yes — it’s $20, but it was so good. Creamy, fresh, and surprisingly sweet despite being made with no added sugar. The ingredients include Malk Organic Almond Milk, bananas, strawberries, avocado, dates, sea moss, coconut cream, Vital Proteins collagen, and more — all top-tier stuff. The use of stevia didn’t leave that weird aftertaste either, which totally impressed me. It’s rare to find a smoothie that tastes this indulgent while still being clean and nourishing.

I also picked up some keto desserts, hummus, and nachos, and every single item was fresh and delicious. You can really tell they prioritize ingredient quality.

I visited on a weekday evening, and it wasn’t crowded at all. I found parking on the street without any trouble (a small win in LA!). The staff was polite and the vibe inside was chill — not chaotic or overly "influencer-y," which I kind of expected.

Yes, it’s definitely not cheap, but if you’re someone who values clean eating and wants to splurge a little on high-quality food, Erewhon is 100% worth the visit — even if just once for the experience.

I adore this market. I stopped shopping at Whole Foods & Trader Joe’s a while ago for personal & political reasons, so I’ve been searching for a Specialty Store with the healthiest options. You can’t go wrong here… this specific location has attentive & caring staff inside with lots of extra parking outside (two distant lots).

I must say, it is a tad small for the crowds they can receive & the aisles can feel tight and claustrophobic depending on the season & time of day. I find that once you determine a comfortable time to shop & get to know where things are, it’s a breeze. The line is never long somehow, the cashiers are diligent and security is present workout being overbearing. The seating area outside is cute & while it’s usually busy, it’s never too full.

No pretentiousness, just amazing finds, delicious fresh fare and the best beverage section in all of Silver Lake! You HAVE to try their namesake canned kombucha in Pink Salt Lemonade, IT’S MY FAVORITE!! I also collect their glass juices & so far, I’ve been addicted to Lovely Day, Heavenly & the stunning organic Lavender Lemonade. I need an Erewhon in my kitchen 😩 I’m so stoked about WeHo & Glendale coming soon since my gym and daughter’s school is in each area.

text.text:
Erewhon in Studio City deserves five stars. It is less slammed than Beverly Hills, yet the people watching is just as good. I even spotted Steven Tyler at the tonic bar testing a new drink, which tells you everything about the casual glamour here. The store has a smaller footprint than some locations, but the layout is smart and the selection feels complete. The hot bar is excellent with fresh options that change often, and the tonic bar is a standout for quick, feel good drinks. Staff move with purpose and actually help you find things, which makes short errands painless.

Prices are the only caveat. Some items feel fairly normal while others are eyebrow raising. Exhibit A is the thirty dollar bag of spherical cocktail ice. It is fun for home bartending, but still a splurge. On the flip side, many of the premium products really are a cut above, so you do get quality along with the sticker shock. For everyday grocery runs I point people to Trader Joe’s for cost effective organics and staples. For specialty items, a quick bite, or just soaking up the fancy Studio City milieu, this is the spot.

Location helps too. Right on Ventura at the Shops at Sportsmen’s Lodge, it draws a mix of locals, fitness crowd, and industry folks without feeling chaotic. You can pop in for a warm lunch from the hot bar, grab a smoothie, and pick up a few extras you will not find anywhere else in the Valley. High quality selection, sharp service, and prime people watching make this Erewhon an easy five stars.

text.text:
As someone who’s originally from Sarasota, FL, walking into this Lucky’s Market brought back all the feels. We had a Lucky’s back home before Kroger sadly shut them down, so getting to be in a Lucky’s Market again after moving to Colorado felt like coming home.

I stocked up on all the classic Lucky’s Market items I used to love and even mailed a big box to my mom and dad for Mother’s/Father’s Day—they were so excited and couldn’t believe it! It’s more than just a grocery store; it’s a nostalgic experience filled with great quality, local goods, and that unique vibe only Lucky’s has.

I’m so happy the original locations like this one are still around. It made my day, and I’ll be back regularly now that I’ve found it again!

text.text:
Lucky's Market supported our nonprofit in a big way this week. We were trying to find in-kind donations on short notice for an artist's brunch with Open Studios, for the Plein Air Arts Fest, and I was weary from making many phone calls. When I called Lucky's, all Saul asked was what we needed. Without a second thought, they were able to give us a bunch of juice that helped keep our artist's hydrated this morning!

It means so much that you are supporting nonprofits and the arts. THANK YOU LUCKY'S!!!

And to anyone reading this, this is yet another reason to support local businesses. The big box stores made us jump through hoops, just to say that there were no donations available for the quarter.

text.text: Unloading: Write the unloading number starting with DEL#T on the cargo list. Don't be late! After entering, drop the cabinet as required, and then drive the front of the car to the opposite side of Gate 448. There is no requirement to adjust the axle, but 90% of the cars in the yard have adjusted their axles. When you enter the office, you will see a device on the wall (see the photo). Write the phone number on the cargo list first, then put it in the bucket with a blue lid, put it into the device on the wall with the arrow pointing upwards, tighten the lock on the small door, and press the green button on the wall. The bucket on your cargo list will fly to the office. If there is no bucket on the table, you can call the phone on the wall, and he will send the bucket to you. Then you can choose to go back to the car and wait or go home. Generally, it takes 4 hours!

text.text:
I love Whole Foods. When I travel, I try to make it a priority stop; between the hot bar and the healthy options I can grab, it just make sense. The hot bar here, at 2 PM, had a couple of chickens and a salad bar but nothing else.

I was heading into the desert, so I grabbed several dozen liters of water. Parking here is a challenge (it's downtown, so no surprise there), and I was fortunate enough to park on the street right in front of the entrance. What WAS a surprise was the carts' automatic locking system that lets the cart no more than 20' from the store lol. I could have thrown a rock (not very hard) and hit my car from the front door, yet i still had to run back and forth to a cart that refused to go 20' outside the stoor. I guess they're only for in-store use.

I'll still stop at whole Foods in other places out of habit, but I'll avoid this one.

text.text: I go here often as the location is convenient and I'd love to give a great review but I just can't. It's very sad that the customer service is sub par and that it seems very much about status than the love of service and people.  That being said the cooks and back of the house crew do a great job of preparing delicious and healthy foods that are usually well presented and tasty.  The pizza guy is an Ace in the company's' arsenal of workers, always there and pizza is always outstanding. The customer service counter left me feeling like I should not bother getting up in the morning and the check out crew was even worse, I felt very much a lack of respect or regard at least three times through the check out and was treated as if I was not worth even listening to.  I have spent more than I should of in this store with supplements and healthy food trying to get my health back on track and that I will say I am grateful for as the whole foods have helped me recover physically.  I will say that whomever is training the customer service crew and management is lacking in love and compassion as I see this store is missing out on this extremely important key ingredient.  I felt a bit like I was at a judgmental church. They seem to have plenty of vegan/vegetarian options in the buffet, bakery, and self-serve food area.. but the gluten-free options are pretty much non-existent, especially in the bakery.. except a couple of exorbitantly overpriced items in a freezer next to the breads.  Anything I have tried from that freezer was not very palatable at all .. not worth the prices.  I really wish they had more gluten-free options; that would make trips to eat A meal there a lot more enjoyable for the MASS amount of people that are gluten-free!  Get on-board with that Whole Foods!  The grocery store itself is usually well-stocked.  We like to get meals sometimes at the Bird Call fast food joint in the store.  The egg prices have out-beat the other supermarkets by a lot, until recently when prices just started going down at other locations. They have a large eat-in area both inside, patio, and outside seating.. with utensils and water/ice machine available.  Overall we enjoy coming here!

text.text:
Whole Foods Market is a high-end grocery experience, offering a dazzling array of organic produce, artisanal cheeses, and specialty items that are hard to find elsewhere. The quality is undeniable, and for a specific recipe or a special occasion, it’s my go-to destination. The prepared foods and hot bar are consistently fresh and delicious, providing a great, albeit pricey, lunch option.
However, the premium experience comes with a premium price tag. It's easy to see why it earned the "Whole Paycheck" nickname; a simple shopping trip for essentials can quickly become a significant expense. My main sensory complaint is the fish department. While the selection is excellent, the overwhelming smell of fish often permeates a large section of the store near the entrance. It can be quite potent and detracts from the otherwise pleasant shopping atmosphere.
On the other hand, the single greatest convenience is the Amazon return counter. The process is brilliantly seamless. You simply show a QR code on your phone—no box, no label, no fuss. I can be in and out in under a minute. This feature alone often gets me in the door, even if I only plan on grabbing a few items.
In summary, Whole Foods offers top-tier quality and an unbeatable Amazon return service, but be prepared for the high prices and a sometimes fishy welcome.

text.text:
One Star – Horrible Customer Service and No Accountability

I had a shocking and extremely disappointing experience at Whole Foods Henderson today. While eating from the salad bar, I bit into a literal rock. When I brought this to the attention of the store manager, Billy, he showed zero concern, gave no apology, and offered no assistance whatsoever.

There was no proper documentation, no incident report, no accountability. Billy brushed it off entirely, making it clear he didn’t care about the safety or well-being of customers. When I asked about follow-up or how this would be addressed, I was told that Whole Foods doesn’t handle complaints directly — they push everything off to a third-party service, with no in-house resolution process. In other words, if something dangerous happens to you in their store, they take no responsibility.

This kind of careless attitude from a supposed premium grocery store is unacceptable. Accidents can happen, but the complete lack of customer care or concern for health and safety is inexcusable. Avoid the salad bar, and don’t expect Whole Foods to stand behind anything they serve.

text.text:
Overall, Whole Foods is a fantastic resource for specific dietary needs, but consistently disappoints when it comes to fresh produce.

The vegan, dairy-free, and gluten-free selection here is truly exceptional—it's easily the strongest aspect of the store. Finding specialty ingredients and substitutes is never a chore, and the variety offered makes it a reliable destination for shoppers with restrictions. Similarly, the frozen food section is excellent. The selection of frozen meals, desserts, and unique frozen ingredients is top-tier, making it easy to stock up on convenient, high-quality items. The pre-packaged snack selection is also quite good, providing plenty of healthy and indulgent options.

However, the experience with the fresh produce is consistently frustrating. Time and time again, I find that fresh vegetables and fruits do not last. It seems the turnover rate in this section is far too slow, as roughly 50-75% of what I purchase goes bad within just a couple of days of getting it home. This lack of freshness is disappointing and has forced me to completely rely on other grocery stores for all my fresh produce needs.

.

I like this store a lot. Ok, it is Whole Foods, so it is a little expensive and even pretentious. Does every employ need a tattoo. I'm just saying. But quality and selection stand out here.

The veggies and fruits are generally great. Mushrooms can be hit or miss. Ask if you don't see what you want, the employees are generally very helpful.

Meats and Seafood, terrific. They know the difference between wet and dry scallops (which qualifies me as pretentious doesn't it). Generally they will trim meat to your liking. Poultry is very satisfactory. I could spend the whole day looking in the refrigerated cases across from the meat counter and its hard not to buy a hundred dollars of snacks and meats and goodies.

Dairy is very complete. and the deli counter is usually well stocked. The food here (to buy to eat while there or to take home) top quality.They have a sandwich shop there that makes very nice items and you can take them to the brew pub area to eat..

I love it. Go there. Seriously it is nicer than several of the larger stores in the LA are.

Buy the Black and White cookie at the check out.

Parking is an adventure.

This is honestly one of the best Whole Foods I’ve been to. The Pasadena location is massive, open, and full of light — it just feels good to walk around in. There’s a relaxed vibe here too, way less uptight than some other stores I’ve visited.

The buffet and hot food section is seriously impressive. Loads of options — from sushi and vegan dishes to fresh fruit and hearty comfort food. It’s the kind of place where you could easily grab lunch or dinner and actually be excited about it.

They’ve also got a great range of everything else — organic produce, pantry staples, frozen meals, supplements, snacks from all over. It’s well laid out and easy to navigate, even when it’s busy.

Staff were friendly, the store was spotless, and I genuinely enjoyed wandering the aisles. Whether you’re shopping for the week or just grabbing a bite, Whole Foods Pasadena is worth the visit.

text.text:
I’m gonna share my worst service experience from this morning(15/Apr/2025). So, I’m a traveler from Asia and used to live in the U.S., but it’s been a while since I’ve been back, so I’m not really up to speed with the recent customs here. If I mess up in what I’m about to say, I apologize in advance.

I found a coffee stand for takeout in a store, and I wanted some coffee for breakfast. There was a big guy with a beard working there, but he didn’t seem to care that I was standing at the register. I tried to get his attention, but he didn’t respond, so I called out again and he told me to wait. After that, I ordered a cappuccino, and when he asked about the milk, I requested soy milk. He said they only had oat milk besides regular milk, so I went with regular milk.
When it came time to pay, I had the option to tip, but since it was a self-service cafe and the guy’s attitude wasn’t great, I chose not to leave a tip. He asked if I wanted a receipt, and I said yes. He took his time checking the receipt before handing it to me. I thought it was weird that he was staring at it so closely, but I figured he just wanted to see if I tipped or not.
Then he started making my cappuccino and pulled the espresso shot. At one point, I noticed the espresso was spilling out of the cup and not actually going in. He eventually fixed the cup and poured the espresso in, but it looked like there was definitely less than there should have been. He added the milk, but then he did something else that I’ve never seen before. He added hot water to the cup for the milk foam and steamed it. I was shocked that he would add hot water to make the foam because I thought that would just water down the coffee. But he didn’t seem to care and poured that watery foam into my drink.
When he handed me the cappuccino, he placed it way at the far end of the counter, far from where I was standing. I felt like I was being totally messed with. I took a sip, and found it was exactly what I expected—a weak cappuccino that didn’t taste like coffee at all. I ended up tossing it when I got back to my hotel, even though I had paid for it.

I wanted to have a nice morning with breakfast from Whole Foods, but thanks to him, my mood was ruined. Do you really have to tip at a self-service cafe? Is that the only way to avoid getting bad coffee? This was honestly the worst experience I’ve ever had. I can’t help but wonder if he treated me poorly because I’m Asian. If that’s the case, that’s just awful.

On the bright side, the cashier at the grocery store before getting coffee was super nice, and the stock clerk I met yesterday was really friendly too.

text.text:
This is a review specifically for the Amazon Prime department of this store. Be sure to ALWAYS get a receipt when making returns to Amazon here!!!!

I have reason to believe an item I returned, was not sent to Amazon themselves but instead was kept by someone working the returns desk that day. Prompting a huge mess on MY end.

I received an order from Amazon. I can acknowledge this purchase was risky—as is most things on Amazon. I took the gamble, because returns are smooth and easy. I have also had great luck and experiences ordering the same thing from Amazon before. It was trading cards. Amazon’s return policy is great and I had no issues with previous orders. Until someone decides to steal the item you’re returning to this Whole Foods—and it’s something in high demand, looking like a score on the surface.

I filed a formal complaint that included pictures, with Amazon about the order—it came completely opened, all packs inside sliced, missing 6 packs, the whole nine yards. Bummer. I returned the item because clearly I don’t want to keep something I was scammed of. Presented my QR code and was told I was good to go—as always. Never had an issue. But after 10 days Amazon had no record of it being returned. I don’t know if this specific thing is store dependent or store wide—I was told (by Amazon) that there is a log of everything scanned, so even though I was missing my return receipt the store MUST have it in the system still.

No, this store said they don’t keep a log of anything they scan for Amazon returns. My return was nowhere to be found, and there was no way of verifying with this store specifically that the item was scanned to be sent to Amazon. But the item probably was not scanned at all to begin with. So this store isn’t trustworthy with Amazon returns, once you drop it off there’s nothing that can be done after you drop it off, they do/don’t scan it and you don’t have the receipt anymore.

But ok, it's just my impression, I want the best for this place and have been loyal to Whole Foods in every state I lived in before. But in all honesty, it seems Amazon did nothing to improve the quality of what used to be here. They did raise prices swiftly, however. Peace, no disrespect is intended, it's still better than other places; but for the price and the vibe, I'm in Erewhon more and more now. Whole Foods is still worth it for many people, and that's all to the good!

I enjoy shopping at Whole Foods! The store is clean, well-organized, and has a welcoming atmosphere. The produce section is especially impressive—everything is fresh, vibrant, and neatly displayed. I appreciate the wide selection of organic and specialty items, as well as the clearly labeled dietary options like gluten-free, vegan, and keto.

The staff are friendly and helpful, often going out of their way to answer questions or help you find what you need. I also love their hot bar and prepared foods section—perfect for a quick, healthy meal on the go.

Whole Foods might be a bit pricier than some other stores, but the quality and overall shopping experience make it worth it. Highly recommended if you’re looking for fresh, healthy, and responsibly sourced products!

A five-star experience, every time.

Whole Foods Woodland Hills is one of those rare grocery stores that’s worth going out of your way for. The place is absolutely massive, which means the selection is incredible—whether you’re hunting for specialty cheeses, fresh seafood, plant-based options, or that obscure pantry item you usually have to order online. Everything is thoughtfully laid out, so finding what you need is quick and stress-free, even on a busy day. The store has a great flow, and it never feels cramped despite the huge crowds it can draw.

Service here is consistently on point. Staff are friendly, knowledgeable, and genuinely willing to help, whether it’s guiding you to the right aisle or offering a tip on a new product. The prepared foods section is a standout, with plenty of fresh and tasty options for an easy meal. Produce is fresh and well-stocked, the bakery smells like it could tempt anyone into picking up something sweet, and the coffee bar makes a perfect stop before or after shopping.

Between the size, the organization, and the service, this isn’t just a grocery stop—it’s an experience. Definitely one of the top Whole Foods locations in the region and absolutely worth the drive, even if it means braving rush hour traffic.

text.text:
I'm constantly on the move, always looking for the perfect balance between work, nutrition, and atmosphere. Let me tell you, Whole Foods? It nails it every single time.

Now, here's the deal. Every Whole Foods has its vibe, and this location is a notch above the rest. It's not just a store, but a destination. It has a large, open dining area that is absolutely perfect for digging into a scrumptious lunch while hammering out some work. Talk about multitasking!

But let's get to the food because, oh boy, it's delightful. Fresh prepared food bars and a pizza station that whips up a mean bbq chicken pizza. The kicker? You can pair it with a craft beer, right from the pizza counter. Yes, you heard me. Craft. Beer.

Have a sweet tooth? You won't be disappointed. The bakery churns out some amazing treats. I can't resist snagging a cookie, or let's be real, two, from the bulk cookie bar. You can't say no to cookies, right?

When it comes to variety, the meat counter is impressive. Fresh smoked meats, BBQ meats, you name it, they've got it. The seafood counter doesn't disappoint either. I mean, this is the full package.

And hey, in this digital age, Whole Foods' Amazon return policy is a game-changer. No box needed for your returns; they just scan the QR code and pack it into a box for you. Simple, smooth, and hassle-free.

Bottom line? Fantastic store, excellent staff, fresh food, and a great location. Whole Foods Market in Huntington Beach is an experience you don't want to miss. Remember, eat better, work better, live better.

text.text:
Whole Foods is best understood not as a market, but as an evolving text — a palimpsest of contemporary desire inscribed in edible form. Its aisles are semiotic landscapes where packaging, provenance, and price operate as much as signifiers as the food itself. The avocado here is no longer merely fruit, but a cultural emblem; the wine selection reads less as inventory and more as a curated bibliography of terroir.

Stepping inside, one finds a peculiar intersection of commerce and idealism. The produce, arranged in an almost painterly chromatic order, suggests Cézanne reimagined through corporate logistics. The bakery, fragrant with its artisanal loaves, borders on performance art — each boule and baguette a sculptural critique of industrialized bread. Even the prepared food bar feels like an ethnography of late-capitalist appetites, where veganism, paleo fervor, and indulgent nostalgia coexist without irony.

The irony, of course, is that Whole Foods stages itself as both antidote to mass consumerism and its apotheosis. Its genius lies in making necessity feel like discernment, transforming groceries into identity, turning the banal into the aspirational. To shop here is to participate in a ritual of aestheticized consumption — a reminder that in our era, even lettuce is imbued with ideology.

This Whole Foods is such a pleasure to shop at now! I’ve lived in Venice for over 8 years, and I’ve never seen the store looking this good.
I always used to avoid this location due to the issues with homelessness and  messiness around the area, but it’s been completely cleaned up.
The store itself has undergone a fantastic revamp…everything is very clean, the shelves are always well-stocked, and they frequently feature great promotions and eye-catching displays that make me discover interesting new products. I’m very impressed with how recent changes in this store.

The staff are consistently friendly, helpful, and professional. I used to do more  online pick-up in the past, now I prefer  shop in person more often and see their new range of products

I also appreciate the self-checkout option and the availability of enough registers during peak times, which keeps wait times reasonable.

This store also has Amazon Return/Pick Up counter which comes in really helpful

Overall, my experience here has been excellent in this store.

Update: today I saw the fall vibes in store, the pumpkin display at entrance was so warm and fall welcoming

The automated return machine literally closed itself as I was doing my returns, we notified the people working there that we need more bags and the man did nothing. This review is really for Amanda in the bakery department. I went this past week 10/3/24 to purchase a cake for my daughter's birthday. I usually love getting Whole Foods cake because it's delicious but also affordable. First when I come to the counter she barely even greeted me and the other woman of color. When she finally gets to me, I make the order and ask for a simple design. I just need pink and blue in some form on this cake. Nothing overly fancy. She proceeds to tell me, they are no longer doing custom cakes. Literally just stopped the week before. Now I understand if the design was crazy, I'm talking like flowers or swirls on this cake in pink and blue. I then ask well can someone write Happy Birthday in pink and blue. She then tells me they only have pink no blue to write. (The cake wasn't to be picked up for 3 days, they could not find blue icing in 3 days...). Finally, I place the order for the Berry Chantilly cake and she proceeds to tell me they don't have blueberries. So what do you have? And why are you open?

I go to pick up the cake Saturday and the sweet decorator brings me the cake. I make a comment to make sure there was no way they could decorate it. The decorator says she's sorry but that day was her last day and that's why there are no custom cakes. I proceed to jokingly say "All I wanted was flowers" and she looks at me apologetically and says, that was simple and could have been done and should have been requested. So my instinct was right Miss Amanda with the bad attitude not only has terrible customer service but didn't even want to try to hear me out about a simple design and just ask.

Whole Foods, do better or do away with the bakery department. Last year, the Whole Foods in Playa Vista gave me the worst decorated cake I've ever seen and this year you have workers who don't at least try to care about customer satisfaction. To the absolutely adorable cake decorator who was on her last day, I hope nothing but good comes your way. To Miss Amanda, your right where you belong. I mean personally you should not be in customer service but at least your at the bakery and not unleashed on the rest of the world.

text.text:
A Disappointing Pattern Behind an Otherwise Great Store

This store has consistently offered a great selection and clean layout, which is why my wife and I have been regular customers. However, we’ve now experienced a troubling pattern at checkout that’s hard to ignore.

On two separate occasions, we were met with complete silence from the cashier—no greeting, no inquiry about bags or receipts, no acknowledgment at all. What made it especially jarring was watching the same cashier warmly engage with the customers ahead of and behind us, offering smiles and friendly conversation. The contrast was stark and unmistakable.

Initially, I chalked it up to coincidence or a bad day. But after the second time, it felt less like an oversight and more like intentional disregard. It’s disheartening to feel singled out in a space that should be welcoming to all.

We’ll still shop here for essentials, but we’ve scaled back our purchases and are exploring other options. Respectful service should be consistent—not selective.

text.text:
I have been shopping Whole Foods, Thousand Oaks since it was in Trader Joes location years (and years) ago.

My rant is about the weakening values of a once greater store brought on by the Amazon buyout.

First off, Bezos is too cheap to take good care of the employees.. you can see since Amazon bought it they dont seem as  happy as before. I guess he doesn't realize happy employees set an upbeat tone to the store and the experience which is really important.

Also, its apparent that the model coming in, was "lets cut costs and make more profit". Now there's more "grab and go" items,  closing the burrito bar, pizza doesn't taste as good as before, a non organic juicebar, most ALL of the prepared foods now have way more added crappy ingredients (take a look for yourself)  spent $$$ on too bright lighting to showcase produce of lesser quality, showcasing the  big brands that have been mostly bought out, much less choice available  and every time I turn around , there's another product disappeared ....but then I'll see Cheerios.

I still shop here for certain stuff but miss Lassens who had integrity.  Hoping not to see chocolate covered insects too soon!!

text.text:
I recently tried the Tres Leches cake at Whole Foods market Bakery and while the presentation was absolutely stunning, I left disappointed. The cake itself was good, with a light and fluffy texture that hinted at its potential. However, my excitement quickly turned to dismay as I realized that whoever made it forgot a crucial ingredient—the tres leches! This traditional cake is supposed to be soaked in three types of milk, which not only enhances its flavor but also defines its identity. Without it, the cake lacked the signature moistness and richness that makes Tres Leches so delightful.

Unfortunately, this oversight means I won't be returning to Whole foods market Bakery. While the presentation showed promise, a dessert as iconic as Tres Leches needs to deliver on taste, and this one fell short.
