text.text:
⭐ 1 Star — 8 Years of Dedication Thrown Away Like Nothing
I gave Central Market 8 years of my life — showing up, working hard, and staying loyal even through some of the toughest times. I showed up after a tornado tore through the store. I worked through COVID as a part-time employee, doing whatever was needed, even when others wouldn’t. I stayed committed to both the company and the customers.

After all that, they fired me on my day off, not because of any wrongdoing on my part, but because a lead cursed me out by name, and somehow I ended up being the one let go. That’s how they treat loyal, long-term employees.

Despite always being told they “promote from within,” I watched them repeatedly give promotions to total strangers with little to no qualifications — all because someone put in a good word. Meanwhile, I was passed over again and again, no matter how hard I worked or how much I contributed.

The Grocery Manager, Lilly Lin, was one of the worst parts of the experience. She cursed in front of employees, told me to “tackle any customer that tries to steal candles” — and she made it clear she was serious. She also repeatedly referred to my kids as “gremlins,” which was incredibly disrespectful and unprofessional. No manager should ever talk to employees or their families like that.

The company’s treatment of employees of color is also deeply unfair. There’s a noticeable difference in how situations are handled, who gets opportunities, and who doesn’t. Customers at this store can be extremely rude and entitled — I’ve had customers yell at me, run up on me, and point their fingers in my face. And management’s response? Nothing. No support, no protection.

When customers gave compliments, it was brushed off as “that’s just your job,” with no real recognition. But when a conflict happens, they’ll turn their backs on you in an instant.

To be fired after 8 years of dedication, after everything I’ve done for this company, is outrageous. Central Market presents itself as a company that values its people — but behind the scenes, the way they treat their employees, especially long-term ones, tells a very different story.

text.text:
Central Market is undoubtedly one of the premier grocery stores you can visit, offering top-notch food quality. In my opinion, it surpasses Whole Foods in many aspects. The variety of products available is impressive, encompassing everything from coffee to liquor and vegetables to meat. Whether you’re looking for gourmet ingredients, specialty items, or everyday essentials, Central Market has it all.

One of the standout features of Central Market is its dedication to providing fresh, high-quality produce and products. The meat and seafood sections are particularly notable for their extensive selection and freshness. Additionally, the bakery and prepared foods sections offer an array of delicious options that cater to a wide range of tastes and dietary preferences.

Despite these strengths, there is one area where Central Market falls short: their kiosk payment system does not support contactless payment methods. This is surprising, given the store's otherwise modern and customer-friendly approach. In today’s tech-savvy world, contactless payments are not just a convenience but a necessity for many shoppers. The absence of this option can be an inconvenience, especially for those who prefer to use digital wallets or contactless cards for quicker, safer transactions.

Given Central Market’s commitment to providing a superior shopping experience, I believe they should invest in updating their point-of-sale (POS) systems to include contactless payment options. This upgrade would not only enhance the shopping experience but also align with the expectations of today’s consumers, ensuring that Central Market remains at the forefront of grocery retail excellence.

Absolutely love everything about Central Market! Visiting during weekend lunchtime always feels like an adventure—there’s so much to explore. The food is consistently fresh, the staff is friendly, and the store is always clean and well-maintained. The cafeteria seating area could benefit from a bit more attention during peak hours, but with the constant flow of guests, it’s understandable and still well-managed overall.

From the expansive salad bar and comforting soup options to the cozy coffee shop, sushi bar, vibrant floral selections, and a wide variety of freshly cooked meals—there’s something for everyone. Our favorite, though, is the incredible sandwich bar, offering delicious choices for all ages.

The overall atmosphere is warm and inviting. I just wish there were more locations nearby! The only downside we’ve experienced is the sandwich line on weekends—it can get quite long, sometimes taking up to 30 minutes despite having plenty of staff. Hopefully, they’ll find a way to improve the flow, but even with the wait, it’s well worth it.

I had heard glowing reviews about Central Market and was genuinely excited to experience it for myself. On my day off today at 8AM I drove 20 miles with high hopes, anticipating a standout grocery experience that matched its upscale reputation.

To be fair, the food quality and selection were impressive. The produce was fresh, and the variety throughout the store—from specialty items to bakery offerings—was clearly curated with care. However, the customer service fell disappointingly short.
From the moment I entered, not a single associate greeted me or offered a smile. When I asked questions in the produce section, the staff seemed disinterested and unfriendly. At the bakery, I stood waiting while the associate behind the counter failed to acknowledge me until I made it unavoidably clear I needed help. Checkout was no better—no greeting, no thank you, just a silent scan of my items.

For a store with premium pricing and a reputation for excellence, I expected a level of hospitality that matched the product quality. Unfortunately, the lack of warmth and attentiveness from the staff made the experience feel transactional and cold. I left wondering what all the hype was about. I will not be going back.

On 4/5/25 Ellie, the Manager, quietly came up behind me while I was shopping and yelled at me that they were closed.  This really startled and freaked me out and she just stood there glaring at me and wouldn’t leave.  I had no other option but to go past her, as I was blocked off from any other exit, which I was not looking forward to.  She was hostile and angry for what reason I don’t know.   Then I began to walk towards her, as it was my only option, and she corrected herself and said we close in 5 minutes.   I continued walking towards the check out and she let two other people in the store as I was checking out.   I was shocked at this due to her anger towards me and that the store was “closed”.  I suddenly remembered my previous experience shopping there and that she was also very rude that day as well, although I don’t remember the exact reason for her previous rudeness, I definitely remembered her being very rude and unprofessional.
The store itself is great, no complaints but the Manager, Ellie…well let’s just say I am shocked she is a manager and even employed there.  She definitely has a negative impact on this business.  I hope the owners read this and speak with this woman who needs some help with people skills and customer service.

text.text: I’ve been an Erma’s customer for more than 15 years and have been so impressed with the staff and management’s knowledge, compassion and professionalism that I thought it was far past time to say so publicly. Everyone from Ellie (the manager for 16 of those years), Taryn, Ruben and all the rest of them have never once failed to  guide me productively and patiently even when I would have found fault with my approach based on being anxious about an issue or illness or  just being less than joy filled though hopefully that is perceived as rare! That is the truest testament I could give to the people who make this business shine and who have earned profound respect and admiration from me and so many of the rest of us. I know I am not alone in being deeply grateful for not only the huge selection of approaching “pharm grade” supplements at fair prices but the unending support this group of people who have served their community for so long and so well that I can speak to people in adjacent communities for miles around and have them share my love of the people who make this business the gem that it is for all of us!   (Sorry for the mushy parts Ellie/Taryn/Ruben…but it had to be said! We adore you!).

text.text: We were so excited to go buy up some stuff as we were heading out of St Louis.   The experience we met at this store was anything but that. Six years we've had to go places with a special needs child. And many times he'd be loud or whiny or that of a typical one year old or less. He is gdd along with multiple others conditions. People have come up and tried to help, or ask questions but never made fun of or insulted us as caregivers. Of course, I never even thought a store employee, owner would do this. For one, they'd lose business. At least ours anyhow. We had a cart full of things mostly not available at a regular grocery store.  Id guess at over two hundred at least . We also had another typical child with us . As we are in the checkout, one person in front of us , the employee yells " can you get control of him, he's acting like a baby" .  My response, " I wish we could, he's disabled" " sorry" . She responds again with crying actions and mocking faces telling us again how much of a baby he's being.  The child with us (7 year old sister) says very upset " he has autism" . My daughter picks him up and goes to car , telling me to do what I want with my stuff. She's already crying and as any mom would be , very upset her special needs son was being discriminated against in such a shocking way. I wait for the person in front of me to finish up, debating back and forth with getting the stuff we were excited to find, or walking out. I opted for the latter. I told the boys sister to put back her sweet find and she did. I very politely pushed my cart over out of the way of the other customer coming up behind me.  As I'm walking past the employee, she loudly asked do I not want the stuff. I say , yes , I did.  But not now after what you said to a disabled child. She then, and this one got me, asks me to put the items back. They were in the cart. And they were going to be bought. And we were next in line before she rudely verbally assaulted a special needs child. I don't think she'd if really wanted me staying in there any longer.   So, to future customers, buyer beware. You might get what you want with an extra dose of discrimination.

text.text:
⭐⭐⭐ — Great Selection, But Room for Improvement

Jay International Food is one of my go-to spots for variety — you can find ingredients and products here that are hard to track down anywhere else in St. Louis. The international selection is truly impressive, and it’s the main reason I keep coming back.

That said, the store could use a little TLC. While I’ve noticed improvements over time, it would be even better with a deeper, more consistent clean. The staff gets the job done, but a bit more warmth and friendliness would go a long way toward making the shopping experience as inviting as the selection itself.

Bottom line: I’ll keep shopping here because the variety is unbeatable, but I’m hoping to see the atmosphere match the amazing products on the shelves.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Sevenanda Natural Foods Market — Atlanta, GA

I’ve been coming to Sevenanda for nearly 10 years, and it has always been a special place — from the incredible selection of holistic, vegan, and health products to the peaceful energy that fills the store.

But today was different. Today was extraordinary.

I had the pleasure of being helped by a woman named Shaina (I hope I’m spelling that right) — and she completely transformed my day. What started as a simple visit turned into one of the most genuine, uplifting exchanges I’ve had in a long time. She took her time to answer my questions, offered thoughtful suggestions, and made me feel truly seen and appreciated. Her professionalism, warmth, and grace are exactly what customer service should be. Whoever made her manager — kudos to you. She embodies what this company stands for.

Yes, the prices reflect the quality — and not everyone can always afford everything here — but when you receive that kind of service alongside that level of product excellence, it’s worth every penny.

If you want to treat yourself to something wholesome, intentional, and filled with good energy — do yourself a favor and shop at Sevenanda

text.text:
I visited Virginia Health Food Store today to purchase ingredients for elderberry syrup for my daughter, who was diagnosed with COVID-19 earlier this week and is still symptomatic. Out of caution, both my daughter and I wore medical-grade masks. When we arrived, I immediately informed the associate assisting me that my daughter was positive and still contagious, so she could decide whether to wear a mask or keep her distance. She was respectful, went to the back to get a mask, and came back to help me find the items I needed.

I was nearly finished shopping—about 7 to 10 minutes into my visit—when a manager named Celeste approached and told me I needed to leave the store due to concerns from other customers. I explained that I was only there to quickly get a few essential ingredients to care for my sick child, but she insisted I leave immediately. No curbside option was offered, no suggestion of an alternative—just a flat denial of service.

I had to call my mother and ask her to drive from Saraland to the store to finish the shopping. I waited outside for about 15 minutes, and even then, no one offered any form of assistance or accommodation. What made this situation worse is that the store was fairly busy with 10–15 other people inside—none of whom were wearing masks. There’s no guarantee that anyone else wasn’t asymptomatic or contagious, but because I was honest, proactive, and masked, I was singled out and dismissed.

When my mother came in to finish the purchase, she was rushed, and we later discovered that not all the ingredients I needed were included. This forced me to return not once, but two more times just to get everything. Despite the inconvenience and repeated trips, no one offered any form of compensation, apology, or even a discount for my time and trouble. The only person who showed genuine understanding and kindness was Alex, who assisted me during my third visit. After I told him this was my third trip back, he kindly gave me some extra elderberries at no charge, which I truly appreciated.

This experience left me feeling disrespected, dismissed, and discriminated against. I took every precaution I could. I was honest, masked, and simply trying to care for my sick child. Yet instead of being met with understanding or support, I was treated like an inconvenience.

Virginia Health Food Store is one of the few places in Mobile that offers raw, unprocessed herbs, so it’s deeply disappointing to be treated this way. I hope the store takes this as an opportunity to improve how they handle sensitive situations like this—with empathy, consistency, and basic human decency.

The staff here can be very hit or miss. Some are absolutely wonderful, warm, attentive, and professional, while others seem to lack even basic customer service skills. Management really needs to address the behavior of certain employees who come across as rude and unprofessional.

I understand they deal with difficult or entitled customers at times, but when a regular customer like myself comes in daily, greets them, and smiles, that same courtesy should be reciprocated. When I’m checking out and the cashier barely makes eye contact, that’s a problem. When another employee starts joking around and “bossing” a coworker in front of me, it’s shockingly unprofessional. I didn’t even realize they were joking until they started laughing, when I lightheartedly chimed in, they both just stared at me awkwardly. No, that’s not on me; it’s inappropriate to act that way in front of customers. A little decorum goes a long way.

That said, the coffee bar team is exceptional, world-class, friendly, and a true pleasure to interact with every time.

text.text: The West Plano Whole Foods used to be a 5-Star, but the ongoing renovations have decimated what was once a spacious, organized, and well-stocked store. Over recent weeks, they have demolished the produce, cheese, seafood, wine, and other departments to make way for what appears to be a banal Amazon fulfillment center. What we are left with is a much more claustrophobic space where all of the above listed departments are crammed into the space that used to hold the fine wines and beers. They have also reshuffled other parts of the store, which has resulted in narrower and darker aisles and less merchandise from which to choose. The Amazonification of Whole Foods appears to have led to the demise of the location that we have called home for 20 years.

Always Worth the Trip!

This Whole Foods in The Woodlands is one of my go-to grocery stops. Yes, parking can be a bit tight and it’s often busy, but it’s always worth the effort. The produce is excellent—fresh greens and potatoes are staples for me—and the bakery is top-notch. I regularly pick up their fresh sourdough bread, which is delicious and surprisingly affordable.

The store is clean, well-organized, and I really appreciate the self-checkout stations. With my Prime membership, I get additional discounts, and the checkout process is smooth and quick. When I’m in a hurry, I grab something from the hot food bar or salad bar—both offer healthy and tasty options.

Overall, a great shopping experience every time. Highly recommend!

The selection of organic produce is always fresh and abundant, and their unique offerings—like specialty cheeses, fresh seafood, and a wide variety of vegan options—set them apart from other stores.

Overall, Whole Foods in The Woodlands delivers exceptional quality, variety, and service. It’s worth every penny and makes healthy living easy and enjoyable. Five stars!

text.text: I know they probably don’t want you to do this but last time I went there I found they had a self serve sample of apple cider. I was in the store for maybe an hour, not shopping, but refilling and resampling and replenishing my one ounce sample cup. Oscar Wilde says that “the only way to get rid of temptation is to yield to it,” I never understood this quote until that day. The only thing that would make longing in my stomach was another one ounce sample and another and another. It was not until I had consumed the entire container of the sweet ambrosia that I felt I must return back to my monotonous existence beyond the sample section of Whole Foods. I am not proud of my actions but that is my past and I cannot change it. I must wait and hope that when I return on my lunch break there will be another self serve sample station.

text.text:
Whole Foods Market has long positioned itself as the go-to grocery store for health-conscious consumers seeking organic, sustainably sourced, and high-quality food products. Founded in 1980 and acquired by Amazon in 2017, the chain has expanded its reach while maintaining its core values of clean eating and environmental responsibility.
One of Whole Foods' standout features is its dedication to organic produce and natural products. Shoppers can expect a wide variety of fruits and vegetables, most of which are clearly labeled and certified organic. Meat and seafood selections are also held to high standards, with animal welfare ratings and sustainable fishing practices prominently displayed.
The store’s layout is clean, inviting, and aesthetically pleasing, with neatly arranged aisles, specialty sections like the hot food and salad bars, and a focus on local products. Whole Foods also carries a large inventory of gluten-free, vegan, and non-GMO items, which caters to a wide range of dietary needs and lifestyles.
However, price remains a common concern. Despite Amazon’s ownership and subsequent price cuts on some items, Whole Foods still tends to be more expensive than mainstream grocery stores. While you are often paying for better sourcing and higher quality, budget-conscious shoppers may find it difficult to make Whole Foods their primary grocery destination.
Customer service is generally excellent—employees are knowledgeable and helpful, and the checkout process is efficient, especially with Amazon Prime integration for additional savings.
In summary, Whole Foods Market delivers a premium shopping experience focused on wellness, sustainability, and quality. It’s a top choice for those who prioritize food transparency and are willing to pay a little more for it. While not ideal for every budget, it remains a favorite for many who value what it stands for: conscious consumption and better food choices

text.text: Whole Foods is an original Austin business dating back more than 40 years. I still remember the original Whole Foods, which was right across from the 7-Eleven on Lamar and ninth Street. Since then, it has become a grocery store behemoth and gets a bad rap for prices, but when you get you get what you pay for. All the produce and meat here is very fresh, and a lot of the meat is certified to be humanely raised. A lot of their seafood is MSC certified meaning it was sustainably harvested. Their fresh food bars are excellent, and their pizza is very good, and an excellent value. I wish they carried their vegan pizza more consistently, as one of my friends often goes there just for this. Their produce is excellent and comparable to the produce at Central market. Despite being an enormous chain now it’s still retains a lot of the Austin flavor. This is their flagship store, near their corporate offices. After moving from their original store, they were briefly a block to the north and what is now REI.

text.text:
I stopped by Whole Foods in San Antonio to return an Amazon item and decided to explore the store afterward. While many products were similar to what you'd find at a typical grocery store, there were definitely some standout features. I discovered a pizza bar and couldn’t resist grabbing a slice of supreme – fresh, hot, and satisfying.

In the bakery and pre-cooked foods section, I came across a cooler filled with unique items like scones and brown butter cookie dough. After a brief chat with a fellow shopper who raved about the cookie dough, I added it to my basket. The hot food bar also looked tempting, but I decided to save that for another day.

Their fresh produce was impressive. The Rainier cherries, in particular, were in season and too good to pass up. (If you’ve never tried them, imagine a cherry and a nectarine had a baby, sweet and flavorful!)

At checkout, the cashier was friendly, and I had my first encounter with a palm-reading payment device, an interesting tech upgrade, which I had never seen before, though I opted for the traditional method this time.

Overall, Whole Foods is a bit pricier, but the experience, product variety, and quality make it worth an occasional visit.

text.text:
Okay, so I've always loved Whole Foods. Their commitment to quality and healthy options is awesome, especially for those with dietary needs. My mom has a tough time with gluten, so she relies on real sourdough bread – it's way easier on her digestion. That's why I was kinda bummed about the 'sourdough' they have now.  When I checked the ingredients, I saw commercial yeast, which isn't something you usually find in authentic sourdough.
And real sourdough? The kind made with a natural starter and long fermentation? It's a game-changer for people like my mom. It's got awesome health benefits that regular bread just doesn't have.  A lot of folks in our community rely on Whole Foods for stuff like this, and I think we all trust them to be upfront about their products.
Look, I get that mistakes happen, maybe this was just an oversight. But it made me realize how important it is to have clear standards about what can be called 'sourdough.'  Having some guidelines would protect folks like my mom and make sure everyone's playing fair, right?
Always look for cultured wheat when trying to find real sourdough bread. If you want the benefits then I recommend looking for that specifically. Like the picture on the right.
Now I may be wrong as I am a human being.

I recently had the opportunity to try the new large vegan pizza at Whole Foods, and it was an absolute hit with my family. The fact that it was added to their menu just yesterday made it even more exciting!

The first thing that struck us was the generous size of the pizza. It was large enough to satisfy our whole family, and the presentation was excellent. The vegan toppings were colorful and inviting, promising a delightful experience.

As for the taste, we were blown away. The crust was perfectly baked, achieving that ideal balance between crispy and chewy. The vegan cheese had a creamy texture and a fantastic melt, making it difficult to believe it wasn't dairy-based. The assortment of fresh vegetables added a burst of flavors and textures that complemented the pizza perfectly.

text.text:
Some highlights from this review:

🔴 Parking difficulties. (Try parking in the garage.)
🟡 Friendly service but poor packing for your grocery-3 out of 5 times (Double check before loading)
🟢 Good selection of organic produce and products.
🟢 Wine section available.

Note: Smaller shopping cart may prefer due to tight space between aisles.

I have been a whole food shopper for many years since I was back in East coast. I do almost all my groceries at Whole Food because of its good quality of fresh organic produce and the large varieties of organic and NonGMO product selections. For example, even grass-fed beef or lamb meat and grass fed milk, vegan food options or vegan option skin care products. Whole Food in KC downtown may offer more trendy brands than the Overland Park one in some cases. Same as the prepared food section and bakery items are better than OP one. They also have a smoothies section and wine section to save you from making another stop from your shopping trip if you also want some wine for your dinner party or a refreshing smoothie while you are shopping. The tea, coffee and wine bar is at the corner of the store and nice to have a quick bite and some refreshing drink with friends and family.

Be aware:
The parking situation is not too great. The space in between cars are narrower and tighter in my opinion. The traffic from coming in and backing up for leaving can be very difficult, so be extra cautious for that. My recommendation is parking in the parking garage to avoid the waiting and stuck in between the coming and going traffic.

Another downside of the shopping experience is making sure your groceries were packed correctly because the cashiers are very friendly but almost every time when I’m there my groceries weren’t packed correctly or carefully enough and messed up my items. They may be too busy and not taking time to make sure things are packed carefully, especially when you bring your own bags. In that case, please take some time to double check when you transfer your grocery bags into your car. For this reason, I definitely prefer the service provided in Overland Park site. Another thing that may worth to be considered is using a smaller cart, if possible. For the space between the aisles can be very limited and crowded especially when other shoppers are also in the same aisle as you. Pick the smaller size one if you can manage your items.

Hopefully these information helps and ease your shopping experience there. Happy shopping at Whole Food KC Downtown!

text.text: My 4 year old wanted to have his birthday at Whole Foods, we live about two hours away from one. So,  it is a treat for him to go and get whatever he wants from the hot food bar and treats from the bakery.  That was the plan for his “party” real simple. I called two days ahead and ordered a cake for him, we were planning on eating it there at the store with our lunch. I mentioned to the cake artist ,Selena, about him wanting to celebrate his birthday at Whole Foods because I thought it was hilarious. I want to be clear, did not ask for ANYTHING because it is a grocery store it is not a place for birthdays.  We just planned to go in (our small family of 4) eat lunch, sing happy birthday quietly and open the few presents we brought with us and go home.  When we got there they had a beautiful cake ready for us and made my son feel SO special. Selena and her manager Taylor showered us with surprises and treated my son like a Birthday Prince! We were so blessed and shocked at the kindness of the employees. I never in a million years thought a birthday at Whole Foods would be so amazing. It just goes to show how good people can make all the difference! Thank you Whole Foods we will be back!!!

text.text:
Well, shucks, walkin’ into Whole Foods is like stumblin’ into a fancy-pants farm where every durn thing’s organic and prouder than a prize hog. The spread’s crazier than a Missouri mule—y’got yer fancy quinoa grains hollerin’ ‘bout bein’ ancient, purple taters sidlin’ up to kale greener than a John Deere. They got kombucha fizzier than a soda pop at a county fair, and eggs so free-range they prob’ly got their own zip code. Labels? Clearer than a creek after a spring rain, so you ain’t gonna grab no chemical-caked spud by mistake.

The folks shoppin’ here? Hoo boy, it’s like a parade of them yoga-lovin’ gals from the city, chuckin’ goji berries in their carts slicker than a swan on ice. Then there’s them beefy fellas, haulin’ grass-fed steaks like they’re fixin’ to wrestle a steer. But, Lordy, the prices’ll make ya choke on yer sweet tea—higher than a cornstalk in July. You’re payin’ to keep from keelin’ over all miserable and full o’ toxins. Yer wallet’ll squeal, but yer ticker’ll thank ya. Whole Foods: where ya trade greenbacks for green livin’!

This place (Destin Commons WF) has really declined in the last few months. Do not go there if you have any kind of accessability issues. Every time we go, the aisles are always filled because they are stocking. The old model of stocking the shelves before they open seems to have gone out the window. Now its hard to get around and heaven forbid you stop to read a box for a product your unfamilar with because that may block other people because they can't get around you because the rest of the aisle is blocked by things that need to be stocked.

Also, the past couple of times we have come home only to find out what we purchased was bad. This time it was organic red baby potatoes which was moldy and sprouting. But since it is across the MidBay Bridge for us to go into Destin, we just have to throw it out. The stockers are probably too busy trying to stock the stuff in the aisles during normal business hours, they don't have the time to check their other stock of food.

We’ve been shopping here weekly for the past two years since relocating to Alabama. Quality seems to be fading over the last several months. We purchase only organic fruits and vegetables and find ourselves disappointed often. In this picture is a bag of organic Brussel sprouts purchased 2 hours ago at Whole Foods. 75% of the bag is rotten.

Organic grapefruits are an item we purchase on a weekly basis. One week, the fruit is sweet and juicy. The next week, the organic grapefruits are dry, flavorless, and tough.

Today while shopping, I left several cartons of organic strawberries opened as a “hint” that maybe the employees should take a closer look. I mean, it is pretty obvious… the white stuff isn’t snow, but mold.

What happened to your standards, Whole Foods? On the West Coast, Whole Foods has it together. In the South, it seems like you have partnered with Wal-Mart.

Whole Foods Market is a popular American grocery store chain known for its commitment to selling natural and organic products. Founded in 1980 in Austin, Texas, Whole Foods quickly expanded by focusing on high-quality foods free from artificial preservatives, colors, flavors, and sweeteners. The company became a leader in the organic movement and established strict quality standards that set it apart from traditional supermarkets.

Whole Foods offers a wide selection of products, including fresh produce, meats, seafood, baked goods, dairy, and specialty items like vegan and gluten-free foods. It also emphasizes locally sourced products and often partners with regional farmers and producers. Shoppers at Whole Foods can find items that cater to specific dietary needs, such as paleo, keto, and plant-based diets.

In 2017, Amazon acquired Whole Foods, bringing about major changes such as lower prices on select items, integration with Amazon Prime for discounts, and expanded delivery services. This acquisition helped Whole Foods reach an even larger audience while maintaining its original commitment to quality and sustainability.

Beyond groceries, Whole Foods is known for its eco-friendly initiatives. Stores often feature recycling programs, sustainable seafood certifications, and efforts to reduce plastic use. Many locations are also active in their communities, supporting local charities and hosting educational events about healthy living.

While Whole Foods has sometimes faced criticism for high prices, it remains a favorite among shoppers who prioritize organic foods and a transparent supply chain. Its blend of quality, ethics, and convenience continues to influence the way many Americans shop and eat. Whether you are looking for fresh, responsibly sourced ingredients or specialty health products, Whole Foods has earned a reputation as a trusted name in the natural foods industry.

text.text:
Sure, most grocery stores are basically the same… until you’re on a “get over him and into something sparkling” girls’ trip to Nashville. Enter the Whole Foods on Broadway, aka the unofficial sponsor of our Hot Sad Boy Heartbreak Recovery Tour.

We rolled in needing the essentials: champagne for brunch, steaks for dinner, and tissues for that post-mimosa spiral (because healing isn’t always linear, especially after T. Swift starts playing). And guess what? Whole Foods had everything, plus vibes, good lighting, and not a single ex in sight.

The staff was so helpful, like emotionally supportive but in a “let me help you pull up your Amazon Prime for that sweet little discount” kind of way. The store was spotless, beautifully stocked, and even the checkout process was smooth (which is more than I can say about my last relationship).

If you’re visiting Nashville with your crew and need to stock up on provisions for a weekend of emotional detox and excellent snacking, this Whole Foods is where it’s at. Who knew heartbreak could be cured with bubbles, ribeyes, and a coupon?

Highly recommend, 10/10 Would cry in the champagne aisle again.

If you’re in Chattanooga and looking for a top-tier grocery experience, the Whole Foods Market at 301 Manufacturers Rd is a standout destination. From the moment you step inside, you’re greeted by a team of genuinely friendly and helpful staff who go above and beyond to assist with your shopping needs. Their warmth and professionalism truly enhance the shopping experience. ￼

The store itself is impeccably clean and well-organized, making it easy to navigate through the aisles. Shelves are consistently well-stocked with a diverse selection of organic and specialty items, ensuring you find exactly what you’re looking for. The produce section is particularly impressive, offering a vibrant array of fresh fruits and vegetables that are both visually appealing and of high quality.

One of the highlights of this location is the hot and cold food bar. It’s a popular spot for both locals and visitors, offering a variety of delicious options that cater to different dietary preferences. Whether you’re in the mood for a hearty meal or a light salad, the buffet is always fresh and well-maintained. The seating area provides a comfortable space to enjoy your meal, with both indoor and outdoor options available.

Overall, the Whole Foods Market on Manufacturers Rd delivers an exceptional shopping and dining experience. Its combination of friendly staff, cleanliness, well-stocked shelves, and fresh offerings make it a must-visit for anyone seeking quality groceries and prepared foods in Chattanooga.

text.text:
I have been shopping here regularly for many years.  I was friends with Diane years ago, before the store moved.  I don't usually give negative reviews, but I feel somewhat bittersweet by my experience lately.  I want to love this store completely, because the selections are genuinely fantastic and the lower prices keep me coming back. Also, the produce, especially. in the last few months has been looking super fresh.  I did notice the new produce guy and he has been very professional and helpful.
However, lately often when I visit, I notice a very tense atmosphere. The employees seem to be efficient and do their jobs, but there's this palpable feeling of stress. Conversations with some of the staff are brief, tense, and everyone seems to keep their heads down. One Sunday I saw a lady, who seemed to be a manager belittling and mocking an employee right in front of me. It was very unprofessional. A few minutes later the employee was in tears. The general mood is more apprehensive than welcoming, which is odd since I know they're putting out great efforts.  I hope the ownership takes note and finds a way to cultivate a more supportive and positive environment.

I always love picking up the ingredients I need at Diane's! I always head first to the produce section. So many good nutritious whole foods available. I even picked up Broccoli Sprouts this time!

I came in specifically for magnesium. I like to wander to the back left corner of the store where clearance items are kept. Sure enough, I found Magnesium + Calcium daily tablets at an almost $10 discount from its original shelf price. I'll take it! Even found biotin supplements at a discount too. There are all kinds of goodies in that corner marked down from their original price. Some visits what I discover in that clearance corner might be a hit-or-miss, but this time I found exactly what I was seeking at a great deal in my preferred health food store.

The prices are high compared to regular grocery stores--but understandably so. It is because the natural, organic, clean or vegan products and ingredients found in this store are worth the money. I prefer to treat my body and my family with only the best foods as often as I can. I wish I could go on a shopping spree here! Instead I just supplement my recipes with organic replacements if at all possible, and we can find here almost everything with need for juicing daily.

Thanks for existing, Diane's. You're just a hop, skip and a jump away here in St. Augustine. Cheers to good health!

text.text:
We've been longtime EarthFare customers, and in more than one state. Today, we were shopping in the meat department for "fresh" grass-fed ground beef and bought some.

Once home, we unwrapped it and found what you see in the attached photos—it looks like the "fresh" red meat had been wrapped around a core of old brownish-gray meat (which actually smelled). How else could the old meat be inside the new meat?

We opened the second package of meat this morning and found the same thing (see the additional 3 pics). This can't be by accident.

It seems the meat department needs serious remedial training in safety policies and health practices (at least). Customers could become ill if they didn't spot this before making hamburgers.

Very disappointing, to say the least, for a store that prides itself on organics, on product quality, and, from its own marketing, on a commitment to ethical management practices.

By the way, before posting this here, we went to the EarthFare website but could find no information for customers to contact the company or even provide feedback—apparently you're left dealing with a local store in person or by phone only, which is astounding in 2025.

P.S. I had to hit a single star instead of the zero (0) which was merited here.

text.text:
​Jungle Jim's: An Absolute Global Food Odyssey

​Jungle Jim's isn't a grocery store; it's a theme park for your taste buds, a genuinely jaw-dropping, world-spanning epic. If you think you've seen a large supermarket before, think again—Jungle Jim's redefines the concept of "massive."
​Even browsing during a work trip, this place was absolutely insane. Walking into the store is an overwhelming, joyful assault on the senses. The selection is the selection of the century—it feels less like shopping and more like an international expedition. The aisles stretch out so far that, as you said, you truly feel like you reach a different zip code moving from end to end. Honestly, Walmart is much smaller and far less exciting.
​The sheer volume of products is staggering. You could spend an hour just in the hot sauce section, which is a glorious, fiery maze of global heat. Beyond the essentials, the store is a treasure trove of niche items and 'nic-nacs'—you'll find international snacks, peculiar candies, specialty wines, and rare cheeses you didn't know existed but now absolutely must have.
​I think I managed to walk only about 60% of the store, and I was exhausted and exhilarated by the sheer scale of the place. Jungle Jim's is an absolute must-visit destination for anyone who loves food and adventure. Prepare for sensory overload and clear out your refrigerator before you go!

​Even browsing during a work trip, this place was absolutely insane. Walking into the store is an overwhelming, joyful assault on the senses. The selection is the selection of the century—it feels less like shopping and more like an international expedition. The aisles stretch out so far that, as you said, you truly feel like you reach a different zip code moving from end to end. Honestly, Walmart is much smaller and far less exciting.
​The sheer volume of products is staggering. You could spend an hour just in the hot sauce section, which is a glorious, fiery maze of global heat. Beyond the essentials, the store is a treasure trove of niche items and 'nic-nacs'—you'll find international snacks, peculiar candies, specialty wines, and rare cheeses you didn't know existed but now absolutely must have.
​I think I managed to walk only about 60% of the store, and I was exhausted and exhilarated by the sheer scale of the place. Jungle Jim's is an absolute must-visit destination for anyone who loves food and adventure. Prepare for sensory overload and clear out your refrigerator before you go!

text.text:
I had recently decided to go gluten- and dairy-free. I was having such a difficult time in the big chain stores finding items that qualified for both. While searching the web, Kindred Market came up. I hadn't been there before and happened to be driving by, so I decided to stop in. I was overwhelmed (in a good way) by all of the choices! I took my time in each aisle because the items they have there are MUCH different than you'd find at Kroger or Walmart. Many local options, bulk options, gluten-free, dairy-free, you name it.

I thought I'd died and gone to heaven when I saw their dairy-free section! I went in there with the idea that I'd only buy some dairy-free yogurt and came out with a full reusable bag. My only wish (with every place I run into) is that they would stock gluten-free Angel Hair Pasta. I can only find it on Amazon and in larger quantities than I wish to purchase.

I'll be shopping here for my gluten- and dairy-free items from now on!

ETA: 4/27/2025 - Kindred Market got in Banza Chickpea Angel Hair Pasta this past Wednesday, and I stopped in to grab some on Thursday.

Tonight, I made my spaghetti with the angel hair pasta, and I'm in absolute LOVE! Thank you so, so much, Kindred Market! You're so amazing!

text.text:
While traveling we stopped here for food to take to a family gathering. It’s a compact size but has  myriad products and more than covers all the bases of what you’d want in a store with whole foods in its name.

Let’s not forget the first word in their name is LOVE and I was greeted immediately with a cheery “Welcome!” All the store staff smiled and were helpful.

Just inside the main entrance door before you enter the market is a sunlit, plant-filled eating area.

Inside the market are packed tables, shelves and displays for crystals, various lines of homeopathic remedies, essential oils, beauty care, clothing, books and health journals, vitamins, snack foods, mixes, refrigerated foods, Florida and local farmers’ organic fruits and vegetables, candy, protein bars and more.

I found exactly what I needed at the cafe which is kind of hidden at the front of the store behind the checkout registers area, directly to the right of the market doors.

Today in the case were grape leaves (like dolmades, but the sign just said grape leaves and I don’t know what was in them); a kale mixed salad; roasted spicy chicken pieces; sweet potato casserole; classic holiday green beans; curried chicken salad; and more. I got the chicken and the spinach noodles with tofu.

It’s a great store that feels very neighborly.

text.text:
I've been going to Rollin' Oats for probably 11 years or so now, and I'm so disappointed to know that Kim was let go. Her help in the supplements department was the majority of the reason I came.

I've been chronically ill since I had a massive allergic reaction in 2013, and Kim was listening to me before any doctor ever did. There are so many times where her recommendations were, quite literally, the reason I was able to still function. Specific example: my doctors ignored me for years when I expressed that my birth control was most likely creating a bunch of my health issues. Kim didn't. She got me to try evening primrose, and it was the only thing that got me through the days full of extreme body pain, emotional breakdowns in traffic, intense digestive issues, headaches, etc. Kim was right about it being a hormone balance issue, and gave me the validation that I needed. I finally found a doctor that listened, and she discontinued my birth control. So many of my issues cleared up almost immediately. It saved my life because it turns out that the style of birth control that I was on, combined with some of my other health issues, put me at an extremely high risk of stroke. It took 8 years to get a doctor to listen to me. Kim figured it out while I was on a shopping trip.

I was always able to trust that Kim knew what to recommend, and that she had my best interests at heart. It never felt like I was being sold the most expensive thing or dismissed. I don't think I ever asked her a question that she didn't know the answer to.

You lost a good one Rollin' Oats. I don't know what your reasoning was, but all I ever saw as as customer was a woman who cared, was very knowledgeable, and was worth waiting my turn to be helped in the aisles for.

This review is of the prepared foods section. I hesitated to post it; nonetheless, I am so sick of buying food that I cannot stomach and having to go back to the store to return it. Gosh!

I wonder how much of our hard earned money WFM is waiting on oils…. Have mercy! Why is the prepared  food literally swimming in oil????….all of the time! Why? Just why?? And what the heck is going on with the Mac and cheese; that stuff is like lard paste or glue. I met a man today who said he doesn’t know what’s in it, but he can’t eat that any more. It’s not like this in New York…at all. The food here raises many questions regarding health and wellness.

I like many other folks shop at WFM everyday and quite often 2 to 3 times per day at different stores. Alpharetta by far is the best right now because they are actually using olive oil on the food and not just some other pretend oils like quite a few of the other stores in the Atlanta area.

Anyway, back to Brookhaven….people shop at WFM because we are trying our best to eat and be healthier, but it the place(s) that we are supporting and depending on is giving us crap food…and thinks that we just have to take it…. (** like the pizza makers in all of the stores that deliver tasteless attitudes and shoulder shrug when asked to make a pizza because I/we don’t want to buy the slices that have been sitting out and look like they’ve been run over by two trucks**)…. oh boy…. folks will get tired of that very soon especially with the economy changing every second.

[**There are 2 ladies who are stellar and always kind and welcoming though— Ms. Angela and the polite Muslim sister that knows what she’s doing over there.**]

I’m gonna stop my rant now, but I am asking this store in particular for the 5-teenth time to PLEASE PLEASE STOP PUTTING SO MUCH GREASE IN THE FOOD. PLEASE MAKE IT EDIBLE AND HEALTHY 🙏

IF YOU NEED SOME ASSISTANCE AND POINTERS, I CAN HELP YOU ALL.

Now I should have taken a picture of more dishes floating in oil, but I didn’t because I was so disappointed. I am however posting a picture of the collard greens that are still as greasy as the oil pan under a car hood after trying to wash the oil off of the greens literally five times.

Lawd somebody call the heart surgeon and the gastroenterologist. 🤦‍♀️

I CANNOT EAT THIS!!
It makes me want to vomit, so as usual…it’s going back to them.

Perhaps WFM needs to examine the cooking team because as a former chef myself, I know that anyone who can actually cook knows how to nurture food and allow the actual flavors of the food to come out and shine through ✨
….like they’re doing in Alpharetta. You don’t even need all of that crap.! Like seriously yall. You’re wasting money, resources, and time.

This is partially what has so many people so sick and overweight right now anyway!! So cut it out.

So come on Whole Foods if you’re going to proclaim wellness then be that and exhibit the crème de la crème of it.

Is that too much to ask?!?

Whole Foods should be ashamed. I went to the hot bar today and got a tiny serving: some beans, plain white rice, and two small pieces of chicken. Nothing fancy, nothing gourmet — just basic food. At checkout, they charged me $29.
That’s not just expensive — it’s outright robbery. There is no excuse for pricing simple, everyday food at such an absurd rate. Whole Foods is clearly taking advantage of customers who expect quality and fairness. This was a complete scam.
I left feeling disgusted and ripped off. I will absolutely never buy from their hot bar again, and I seriously question if I’ll even keep shopping at Whole Foods at all. If you value your money, stay far away from their buffet.

text.text:
PLEASE READ IF VISITING THIS STORE.

I stopped in to pick up a few groceries from Whole Foods and a pizza from a nearby restaurant in Avalon. I left the Whole Foods parking area and came back — pizza in hand — to find a $55 ticket waiting on my car. I was parked by the bank, about as far from the store as you can get.

I did purchase what I needed from Whole Foods, but apparently stepping away for a few minutes to grab a pizza to-go is a $55 “lesson.”

They do have signs stating the parking is for Whole Foods visits only, and I admit I’ve never really mentally processed them in my many prior times shopping at Whole Foods. My main issue is that if someone was watching and immediately followed me to place a ticket on the car, they could have at least given a polite reminder. Placing a first-time warning on the car instead of a ticket would have been fair — they have my plate, after all, so how hard would that be. It feels like a heavy handed way to fleece $55 from someone. It’s also a little creepy that they appear to spy and follow you.

It’s their store and parking lot and they can set the rules, but I expected better. The store is nice and staff are always super friendly and helpful — this is just a horrible policy.

Other supermarket chains don’t fine me when I pop next door to quickly pick or drop off something up while shopping. This experience has made me rethink shopping at this Whole Foods.

My main issue is that if someone was watching and immediately followed me to place a ticket on the car, they could have at least given a polite reminder. Placing a first-time warning on the car instead of a ticket would have been fair — they have my plate, after all, so how hard would that be. It feels like a heavy handed way to fleece $55 from someone. It’s also a little creepy that they appear to spy and follow you.

It’s their store and parking lot and they can set the rules, but I expected better. The store is nice and staff are always super friendly and helpful — this is just a horrible policy.

Other supermarket chains don’t fine me when I pop next door to quickly pick or drop off something up while shopping. This experience has made me rethink shopping at this Whole Foods.

text.text:
Disappointed with Today’s Experience at Whole Foods

I genuinely love Whole Foods and willingly spend two hours on the road—one hour each way—just to shop for the products I truly enjoy. However, today, I was extremely disappointed by what I saw.

First, the parking lot was cluttered with shopping carts, while inside the store, only a few were available. I had to grab a smaller cart from the parking lot, which I actually prefer, but it was frustrating to see such disorganization.

The biggest disappointment, however, was in the fresh produce section. I was shocked to find mold on the mushrooms. Even if they are discounted, selling spoiled products is unacceptable. Additionally, I saw a rotten nectarine surrounded by fruit flies, which is simply disgraceful for a store with above-average—if not significantly higher—prices.

On a positive note, I do appreciate that Whole Foods has special items for Valentine’s Day, including berries in heart-shaped packaging. They also have Blood Oranges and Caracara oranges, which have unique and interesting flavors. Additionally, my favorite yogurts are available in special red packaging for the holiday.

I also want to highlight a new snack I tried today, which was on sale—a delicious peanut butter and grape jelly treat.

Once again, I want to emphasize that I love this store, and that’s exactly why I’m writing this review. I hope the management takes better care of the quality of the products on their shelves. Whole Foods should uphold the standards that loyal customers expect.

text.text:
A very cool place, I really enjoyed my shopping experience here! I originally went to return an Amazon package (great experience,) and had some grocery shopping to do, so I decided to look around a little bit, and I'm glad I did. If I could give a more accurate rating, I'd probably give it a 4.8 or 4.9.

The store is very clean and well-kept, and fun to walk around in. They have many of the basic things you'll find in a regular Big Box store, but an Organic version instead. Now, their portions are definitely smaller and more expensive, but I assume that the trade-off is that they're healthier and better for you.

Although I'm not an experienced drinker, they have a very large selection of both local alcohol and seltzers, as well as well-known national brands.

The only particular downside is that there were a few times that I thought the selection was a little too large, and I couldn't find an "original" or "classic" version of the item I was looking for. The two that stick out for this were the coffee and nut selections. I would've liked to see a basic version in addition to all the exotic flavors.

The customer service was great as well, and there were many pretty girls working there. There were two different times where I was asked if I needed help finding something, and when I asked a worker where something was, she very kindly told me the exact spot I could find it.

Overall, it was a nice trip and I'm excited to try the food I bought!

text.text:
The Whole Foods in Asheville is a solid grocery spot with a great atmosphere and consistently friendly service. Every time I’ve visited, the employees have gone out of their way to be helpful—whether it’s directing me to a specific product, offering a recommendation, or just greeting customers with a smile. You can tell the staff here takes pride in what they do, and it definitely makes the shopping experience more enjoyable.

The store itself is clean, well-organized, and stocked with a wide variety of high-quality items—from organic produce and fresh bakery goods to specialty items you can’t find at regular grocery stores. Their hot bar and prepared foods section is also a plus, especially if you’re looking for something quick and healthy on the go. I’ve picked up lunch here a few times, and it’s always fresh and flavorful.

Parking is easy, and the location is convenient if you’re coming from downtown or nearby neighborhoods. While prices are what you’d expect from Whole Foods, the quality and service make it worth it.

Overall, this Whole Foods does a great job representing the Asheville community—laid-back, welcoming, and focused on quality. Definitely one of the better Whole Foods locations I’ve been to.

I had a very disappointing experience at the bakery section of this Whole Foods. We purchased a fruit cake, only to discover that some of the fruits on top were clearly rotten. When we brought it to the staff’s attention, we were told not to touch it anymore — because “now they can’t sell it.”

That response was honestly shocking. It seemed like they fully intended to resell a cake topped with visibly spoiled fruit. That’s not only unacceptable customer service, but also a serious food safety issue.

I’ve always trusted Whole Foods for its quality and freshness, which makes this experience even more disappointing. I hope management investigates how something like this made it to the sales floor — and that they rethink how their bakery team handles customer concerns.

I usually love this Whole Foods and have never had a problem. I actually drive 30 minutes just to come to this location, even though there’s one closer to my home, because the selection is better and the store is always clean and well-stocked.

But today, I had a disappointing experience at the coffee counter that left me feeling uneasy. I walked up to order and the older woman working there didn’t acknowledge me at all. She saw me standing there, walked away without saying a word, and left me waiting for about three minutes. When she returned, she still didn’t speak to me. She just asked another employee, “Is the coffee station closed?” He said yes, and she turned to me and said, “Yeah, we’re closed.”

No greeting. No apology for the wait. No effort to communicate respectfully.

It may not sound major, but as someone who shops here often and chooses to spend my time and money at this specific store, it made me feel unseen and dismissed. It’s the kind of interaction that makes you second-guess whether you’re truly welcome in a space, especially when basic courtesy is missing.

I hope this was just a one-off moment, but it was enough to make me look at this location a little differently.

text.text:
I recently visited the Whole Foods in Winter Park, Florida, and overall, it was a delightful shopping experience that I’d rate at four stars. Here’s why:

Food Options Galore:
One of the standout features of this Whole Foods is its impressive array of food options. From fresh produce to specialty items, it feels like a culinary paradise. The store offers an extensive selection of organic fruits and vegetables, artisan cheeses, and unique snacks. The highlight, however, is the hot food bar. They have an impressive variety of food options, including brick oven Pizza, Pastries, plant based options, as well as a coffee bar, making it easy to grab a delicious, meal on the go. Whether you’re in the mood for comfort food or something more exotic, there’s something for everyone.

Seating and Atmosphere:
The indoor and outdoor seating arrangements are fantastic. The spacious layout provides a welcoming atmosphere where you can sit down and enjoy your meal, whether you choose to dine inside amidst the vibrant decor or outside on the patio, soaking up the Florida sun. It’s a great spot for catching up with friends or enjoying a quiet moment with a good book.

Convenience Features:
Another big plus is the Amazon drop-off point. This feature makes it incredibly convenient for those of us who shop at Amazon frequently; it’s a seamless way to return items without the hassle of extra trips. It’s a nice touch that adds to the overall convenience of shopping here.

Cleanliness and Organization:
The store is impeccably clean and well-organized. Each section is easy to navigate, and the staff regularly keeps the areas tidy. I appreciate a store that prioritizes cleanliness, especially when it comes to food. It certainly enhances the overall shopping experience.

Pricing:
Now, let’s talk about the pricing. While Whole Foods is known for its high-quality products, it’s also infamous for its higher price points. This location is no exception. Many items are on the pricier side, which can be a deterrent for budget-conscious shoppers. However, the quality often justifies the cost, especially if you’re looking for organic and specialty items.

Staff Friendliness:
As for the employees, I found most to be friendly and helpful. They’re knowledgeable about the products and eager to assist customers. However, I did encounter one or two staff members who seemed less enthusiastic, which was a bit off putting in an otherwise positive environment. It’s a small detail, but it’s worth noting.

Final Thoughts:
In conclusion, the Whole Foods in Winter Park offers a fantastic shopping experience with a wonderful range of food options, great seating, and convenient features like the Amazon drop-off. While the prices can be high, the quality of the products often makes it worth it. With a friendly atmosphere and a mostly helpful staff, I would definitely recommend this location to anyone in the area. I’m looking forward to my next visit!

text.text:
Actually went here to drop off an Amazon return. First time here, I came from Countryside Drive and saw several Handicap parking on the south side, so parked there and walked to door. Doors locked! No sign indicating that. Strike one. I parked at the busy west entrance halfway down a row. I walked through the store and was very pleased with their selection of fresh fruits and veggies. We still order for home delivery most times and often disappointed on the quality of fruits. Often they are very unripe or very ripe. So I grabbed a lot of fresh fruits and veggies to bring home. I did look at a lot of the things they carried, pretty extensive list, but most were priced higher for pantry items we stock, so just the fresh stuff.

I had been told that returning things to Amazon was very quick and easy, provided you had the original box, which we did. My wife wears a 10.5 wide shoe but the ordered ones were really not wide. When I arrived at the back of the store, where I was directed for return drop offs, I was shocked to see a line of 10 people waiting. No live person, just a machine. Not the best for some "mature" people not used to electronics. After a wait of some 20 minutes, an attendant came, so most were waiting on her. The line for machine was empty now, so I decided to use it.

The instructions were pretty clear, so I followed them but had a bit of an issue getting the return label scanned, but finally got it. Put the shoebox in a plastic bag provided on top the machine, placed the sticker return label on the bag. Then pressed Next and door opened to place item inside, which I did. Next I was prompted to close the door, but I couldn't! The bin to hold items was full and my shoebox was halfway in. So I was stuck. I couldn't finish the process since it was telling me I must close the door. And the bin was far enough away that I couldn't reach my bag to pull it out.

I waited while the attendant finished with a customer and asked her for help. She replied "Sir, I'll be with you in one minute." So I waited, for ten minutes. Again I asked for help "I just need for you to pull bin out so I can finish." "Sie, I said I will be with you in ONE MINUTE!" Another 10 minutes wait, so I called the store and asked for someone to PLEASE come back and help with an issue with the Return machine. Another 10 minutes, someone finally came opened the bin. But my session on the machine had timed out. I thought I would have to start over but he said the return code was read and return label was printed, so my return was fine, nothing else needed. Strike two. So had I been told that, I could have saved myself 30 minutes of frustrated wait time! I will not be back.

Fresh fruits and veggies - 5 stars. Prices minus 1 star. Customer service minus 1 star. Thus my 3 star rating.

text.text:
Whole Foods definitely leans pricey and trendy, but when you catch a good sale, some items are actually more affordable than other stores. I’ve found great deals on dairy-free milks and yogurts I can’t get anywhere else in Wilmington, which keeps me coming back.

The store is always sparkling clean, and the staff are consistently friendly and helpful. I usually stop in with my daughter to grab a few sale items and pick out a cupcake or bakery treat—we love that their baked goods are free from synthetic food dyes, which is a rare find in mainstream grocery chains.

There’s a wide selection of specialty items, and trying new things here feels fun. The atmosphere makes you feel a little fancy (which is totally intentional, and honestly, it works). That said, not everything here is as “clean” as the branding suggests—read your labels if that matters to you.

✅ Super clean store
✅ Friendly staff
✅ Hard-to-find dairy-free items
🎯 Tip: Check sales before shopping and don’t skip the bakery
🧁 Favorite treat: dye-free cupcakes

text.text:
If you are not familiar with Whole Foods, this is a really great place to shop for Natural and Organic foods. They have a lovely Meat and Produce section. The nuts, grains, and granola section is vast. The prices can be high, but if you are a Prime Member, you can get a discount on items that are already on Sale. This location has a Salad and Hot Bar. They also have freshly made hot pizzas and Sushi. The deli has cold cuts and premade items like chicken and pasta salad. The cheese section is really nice. If you are looking for a particular Cheese, they probably have it. They have an excellent bakery with Breads and Sweets and an all-natural area that sells vitamins, cosmetics, soaps, etc.… There is an excellent wine and beer selection with local beers.

This location, in my opinion, is overdue for a remodel. There is nothing wrong with the current store, and they keep it clean, but compared to the newer locations I have shopped at, I think it is time for an upgrade. This is a must-try if you visit or live in the area.

text.text:
I really enjoy coming to this location. It’s close to my home, the store is typically well stocked, and most of the employees are always friendly and helpful.

That being said, there is one concern I feel should be addressed. The employee with blonde hair who works at the Amazon returns counter has consistently shown poor customer service. She often appears frustrated when customers come in with returns, avoids assisting people in line, and tends to make customers feel like they are inconveniencing her.

For example, during my last visit, a gentleman came in after 9 a.m. unsure where to go. Instead of politely guiding him, she told him to wait while she “got things ready” and then walked around without helping him. He remained polite, but her attitude was dismissive and unprofessional.

Good customer service doesn’t mean the work won’t be busy—it means communicating with kindness and professionalism no matter the situation. I come here often and have repeatedly witnessed this same behavior, which is disappointing given how wonderful the rest of the staff is.

I believe this is something management should address to ensure all customers have a positive experience.

She was the opening employee at 9am on 8/22/25.

text.text: Went at lunchtime and the salad and hot food bars at this Whole Foods are depressing.  Half the hot food bar is empty and the cold foods are gone and replaced by…drinks.  They cut the salad bar and cold foods bar in half and combined them.  50% of the salad bar is empty as well. So overall less than half the options of a well run Whole Foods. Oh and they raised the price from $7.99 to 11.99 per pound.  So basically half the options and almost double the price.  Overall the quality of the food is terrible and crusty.  All fried chicken tenders and Mac and Cheese type stuff.  Nothing remotely healthy or of decent quality.  It looks like fast food that’s been sitting out for 8 hours.  I’ve traveled extensively on the road and have been to about 100 different Whole Foods across the US.  It’s sad honestly this is quite possibly the worst Whole Foods in the United States.  Luckily it’s just this Whole Foods. The ones in South Florida, Tampa and Boston that I’ve gone to in the past couple months are fine.  This Whole Foods and the other Sarasota Whole Foods should be avoided if possible.

UPDATE

It’s not even 1pm on a Tuesday, the hot bar is emptied out, the salad bar is empty, no pizza. This place needs an overhaul, the other two locations never have this issue and this the situation here most days. This location doesn’t represent the brand very well, if anyone came in and had never been to another location they would likely think this was how they all are. Get it together. See updated pics.

I mean, it’s a Whole Foods, it’s clean and the people are decent. The problem is the absolute and utter inconsistency in the food bar. Some days there’s a full bar, some days there’s no lettuce on the salad bar, some days there’s no food at all. If you are wanting a quick breakfast burrito there’s maybe a %50 chance that there will be any food put out for breakfast at all. Often there are dishes like curry but no rice. Also, the food is set out very late so if you show up at 11 and you’re on a time crunch, don’t count on eating. More often than not I am disappointed by their food bar at this location. They need to fix it, I generally just won’t come here if I don’t have time to go to a backup plan because of how frequently they just don’t have what I need.

The cashiers are nice too. I deducted a star because the floor has these annoying metal plates interspersed throughout the aisles, and poorly planned aisle spaces, with pillars that are really close to some of the shelves, so that if you want to get anything you have to basically squeeze in between the shelves and the pillar to get items. It's not horrible enough to make me not want to go, but it is a minor annoyance, enough to make me want to deduct a star from my rating.

text.text: This is my local grocerier and as much as we’d love to support them over TJs or WF the pricing gouging is out of control. The quality of prepared foods has gone down and the pricing has skyrocketed (items are an average of $1-3+ more expensive than WF). $23 for strawberries? TWENTY THREE DOLLARS?!?! (Same type were $8 at WF - which is still a rip. See photos). I mean, FFS. I can’t believe they had the audacity to print and post that price. Convenience is the only thing they offer and I only shop there if I’m desperate these days. Also you have to check everything that gets scanned as a lot of time the sale prices don’t register or pricing comes up completely different than what is listed. ALSO, check the expiration dates - more than once have a found old, expired products on the shelves. It’s a shame because it’s a nice, clean store with a good selection/variety but it feels like a battle every time I shop there.

text.text:
My spouse and I have both dined here as well as hosted a wedding event here. In both cases, the staff, atmosphere, and food were incredible.

Rachel, the Events Director, was phenomenal to work with in the lead up to our event (as was all the staff!) I could tell that our event going well was as important to her as it was to us, and she truly made us feel like family when it came to advising us on menu, music, decor, and run of show. While we did have our own planner, Rachel brought a lot of details to our attention that we wouldn't have otherwise thought of, so it really felt like we got lucky and had two amazing planners.

We also have a lot of non-drinkers and we wanted to serve an all vegetarian menu, so finding a venue that could accommodate our needs was super important - the drinks and food menu is so versatile and FtP made sure we were all fed and watered 💙

The night of the event itself was a dream and went so smoothly. The staff and kitchen made sure everything was tasty and served on time with our schedule. Our guests had an incredible time and we are actually still hearing compliments about the event, the venue, and the food over a month later.

We can't say enough good things about Rachel and her team, and we are forever grateful for such a special night!

text.text:
Came here for a late dinner close to the restaurant’s closing time. Our waitress was exceptionally kind and accommodating.

We ordered a variety of apps and the shaved kimchi beef for our main. For apps we got fries, ceviche, tzatziki, and an order of pita. Note that the tzatziki itself does not come with anything so you’ll need to order something else to dip.

The fries were nice and crispy. The ceviche was tasty as well, but felt the sweet potato was unnecessary. The tzatziki went well with the soft pita bread, and was quite large in portion.

The shaved kimchi beef felt like a more extravagant Korean chipotle bowl. All the flavors were tasty, but the dish itself was not quite what I was expecting. I’m not sure I would choose to pay $30 for it again.

I think we definitely over ordered and filled up quickly on the apps. Overall the quality of the ingredients felt very good and the produce tasted fresh. However, the flavors themselves were not something I’d write home about. I would consider Farm to People a solid restaurant if I had no other options nearby, but don’t see myself coming back.

text.text:
I’ve been shopping here for about five years now, and it’s one of the best places for fresh, high-quality produce. Everything is high quality and locally sourced.

One of my favorites is their ice cream selection. They offer a wide variety of flavors from local producers, like Van Leeuwen and Jeni's.

The coop also regularly hosts local events like plant swaps, which is a fun and free way to get new  plants.

Most of the staff has been fantastic over the years — always friendly, helpful, and knowledgeable. That being said, recently an older Indian woman, who works as a manager or staff member, felt the need to follow me around the store. Yikes!!! This was a one-off incident though and I’m removing a star due to that experience.

My recent visit to **Food Bazaar** was fantastic! The store is **immaculately organized and well-maintained**, with wide aisles, neatly stocked shelves, and an impressive selection of products—from fresh produce and groceries to international foods and household essentials. The layout makes shopping a breeze, and the **ongoing promotions** make it even more budget-friendly.

What really impressed me was their **Food Bazaar app**, which lets you **accumulate points on every purchase** and redeem them for discounts on future shopping trips. It’s such a great perk on top of their already amazing deals!

The **staff was incredibly friendly and helpful**, always ready to assist with a smile. Even though the checkout area was busy, the lines moved **quickly and efficiently**—no long waits!

Another huge advantage is the **spacious free parking lot**, so you never have to stress about finding a spot.

Between the **well-stocked store, fantastic prices, helpful employees, and the rewarding app**, Food Bazaar has become my go-to grocery store. Highly recommend downloading their app to maximize savings!

Pro Tip: Stack their in-store promotions with app rewards for even bigger savings!

text.text:
Fresh Direct Manhattan
Epic fail.  I have been buying from FreshDirect for years without very many poor incidences. However, this is the first time I have ordered in many months, and what a huge disappointment! I took pictures of the produce and bread last week when I received it to complain about the quality however, this week, I am adding to it due to the spoilage rate as well.

I was shocked by how filthy the celery and cilantro was and there was so much sand in the cilantro and so much dirt in the celery that it was clear the produce hadn’t even been given a perfunctory washdown.

The bagels and the sourdough bread were stale when I received them, so I ordered another loaf uncut the next day. However, those two bread products have since gone completely bad and moldy, see pictures attached. This tells me the product is either not being stored correctly or is being bought very late in the game and is already on the verge of spoilage by the time it’s delivered. That’s my personal take.

Of course I will go back to FreshDirect because i find them terribly convenient and overall this is my first terrible experience. but another experience like this would drive me away permanently.

Also, worth noting since they changed the bag styles to no longer have a cover flap and we were experiencing heavy rain, there was about a half an inch to an inch of water in the bottom of each bag. Not nice.

text.text:
So I ordered from these guys and they missed their promised delivery window by two hours and then (wish I was exaggerating here) half the order was missing. Then I called customer service and someone located abroad tells me sorry they can get me SOME of my missing items to me express and that will be there four hours later (makes you wonder how they define the word "express"). Plot twist: that express, emergency order arrives three hours late as well! You can not make up this level of incompetence.

Go ahead and search for reviews online. This is common with Fresh Direct. There is an entire subreddit dedicated to the chaos they cause in people's lives. The staff that work their call center must get paid handsomely because that level of curtness and blithe disinterest in your problems cannot come cheap.

And when the second half of my original order finally arrived? All the eggs were broken so I had to spend more time washing egg yolk off my vegetables and then calling customer service (again!) to beg to have the eggs refunded. Never ordering from these guys again.
