text.text:
Really lovely food coop and community of folks. Rotating seasonal produce (root veggies, fruit, greens), bread (including good gluten-free options), plenty of pantry items (broth, pasta, oils/vinegars, etc.), household items (paper towels, detergent, etc.), bulk goods (nuts, grains, coffee, tea, etc.), and perishables (meat, dairy, vegan, frozen foods, etc.). When you become a member, you put in a few hours per month to keep prices low and it's also a nice way to meet folks and learn how everything works.

I've been a member for about a year and half and been very glad for it. If you're not a member, just stop by and ask about joining (can always look around and do a trial membership to see whether it fits your needs). You can then just stick with shopping and putting in your occasional hours or always get more involved too as you get more comfortable -- e.g., helping decide what to buy, attending meetings, etc.

text.text:
Kalustyan’s has been a wonderland of spices, herbs, teas, and more in Manhattan for ages. I’ve had the pleasure of shopping here on many occasions. I love being able to select more varieties of curry than anywhere else in the city. I already have hot Jamaican curry, this time I chose Trinidadian curry. There are varieties from a vast number of countries, each with their own unique flavor profile. In addition, I was able to find Chinese herbs of Anjelica Sinensis or Dong Quai (women’s ginseng), a pepper popular in Nepal, a variety of American bbq spices, dried and chilis, and so much more!

I noticed they carry rose water, orange blossom water, lavender, many natural hair care products, different coffee types ranging from those commonly found and used in America to more international varieties and favorites like Turkish coffee and the copper coffee pot. There are many baking products like differing levels of dutch cocoa powder, sugar - demerara, coconut sugar, many more kinds. A large array of flour types, sprinkles and dragees, including the De Ruijter variety beloved in The Netherlands for fairy bread.

You’ll find spices, herbs, ingredients, and sauces from all parts of the world. They also have some baklava and desserts near the register, even Dubai chocolate. In the back, there are many refrigerators and freezers with a variety of foods like Naan, Ras Malai, yogurts, meals, tapenades, olives, kefir, and so much more. Be sure to stop in if you’re in the neighborhood or visiting from abroad. This is a wonderful gem of a shop with many great options!

text.text:
I’ve been a loyal Stop & Shop customer for many years and have always appreciated the friendly and helpful staff. Lately, though, I’ve noticed that some items I regularly shop for are often out of stock, which has meant making additional trips to other stores to complete my shopping. I’m wondering if some of these stocking challenges might be related to broader sourcing issues.

I also noticed the recent store layout changes, and while I understand updates can be necessary, it’s made finding items a bit more time-consuming.

I still appreciate the customer service, but due to these recent experiences, I’ve started shopping at other stores where I’ve been able to consistently find everything I need in one trip. I hope things improve soon, as I’d love to return to Stop & Shop as my go-to grocery store.

Who decided to screw up the store? This new layout is absurd. I can find cookies in several different aisles.  They have a chips/pretzels section that takes up about 20% of the store and I never see anyone in it. Candy takes up 25% of an aisle yet there is no sign telling you where it is located. It's so messed up that nobody in my family will shop here anymore.  It takes 10x longer .  It's not because it was redesigned and we aren't used to it, it's because the redesign is ridiculous.  Someone was drunk when they came up with this plan. It makes NO SENSE and is incredibly awkward.  Now Shop Rite has gotten more crowded, especially since Stop n' Shop raised their prices  to charge us for the redesign. This store is so stupid they don't realize that Ocean State JobLot (next door) has some of the same items for half the price!!!

The store is fairly empty these days. I predict it will close within the next 2 years.

One more thing...they are ALWAYS OUT OF STOCK and when you ask the staff,  nobody  knows why!!

text.text: I was shopping with my ebt card and one of the items that is ebt eligible wasn’t registering as a food/beverage item. The “manager”, a woman with short medium brown hair and highlights, told me she doesn’t know what’s eligible and she didn’t know what do and she was clearly pushing me to pay for it in cash when it’s an ebt item. I didn’t have time for all of that so ended up having to pay for it and leaving. I am on ebt for a reason and i have a budget, I can’t afford to pay for the incompetence of this grocery store manager. This was a regular beverage item. She should know what items are ebt eligible if she’s managing a GROCERY STORE, she also hardly showed concern in the fact that the item was being registered wrong in their system which is what pissed me off the most and tells me she won’t be proactive in fixing it for the future. I will be contacting the state ebt agency to ensure they remain in compliance with SNAP eligibility rules.

text.text:
To the Store Manager:
This may come as news to you but some of us work on the weekends, and when we make the effort to stop by your store before noon. expecting to pick up a ready-made sandwich for lunch, it’s disappointing to find none available. As a business, isn’t your goal to meet customer needs —especially during peak times— and generate revenue in the process, is it not? SMH

REVISION
One thing that is consistent about Stop & Shop is their lack of consistency. I stopped by a while ago for a California Turkey Panini. The sign in the case clearly states that the sandwich contains avocado (which is what makes it California), but there was no avocado to be found on the entire sandwich. At this point, they should probably rename it the "New York Turkey Panini" because it's pretty far from California. Or maybe the "Disappointment Panini – truth in advertising and all that.

text.text:
This is the closest WFM to us. It’s relatively smaller than some of the other ones we have been to. Still they have all the services like bakery, butcher, seafood, cheese, pizza and sandwiches. The hot bar and salad bar are also there. I love the potato samosas they make. I get them often. We also get cookies and brownies from the bakery section. We also had ordered birthday cake with them for our daughter. It was perfectly made and ready for pick up on scheduled day.

Through out the store they have many items on sale. They keep excellent inventory of healthy and sugar free drinks. Produce has lots of good quality fruits and vegetables. They also promote lots unique, local and homemade brands through out the store.

At the entrance they have the customer service booth. There’s also the Amazon prime service area for package pick up and returns. I have returned many items here over the years. Always a good quick service.

The store is very well maintained. I have never seen a mess or dirt in the store. There’s a dining area available near exit door. Lots of self checkout lanes available, have never seen a long line. Lots of customers do online grocery pick up orders from here as well. It is a very popular location among locals, always having lots of foot traffic.

Without a doubt, this is the best Whole Foods in the Westchester area. They have a large selection of items, customer support lane at the entrance, plenty of self checkout machines/cashier lanes, a clean public restroom/dining area, free WiFi and an Amazon return/pickup station. Whatever you need or want, they got it and the staff are always willing and able to help. There is only one major problem with the location and that is their new automated parking system. They have plenty of paid parking spots and the first 30 minutes are free, but they take pictures of your license plate as soon as you enter/exit. Meaning, you better watch the clock the second you enter the parking facility (it's not managed by them but rather Ridgehill Mall). Good news is, they usually have free 10-15 min parking spots outside the facility if you are suspicious like myself about people photographing your license plate.
Oh and it should go without saying, it's Whole Foods, be prepared to spend a pretty penny. However, if you have Amazon Prime, you get 10% off sale items. So I highly recommend to check the Whole Foods app or Amazon app for their current sales. Other than that, I highly recommend this Whole Foods.

text.text:
I used to love Whole Foods, but this location has been consistently frustrating - and I’ve truly reached my limit.

1.    Constantly empty shelves. Many times I’ve visited, essential items like fresh produce, milk, meat, and other basics are simply out of stock. It’s shocking how frequently the shelves are half-empty.

2.    Expired products on the shelves. I have personally found expired items multiple times. Once, I even told a staff member that many products on a shelf were expired - and when I returned a week later, those same expired items were still there. I ended up removing them myself and handing them to an employee, who looked completely indifferent.

3.    Unsanitary practices at the hot food area. I once witnessed a cleaning staff member spraying disinfectant directly on the glass barrier - while food was sitting right below it. It’s unacceptable to ignore the risk of contamination like that.

4.    Spoiled chicken and awful customer service. The final straw was buying a whole packaged chicken that reeked when I opened it - and this was before the sell-by date. I called the store and was told I could get a refund on my next visit. But when I returned, the customer service guy rolled his eyes and asked, with a condescending tone, “Did you bring the chicken?”
•    Obviously, I didn’t keep a rotten chicken sitting in my house for a week - why would anyone do that?
•    He then said I should have come back the same day, as if he knew anything about my schedule or whether I even had transportation that day.
•    And when I pointed that out, he suggested I could have put the chicken in a Ziploc bag - as if everyone just happens to have a giant Ziploc bag to hold an entire chicken.
Not only did I lose the dinner I had planned to cook, but the spoiled chicken stank up my entire kitchen. And instead of an apology or any empathy, I was met with eye-rolling and a dismissive attitude - an unacceptable response from a store that claims to care about quality and customer experience.

This is by far the worst Whole Foods I’ve ever visited - and that’s deeply disappointing coming from a brand I used to trust and love.

text.text:
I visited this Whole Foods to return an Amazon package while traveling in New York, and it turned out to be incredibly convenient! The return process is on the second floor, where self-service machines and helpful staff make it quick and easy. Upstairs, there’s a small Kimaka coffee bar and plenty of seating areas, which was a pleasant surprise in such an expensive area. It’s perfect for a quick rest or even getting some work done.

The first floor has the classic Whole Foods setup with a wide variety of products and plenty of checkout counters. While it’s not the tidiest, it’s impressive for Manhattan, where spacious places to sit and eat are rare. You can grab food from the first floor and relax upstairs. For a grocery store in such a busy area, this location offers a great shopping and dining experience. Highly recommend stopping by if you’re staying nearby—ideal for shopping, resting, or even working for a bit!

I went to Whole Foods today around 3pm to return an Amazon package and had a very unpleasant experience. The staff member worked at Amazon returns was extremely rude and unprofessional, speaking in a disrespectful tone that clearly carried personal emotion.

The issue started because I didn’t see the small sign indicating where the line began. The “Exit” door was already open, so naturally I just walked through. The sign was so tiny that it was almost impossible to notice unless you looked very carefully. Instead of kindly pointing this out, the staff member spoke to me rudely and told me to go all the way back.

If she had spoken politely, I would have had no problem complying. But as a customer, I should not have to deal with an employee’s negative attitude while shopping.

Whole Foods needs to:
1.	Make the return line signage larger and clearer so all customers can see it easily.
2.	Hire staff with basic courtesy and professionalism, or provide proper training to ensure they treat customers with respect.

text.text:
If you read past Google reviews, you'll see customers reporting RACISM, RACIAL PROFILING, AND DISCRIMINATION at this store. The pattern is clear, and the manager’s dismissive attitude is part of the problem. That’s why these experiences continue.

I reported a serious incident involving mistreatment that strongly appeared to be racist and discriminatory by an employee in the seafood department. What shocked me most was not only the behavior of the employee, but also the store’s refusal to take any meaningful action or even acknowledge wrongdoing. According to the manager, KUNHO, I will receive neither an apology from the employee nor any follow-up from the store. He questioned whether my experience was real but wouldn’t even attempt to verify what happened while I was still physically present in the store. When I offered to wait so he could check the camera, he told me I could wait as many hours as I liked, and he still wouldn’t check it because he was “very busy.” What kind of manager responds like that? Shame on you, KUNHO.

To the employee: If you do not want to interact with customers respectfully, why not work at a place where you do not need to deal with customers? That way, you will have no opportunity to mistreat customers, and more people will be happy.

To the store manager KUNHO: I hope you and your family will never be mistreated like that in any place by any employee like yours, and if that unfortunately happens, the issue will be resolved effectively by a good store manager—not someone like you.

I am very disappointed with Whole Foods for continuing to sell Lake Champlain Chocolates that are clearly not fresh and are only a few days away from their expiration date 12/1/24. I purchase these chocolates frequently and recently bought some on sale a few weeks ago. The product tasted spoiled, stale, and nothing like it normally does.

I informed customer service about the issue, yet the chocolates remained on the shelf. When I returned yesterday and purchased them again, the taste was even worse. This is unacceptable. Shame on Whole Foods Port Chester for prioritizing profit over customer health and quality.

Prices ring up higher than what is labeled!

This whole foods consistently has prices ringing up higher than what is labeled.  I've had several items rung up higher than what is labeled on several occurrences while shopping here. Today, I bought turkey slices labeled at 4.99. It rung up for $7.99. When I alerted the cashier,  the female supervisor on staff refused to give the item for free.  Instead, she edited the price of the item from $7.99 to $4.99 when ringing me up. She went and removed the incorrect price from the shelf. (Employee hand in pictures)

Please be diligent in checking what prices you are being charged when shopping here.

The store itself is great and employees are nice for the most part.  Just be sure to check your prices when being rung up at register.  I've only had an issue with that one supervisor.

I am writing this review to bring to light a serious safety issue and a concerning lack of professionalism at this Whole Foods store.

On multiple occasions, I have noticed that a couple of cars are consistently parked, bumper to bumper, directly in front of the main entry doorway. This is extremely dangerous. This area is designated as a walkway for customers, and these vehicles completely block the path, creating a significant hazard for anyone entering or exiting the store. It is clear the store has chosen to ignore this ongoing problem, which demonstrates a profound disregard for customer safety.

Today, at 4:43PM, I called the store to speak with a manager about this issue. The woman who answered the phone was rude and unprofessional. When I explained the problem, she became unprofessional and ended up hanging up on me. I immediately called back to express my frustration and asked for her name. She refused to provide it, only offering the names of her managers: Keith, Scott, and Rebecca. I told her that her behavior was unacceptable and that hanging up on a customer was completely unprofessional.

Due to the store's inaction on this safety hazard and the recent poor customer service experience, I will be filing a formal complaint with the Municipal Building. Whole Foods needs to do better.

text.text: Shopping at Whole Foods Market is interesting for me as I like to see all the aisles. This large location is on Seventh Avenue in Chelsea. As I enter, I am in the large vegetable and fruit section. Both organic and conventional varieties are available. Naturally organic prices are much higher. The fresh seafood and meat sections are next. Occasionally I get a salmon cake that I can sauté. In the middle of the store is the prepared foods and salad bar which is by weight. The cheese section is also there. Plant based pizzas and cauliflower crusts are in refrigerated cases. A variety of domestic and international butters are here priced decently that sometimes I can afford to buy them. Egg cartons are still rationed at three per customer due to the avian flu that had started a while back. These eggs range in price from $7 upwards. I don’t buy them as they are too pricey for me. My favorite section are the yogurts and when they are on sale I like to get Ellenos mango or passion fruit. Valley Shepherd Farm is another yogurt brand that I like a lot. Aisles are filled with teas, coffees, grains and the usual varieties of foods most supermarkets have. The body area is colorful and I like browsing here for deodorants on sale and the occasional face cleanser. One cannot forget the ice cream selections of which there are many. I am partial to Jeni’s Splendid ice cream in Wildberry Lavender and Dark Chocolate. Freshly baked breads, cakes and cookies are here too. I like the “Last Chance”where items are heavily discounted. One can either go to the self checkout machines or to the cashier. Magazines and temptations are always as one is waiting to pay. One needs self control not to go berserk! Two clean restrooms are here too which is convenient. Customer service is good with everyone trying to help you. Security guards are also manning the store and the entrance to avoid any incidents.

text.text:
If you’re looking for a top-tier supermarket with an exceptional fresh counter, this place is a hidden gem. The seafood, meat, and specialty products are of outstanding quality, making it a go-to destination for food lovers and home chefs alike.

The seafood section is particularly impressive—always fresh, well-stocked, and offering a wide variety of fish and shellfish. Whether you’re looking for wild-caught salmon, fresh oysters, or high-quality shrimp, you’ll find it here. The staff is knowledgeable and can even provide recommendations on the best ways to prepare your selection.

The meat counter is just as remarkable, offering premium cuts of beef, lamb, and poultry. The butchers are skilled and happy to assist with custom cuts or special requests. You can really taste the quality, whether you’re grilling a steak or slow-cooking a roast.

Beyond seafood and meat, the store boasts an excellent selection of specialty products, from gourmet cheeses to rare international ingredients. The variety ensures that you can find everything you need for a high-end meal at home.

Customer service is top-notch, with friendly and helpful staff always ready to assist. The store is clean, well-organized, and makes shopping a pleasant experience.

If quality and freshness are your priorities, this supermarket is a must-visit. Highly recommended!

What sealed the deal to never come back is calling today to see if I could get one small cheese platter and one small veggie platter for tomorrow (24 hour notice instead of 48). Amazon has made it that they have such a barebone crew schedule- and those that are there have no sense of Whole Food’s original service oriented business. With Target coming next door, and many other grocery stores within a small radius, there’s no reason to go to Whole Foods anymore. Such a shame, used to be great.

text.text:
I stopped into Whole Foods looking for something healthy to eat they have such a wide selection of fresh and healthy options. At first, I was leaning toward a salad, but then I saw the pizza and decided to give it a try since I love pizza, and honestly in New York you can’t really go wrong with it.

I grabbed a slice and it was pretty good cheesy, flavorful, and satisfying. It’s not your typical greasy slice; it had a fresher taste, and I liked the balance of toppings. Definitely a decent option when you’re hungry and want something quick.

What’s also nice is that Whole Foods has seating upstairs, so you can enjoy your food right there after shopping. Overall, I’d recommend trying their pizza. You can buy it by the slice or get a whole pie, and for a grocery store, it’s surprisingly solid.

I shop here for the vegan and organic options that are hard to find elsewhere. This is my neighborhood Whole Foods and it’s really disappointing to see how little they care about keeping the water fountains and bathrooms maintained and usable. Especially with the need for water this time of year. They just got a new fountain with a water bottle filler, but within the first couple days the filter status had a red light. They fixed that after about a week. But now, for several weeks, the water bottle filler has only been working very very slowly. It takes about 5-10x longer to fill a bottle than normal depending on the size, and I always feel rude because there’s always someone behind me waiting to fill theirs. Oh and the amount of bottles it says has been saved is going up normally so it thinks it’s dispensing more water than it is. The last time I used it it never stopped when I took the bottle away.
The part where you sip from stopped working at all a couple weeks ago. The water coming out has no pressure so it just goes down.

text.text:
Update on January 6th, 2025. There was a time when Whole Foods was a great store before Amazon owned it. Just returned from vacation and went to get some groceries. There was nothing on the shelves. This doesn’t happen at Trader Joe’s. They prepare before the store opens. It was so frustrating to shop there on a Monday morning, note to self not to do it again and to get to Trader Joe’s instead. When I asked for help locating some produce, the employee told me he didn’t know if they had any that he just got there and continued loading his lettuce, not interested in helping at all. He said there’s nothing on the shelves because yesterday was Sunday and busy! Really?
#TraderJoe’s please come to Jersey City!

No fresh pizza dough! Sold out by 3:00. In the past in NY and CA,  the pizza chef is happy to share the dough. Not here. Nothing in frozen either except cauliflower and almond crust. Only whole wheat in the bread section and nothing in front end. Now that owned by Amazon, service is down and unhelpful. #traderjoes we need you! Please come to Jersey city!
Update:
On Sunday June 8 and Monday June 9 there was so many bear shelves once again. Heard on the news that this was due to a cyber security attack on a distributor. No signs warning shoppers except on empty shelves. Have not heard a peep from Whole Foods.
Update Oct 6,
Need to ask food health services to check this WF out.
Yesterday all the lettuce was brown. It seems others before me had also been searching for fresh lettuce as they were strewn all over the place. Awhile back all the ice cream was half price because it was so soft. Such a disappointment.
See the bags of brown lettuce below .

text.text:
🌻 Unforgettable Service at Whole Foods—Thanks to Samantha!
I had the absolute pleasure of being helped by Samantha at the flower section inside Whole Foods, and I truly cannot say enough good things about her. From the moment I walked up hoping to find sunflowers for my sister—her favorite flower—Samantha greeted me with warmth and genuine care.
💐 Above and Beyond Service There was only one bouquet of sunflowers available, so I decided to get roses instead. While waiting for them to be wrapped, I asked Samantha if there were any more sunflowers. She kindly asked me to wait and said she’d check in the back. She magically returned with the most stunning sunflowers I’d ever seen—fresh, golden, and vibrant, like sunshine bundled into stems. She wrapped them with beautiful attention to detail, adding her own artistic touch to make them feel like a true gift.
😊 A Touch of Humanity and Knowledge With a cheerful smile, Samantha shared a little sunflower lore, including the fact that they’re the national flower of Ukraine—something I hadn’t known. That moment turned a simple purchase into a meaningful encounter. She didn’t just sell flowers—she offered joy, warmth, and a touch of culture all in one.
🌟 More Than a Transaction Samantha elevated the experience from routine to unforgettable. Her kindness and enthusiasm were contagious—leaving me with a huge smile and attracting admiration wherever I went with the sunflowers.
If you ever find yourself near the flower counter at Whole Foods and Samantha’s there, trust me: you're in for more than just a bouquet. You're in for a moment of grace, beauty, and genuine human connection.
Thank you, Samantha, for turning a simple errand into a lasting memory. 🌻✨
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Revisited with Hope to Upgrade My Review — Unfortunately, Things Got Worse

I came back to Whole Foods Tribeca hoping to update my last review and give the store a better rating — as 99% of my reviews are positive. Sadly, what I witnessed made that impossible.

A known bottle and can collector, carrying two filthy bags filled with recyclables, was seen stealing what appeared to be hundreds of dollars in vitamins. He then made his way to the salad bar, where the dirty cans repeatedly brushed against the food. Shockingly, security watched and did nothing. I informed customer service, who also failed to act.

As customers, we deserve clean, healthy food and a basic standard of hygiene. This experience was unacceptable, and I will never return to the Tribeca Whole Foods salad bar again.

Please see the attached photos.

Complaint about today’s incident (2:39 PM)

I purchased three flowers and had the receipt with me. Despite this, a security guard stopped me and accused me of not paying. I immediately showed him my receipt, my Whole Foods membership account transaction, and even the bank transaction proving the purchase.

I don’t know the name of the guard, but the interaction felt biased and disrespectful. I want to make a formal complaint so this does not happen to other customers.

From the moment you walk in, you’re greeted with a clean, well-organized store and an incredible variety of organic produce, responsibly sourced meats, and specialty products that cater to every dietary need.

What truly makes Whole Foods Market shine is their commitment to sustainability, local sourcing, and high food standards. It’s a place you can trust for both everyday essentials and gourmet finds.

Highly recommended for anyone who values quality, health-conscious options, and a superior grocery shopping experience.

text.text:
It’s positive that the store offers quality organic products, and I recommend it for your shopping. However, it would be preferable if it didn’t focus exclusively on promoting its own products, thereby limiting consumer choices. Variety and availability of different products are important for a comprehensive shopping experience.

Recently, Whole Foods has shifted its focus to promoting only its own products, such as chicken and eggs. While supporting local produce is commendable, I noticed that the highest quality items are placed on the top shelves, making them difficult to reach. Additionally, some premium products are tucked away at the back of the shelves, making them less visible to customers. This arrangement can be inconvenient for shoppers seeking the best organic options. It would be beneficial if the store reconsidered its product placement strategy to enhance accessibility and visibility for all customers.

I also concern regarding Amazon Prime’s exclusive discounts being primarily available on their own branded products, which can feel restrictive and unfair if you prefer other brands. While Amazon does offer discounts on a variety of products, many of the significant promotions, especially during events like Prime Day, often highlight Amazon’s own items or those from select partners. This practice can limit choices for consumers who are not interested in these specific products. It’s important for retailers to provide a diverse range of discounted items to cater to all customer preferences.

text.text:
Debra’s Natural Gourmet is a hidden gem in West Concord. You come here if you are in need of stuff you cannot find at Whole Foods or a similar store. You can tell the love and passion of the people that work here. The store is known for the wide selection of organic goods, deli, and food you can eat there or takeaway.

I was on a mission to find a very specific vegan butter. Instead of winging it and going to the store (which would have been going to my fourth store to find this butter), I called and asked if they had it in stock. Fortunately, it was! Once I got in the store, an employee quickly assisted me and shared that it was a fantastic butter indeed. Upon walking through the rest of the store, there’s plenty of Walden Co. Meats, various organic fresh and canned vegetables, cheeses, and other grocery items.

Debra’s also has an assortment of vitamins, supplements, and prepared food. I would love to come here for lunch one day and check out the rest of the store!! She also hosts a variety of different events, such as making your own face cream, book discussion, and making bath bombs. If you also follow their Facebook page, you’ll get a heads up on Epic three day sales from Friday to Sunday.

text.text:
Dear Co-Op Management,

I am writing to express my deep disappointment with the treatment I received at your Hanover location today.

My husband and I were purchasing beer, and while he presented his U.S. driver’s license, I showed my valid Kazakhstani national ID, which includes an English translation and clearly states my date of birth. I am 26 years old, and I have never had issues using this ID elsewhere in the United States.

However, the cashier refused to accept my ID without any clear explanation. What made the experience especially upsetting was that she proceeded to address my husband instead of me — apologizing to him for “not wanting to lose her job because of us.” I was completely ignored during the interaction, as if I were not part of the conversation or not a full person.

This behavior felt humiliating, disrespectful, and discriminatory. I understand that employees must follow rules when verifying age for alcohol purchases, but this was not about the policy — it was about the attitude and the way I, as a foreign customer, was made to feel unwelcome.

I would like to know:
•	What forms of foreign ID are officially accepted at your stores?
•	How do you train your employees to handle situations involving international customers?

I hope you take this complaint seriously and review both your policies and employee conduct. I am open to further discussion if needed.

Sincerely,
Dameli

UPDATE: this is why you need to do something about the flies in your baked goods cabinets... When flies land on food, they regurgitates digestive juices to liquefy the food into a liquid it can slurp up. They transmit microorganisms and pathogens from the waste and filth they've been on, potentially spreading diseases! Please stop making excuses and fix this!

While I’ve always found this place overpriced — even more than some spots in Midtown Manhattan — I’ve kept coming back because of the commitment to organic products, the community vibe, and the local sourcing, but I can no longer overlook an issue I’ve noticed (and mentioned) for a couple of years now.

The front baked goods display with croissants, cinnamon rolls, and other pastries is consistently covered in flies. Swarms. Crawling all over uncovered food. It’s not just unsanitary it’s a health hazard and it’s impossible to believe management isn’t aware, as it’s visible every time I visit.

This is a great place with great potential, but something is clearly being ignored. I honestly wonder if the health department has ever inspected this area.

Hawthorne Valley Farm Store: Please fix this. It’s unacceptable.

text.text:
The co-op is a wonderful place, but not a perfect place for everyone. They will admit that their prices are somewhat higher because the experience is better. There are some things that co-op does that they do better or only they do, there are some things that they are not as good at.

The produce is generally wonderful although a bit more expensive. Much of it is organic and much of it is local. The bulk section is like no other.  I’ve heard it said that it is the largest section like this in the northeast and I would not have trouble believing it. The assortment of nuts, trail mix, dried fruit, spices, maple syrup, etc., etc. that you can buy or as much or as little as you want is huge. It is hard to find a cheese section in the capitalist district with as much variety, or with the kind of service that will cut as much as as little as you want and they are extremely knowledgeable about cheese. The bakery is one of the few fully vegan bakeries in the capital District. They prepare wonderful meals and have a hot and cold salad and prepared food bar with a couple of different soups every day. there is just so much here that you won’t find in the price choppers and Hannaford‘s of the world. And, you do pay a bit more for it. The sale items tend to be really good on gourmet products. There is also a wonderful vibe with customers who will routinely say hello, let you go in front of them with your cart and the staff in general seems happy to be here. If you join for $100 you get a discount and if you work you get an increasing discount. Oh, and I didn’t mention all of the plantsin the nice weather. I can go on, but the co-op is more than just a grocery store it’s an experience.

People mention “hippies”, a “cult” and similar terms. No value judgement but a large part of the mission of the coop is to embrace inclusiveness of all….to embrace diversity and to promote social causes. The mission is also strongly supportive of respect and restoration of the environment, and this may attract shoppers and workers who are a subset of the population at large.

text.text:
I came in, one side is a small limited marked with wonder niche drinks and other such items, as well as fruit and vegetables, and the other side is a lovely restaurant and study space.  I loved the vibe felt so relaxing on the Market side. The restaurant ordering, she acted like I was lucky she took time out her busy day. But since she told me something was old, I thought, great she did me a solid, so maybe she is just tired. Then I heard the kitchen staff talking too. A bunch of hostile folks for no reason whatsoever! I bought my drinks on the market side, because it was cheaper that way.

I know, it was a Friday, and the week is long, but why you mad at me for ordering food? That is what this establishment is designed for. So my first thought was:
1. This food was not made with love. It will likely not be good.
I hate when I am right about things like this.

When somehow the spices are not ground fine enough, so one of your bowls you feel like you are eating gritty sand the entire meal that has the occasional flavor of beef and ginger, and lentils so salty I could not choke them down without rice, and even then could not eat them, that is how you know, maybe is not the hot spot after all. Where was all the flavor I read about? What is this grit?

My cabbage, jerk chicken, and rice were great. Everything else was a NO. I even included a side shot of the lentils left over I tried to mix with rice that I threw away.

VERDICT: Hit the Market and only get the jerk chicken, rice and cabbage from the other side. Godspeed on this one.

text.text: While visiting Maine, we had heard about this gluten-free brewery in Portland, and we were blown away about how cool it really was in person. We came on a Friday afternoon, and there was a band playing, and the atmosphere was just very relaxed and happy. We enjoyed sitting outside and listening to the music and talking with others. As we left, we met the owner, Tom, and he thanked us for visiting, and also explained to us the mission of the brewery. We highly recommend visiting here, whether you are a gluten-free person or not. The beer is delicious and the people who work there are very friendly. We decided to come back the next day, and it was a slightly different atmosphere because it was a rainy day, but they opened up tables in the brewery room and it was very cozy and fun to listen to music again. We met the manager, Andie, and again a very friendly and personable staff member. Visiting from the Seattle area, we can’t wait to come again someday! We really had a wonderful time!!

text.text: I’ve shopped here as a non-member for over a year and took my time to review this space in order to give it a fair chance to impress or shift. The best part about this space: mini carts for your kids and a variety of selection when it comes to organic and natural items. The worst parts about this space: the products are insanely priced (if they want us to support local, they’re going to have to compete with Walgreens and Whole Foods at the VERY least), their bathroom is never cleaned, the farmer’s market (also local) is cheaper and has fresher product, and the employees have given me and my family some of the rudest (and most boring) customer service I’ve received in Portland. I do hope they change. I love what they care about but they go about it in what feels like all the wrong ways.

text.text: I've been shopping at Market 32 since the day they opened the new store. There are dandelion greens and many different types of kale!  One day when the fabulous radishes were not there, I spoke to a woman I thought was simply a pair of hands -- and she informed me that the radishes just were not up to snuff that week and she passed them by!  What a help that is!  I rarely go to the middle of the store – but the Produce, the Bakery, the Meat Department where you can find tomahawk steaks and grass fed beef, and the Fish department - where you can find things fresh and there's someone to talk to who can guide you to what's especially good --  it all makes a difference.   I wish the Price Chopper fellows had the courage to go all the way – but for the moment, what they're doing is so greatly appreciated!   And -- by the way -- there is someone packing your groceries while you're unpacking your cart.  The help is terrific.  And I thank them.  Overlook the fact that they're in a Wallmart Strip Mall -- and give them a try.  You'll be pleased you did.

Extremely Racist and Disrespectful Behavior from Employee Named Penny

I am writing this to bring attention to the unacceptable behavior I experienced at Market 32 in Torrington, specifically from an employee named Penny. As a Black woman and a mother, I was deeply hurt and humiliated by her actions and comments.

Penny was not only incredibly rude and condescending, but she also made blatantly racist and discriminatory remarks toward me and my children. She accused me of shoplifting without any cause or evidence, made derogatory comments about my use of an EBT card, and looked down on me for simply shopping and feeding my family. The racial slurs and overall hateful tone were beyond offensive — they were traumatizing.

This kind of behavior should never be tolerated in any workplace, especially one that serves a diverse community. Market 32 needs to take immediate action to address this. I am requesting a formal apology and accountability from management, including proper diversity and sensitivity training, if not serious disciplinary action against this employee.

No one should be made to feel unwelcome or criminalized because of their race, their financial status, or how they pay for their groceries. I will not be returning until this issue is acknowledged and resolved appropriately.

text.text:
I had a very disappointing experience at the Market 32 bakery. Yesterday, I went to place an order for my son’s birthday cake, only to be told that no one from the bakery was available to take the order and that I should come back the next morning at 9 AM.

When I returned the next morning, the staff was extremely rude and dismissive. They told me they couldn’t take the order because they didn’t have enough staff to make the cake. Instead of showing any concern, they were laughing about the situation, which was very unprofessional—especially since my son was standing right there with me.

Because of this, I had no time to arrange a cake elsewhere, and it ruined what should have been a special moment for my child. My kids always loved cakes from Market 32, but this experience broke their hearts and completely shattered my trust in this bakery.

Going forward, I will never order cakes here again. Very disappointing and unacceptable service.

text.text: This review is strictly regarding their pre-made sandwiches and other prepared foods.  First off, their baked goods are excellent.  The grocery selection is good.  I have no criticisms of those area of the business.  However, with respect to their sandiwches, they are poorly constructed and have very little meat.  It's basically all bread with a thin slice of meat.  Honestly, for the price charged, it's shameful.  Zero value for the sandwich and I would never recommend anyone buy a sandwich from here.  Frankly (and sadly), Hannafords produces a better sandwich than Rosemont.  The prepared foods are terrible as well.  We paid $63.00 for food that wasn't worth more than $15 in my mind.  We got Korean meatballs tasted like they were rolled in salt.  My God was it ever overly salted.  It was absolutely terrible.  If you want excellent baked goods and groceries, give them a shot.  If you want prepared foods and sandwiches, steer clear from Rosemont.

I'm betting things would change rather quickly.

text.text:
This is a good store overall, and I like shopping here.  I find the produce is usually in real good shape.  I’m always buying strawberries, bananas etc.  here with no problems.
Healthy food:  There is a department here for the health conscious that includes protein, gluten free and dairy free.  Pretty good variety.
Frozen foods: Ice cream, vegetables etc. These are usually well stocked, but the only complaint I’ve had with this is that sometimes the ice cream from certain vendors is left too long on the shelf, and when I get home and open it; there’s ice frost on top.  There’s not a problem bringing it back, but I’d rather not have too.
Express registers: Are good here, and there always seems to be an open register. That’s really appreciated.  Be careful when you take your receipt though, because when you pull on the receipt to get it out of the machine, if you pull it too fast the door where the roll is kept falls open. I’m aware of it now, so I just don’t pull it too fast.  This is the only store where I’ve seen that happen.
There’s one or two young cashiers that oversee the express registers, that just don’t get the concept of customer service.  Instead you get the impression, that they can’t wait to get out of there, and your holding them up.  I blame management more for that, because they should be able to tell who wants to do that job and who doesn’t.  I’m sure there are other jobs in the store that they would be better at.    I don’t want to paint them all with a broad brush, because there are some good caring ones there also.
Citizens bank inside: People in this bank are very friendly and willing to help.
Parking: Tight at times but manageable

text.text:
I rarely find myself shopping at Stop & Shop in Kingston, primarily because their prices consistently lean higher than most other grocery stores in the area – perhaps with the sole exception of the Big Y right down the street. Still, I recently popped in to grab a few non-perishables while I was waiting for another local business to open its doors.

The self-checkout experience, true to form, felt like an obstacle course. It always seems to drag on and be unnecessarily complicated. In my growing frustration with the machine, I definitely let out a grumble (or two!). To my surprise, a staff member who was nearby swooped in to help. I genuinely can't say enough good things about her. She was incredibly pleasant, patient, and even had a fantastic sense of humor, which definitely helped defuse my annoyance with my own fumbling at the machine.

The people working at this Stop & Shop are genuinely a highlight, and I want to make sure that's clear. However, despite their excellent customer service, the consistently steeper prices and the clunky self-checkout process mean it's unlikely to become my regular grocery stop.

I understand some of the staff are also minorities, and that makes me wonder how they’re being treated by management  as well. If they treat customers like me this way, I can only imagine what happens behind the scenes.

I’ve been shopping at Stop & Shop for three years, but I can’t continue supporting a store where I’m treated like a threat when I’ve done nothing wrong. I also understand is 2025 and everything is about race bla bla bla, but shopping is crazy. If someone is going to steal common sense, the machine flags and camera are installed inside.

text.text:
I needed to order 4 dozen cupcakes for my daughter’s birthday, which was scheduled 48 hours from when I called the Stop & Shop bakery. I spoke with Shelsey at 5:06 PM for about 4 minutes, and she was very helpful in explaining the ordering process, including allergen information. I asked if I could come in the following day (Thursday) after work around 6 PM. She informed me the bakery closed at 7 PM and said it would be fine as long as I arrived before then.
Since I work an hour and 25 minutes away, I left work two hours early to make it on time. I arrived at the store at 5:45 PM, only to be met by a man named John, who rudely shouted that there was "no way" he could make the cupcakes for the next day. I explained I had already spoken with Shelsey, but he was dismissive.
I then asked to speak with the manager, Gail, who showed no concern for my situation. She simply told me there was nothing they could do and offered a flat “sorry.” I was left extremely disappointed and frustrated after making every effort to follow instructions and accommodate the bakery’s timeline.
Fortunately, the Stop & Shop in Southbury was able to accept and successfully fulfill my cupcake order.

text.text:
Be prepared to be judged, incorrectly and with no ability to defend yourself, based on your purchases by the staff.

As I was checking out today the bagger saw the word 'India' on a beer and told me that I 'was what was wrong with America', by 'buying foreign beers from India'.

I attempted to point out that it was an India pale ale style beer produced by New England Brewing, which is based in Connecticut. The words 'New England' were prominently featured on the top of the can.

The bagger actively ignored me, turning away from me while muttering under his breath that I 'was what was wrong with America.' While he was an older man (my guess in his mid to late 70s), he certainly could hear me as we had talked earlier in the checkout process.

All he saw was a 30-something-year-old man buying what he thought was a foreign beer, and shut off all information about the outside world while judging me on false information. I literally walked around him to make eye contact while trying to point out what I thought might be an honest mistake on his part. He completely ignored me, and continued to talk about 'India beers' and 'the problems with America'.

He made no comment on the Heineken I also purchased (I guess that was less offensive to this man than supposed 'India beer' being sold in the US).

That this happened all in front of my 5 year old son was even worse. He was then asking me what we did wrong. I got the opportunity to talk with him about how a problem in our country is people like that man instantly judging people based on false information and refusing to listen to facts. So at least there was that silver lining.

He completely ignored me, and continued to talk about 'India beers' and 'the problems with America'.

He made no comment on the Heineken I also purchased (I guess that was less offensive to this man than supposed 'India beer' being sold in the US).

That this happened all in front of my 5 year old son was even worse. He was then asking me what we did wrong. I got the opportunity to talk with him about how a problem in our country is people like that man instantly judging people based on false information and refusing to listen to facts. So at least there was that silver lining.

“The Matrix Is Everywhere.”
-Morpheus, The Matrix. (1999)

Stop & Shop is a regional chain of supermarkets that operate in the northeastern United States. They have over 400 stores located in New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Massachusetts. The Stop & Shop located at 855 Bridgeport Ave. in Milford, CT is one of those stores.

This Stop & Shop offers a variety of food choices at competitive prices. In particular, there is a brand of strawberry frosted cupcakes that my wife really likes, but they sell much more than just strawberry frosted cupcakes. Overall I would say that Stop & Shop offers the equivalent grocery shopping experience you would find at the other major grocery stores in the area such as Big Y and Shop Rite.

But that’s not what I’m here to write a review about…

My purpose is to write a satirical opinion of the robotic abomination known as Marty. Please be seated.

The Blue Pill:

Marty is an autonomous robot that is employed by Stop & Shop to report spills, debris and other hazards so customers may enjoy a clean and safe space to shop for groceries.

Using its imaging technology, Marty can also detect product availability and notify store associates when an item needs to be re-stocked or is misplaced. This helps customers have aesthetically pleasing choices when shopping and do not have to be inconvenienced with items that are not in their assigned places. This also allows the store associates to spend more time with the customers to ensure an outstanding shopping experience.

The Red Pill:

Marty could be one of many robotic machines created by an architect that may be able to manipulate people into believing that a utopian grocery shopping experience exists.

Although the origins of Marty is known, its ancient predecessors may have been a more sinister collection of machines that were instrumental in the last large extinction event here on Earth and led to the destruction of the natural grocery shopping environment. Marty’s predecessors may also have been who actually built the pyramids.

Although Marty seems to be programmed to learn from its environment and adapt to changing situations, there may also be a possibility that Marty is controlled by an architect to maintain the mirage of a grocery shopping experience and deal with any anomalies that may arise, such as satirical Google review writers.

The choice is yours:

Take the blue pill and enjoy the delicious strawberry frosted cupcakes.

Take the red pill and come to understand what may be happening outside the illusion that Marty helps control.

Morpheus; if you’re out there, please help us free our minds.

text.text:
Lately, I've been observing that my trips to the market can get a bit busy, especially at the checkout. Sometimes, while I’m trying to pack my groceries, the cashier moves on to the next customer's items before I'm finished. It can feel a little rushed, and I do miss the days when cashiers would lend a hand with packing, which I found really nice.

I’ve noticed that the person behind me often stands pretty close, which can make it tricky to collect my change and put my money away. There seems to be a bit of stress in these situations for both customers and staff.

It’s fascinating how being in crowded places can sometimes lead to moments of rudeness. With the rising cost of living and service challenges, it’s understandable that people might feel overwhelmed and react in ways they don’t intend to. I imagine staff also feel the pressure from their jobs, which can influence how they interact with customers.

As a retiree who loves my regular trips to the market, I’ve become more aware of these dynamics. Sometimes the markets can feel a bit cluttered, and I've noticed expired items on the shelves, which adds to the experience. I believe everyone has their moments, and if we all take a little extra time to be kind, both customers and staff can create a more enjoyable shopping environment together.

I do wish that customers would give a little more space and let me finish paying and packing my groceries. It would make the experience so much smoother for all of us!

The people who work here are always great but since they were bought out by Amazon they have lost their homey, grass roots "Whole" foods feel and have become more corporate.

I have a severe dairy allergy and I used to be able to stop in and find more vegan baked goods as well as goods from local bakeries thay sold their items through the store, as well as stop in at the Cafe and get a freshly made coffee. Now their bakery has only Blueberry vegan scones,  and only a basic variety of baked goods you find anywhere with not many vegan options.

I went in the other day to grab a coffe only to find out they now o ly have coffee machines with no, non dairy options. As someone who has struggled to find non dairy options and this had been my first store I could rely on for options as I navigated this allergy I  both sad and disappointed to see this store gear more toward a more basic grocery, rather than a niche place.

text.text:
I'm writing this review filled with mixed emotions. The cereal aisle had this weird mix of aromas. It smelled like orange peels that were left in a musty attic.  Not sure how, but there appeared to be pieces of pink ceiling insulation scattered in the aisle too.  I thought that was a little odd.  I will say they have a great selection of protein bars. However, please use caution in that section as one of the shelves is actually just held up by a can of taco sauce.

The best time to shop is in the morning when the case count is fresh. The only positive thing about this review was the conversation I had with the only person working in the aisles. Does a phenomenal Lloyd Christmas impression. They were so kind and super informative about the water aisle.  We eventually got to talking about rollerblading and indoor bird photography, even their mom's favorite cooked supper - spachcock.

Worth noting - best cornbread around. The person responsible for baking the cornbread deserves a raise.

text.text:
I recently visited the Whole Foods in Boston (Cambridge Street / downtown area) and I have mixed but mostly positive impressions. The first thing you notice is variety — they carry a wide array of organic produce, specialty items, bulk goods, artisanal cheeses, and a solid selection of prepared foods and grab-and-go meals. The prepared food / salad / hot bar area is especially handy if you want a quick, healthier option. (Though, side note: I learned Whole Foods doesn’t always prepare all their hot / cold bar items in store — many are made at third-party kitchens and delivered to the store.¹)

The layout is decent, though in peak hours things can feel a bit cramped, especially near the deli / bakery section. Some aisles shrink when carts pass through, and the checkout area can get congested, but staff generally seem to handle the flow well. The cleanliness is good overall, though I noticed surfaces and bins in the prepared food zone could use more attention during rush times.

Staff interactions were a highlight. Most employees I encountered were friendly, helpful, and knowledgeable when I asked about specialty items or replacements. That said, I did catch a few distracted or less engaged workers — likely tied to busy shifts. The value side is trickier: you pay a premium in many places compared to more standard supermarkets. Some specialty or organic items feel overpriced relative to nearby options, but you're paying for selection, quality, and convenience.

As for consistency, that’s where the store stumbles occasionally. On one visit, I ordered a hot meal that arrived lukewarm, and a salad bar container was missing a topping I requested. Also, inventory can ebb — I walked by empty spots in the bulk bins and some niche items were out of stock. The bakery is a nice touch — their breads and pastries smell fresh, though I’d be cautious about freshness late in the day.

Overall, if you want a one-stop for high quality, interesting, healthy grocery options, this Boston Whole Foods is a solid choice. Just be ready to spend a little more, and visit earlier in the day if you want the full selection.

The areas appeared orderly and clean. There weren't any offending smells of significance noted at the time. I walked and observed while my spouse shopped for what was needed for the trip. This is her favorite store to shop.

text.text: I've been coming to this location for over 3 years now and compared to the other locations, this one is expansive and offer more variety of products. Initially the hot and cold bar used to be good but the quality has dropped. I started seeing for example the chicken tenders look really dark which means they don't change the oil as much anymore and the cold bar's saseme tofu tasted spoiled. They don't have any dates on the cold bar items and I always feel they looked old. The premade items also look like they were sitting there for a while. They definitely need to do some quality checks on the ready to eat products. The produce are usually not bad but one time I saw mold on organic carrots and told the person who was stocking it and he just wiped it and put it back. Also I had bad experience with the red meat. I bought packaged steaks and the expiration date was ok but as soon as I opened the bag, I could tell that the meat was not fresh and it had old odor, they refunded me but gave me a look before they did. The fish are not the freshest either. For some reason, they don't remove the scale of the fish and I've tried their salmon few times and they always have a little bit old fish smell. The pastry section seems fresh but it's not. The cakes and bite sized desserts just sit there for days, specially not the popular ones. Probably the only thing that moves fast is the fresh breads. All in all I used to buy everything from here and get excited to go here but I started seeing some issues and the employees don't seem to care much. These days I only go there to get 4 items: organic low fat yogurt, organic chicken, avocados and toilet papers.

text.text:
Whole Foods in Portland? Ayuh, it’s wicked good! The place is clean, organized, and has just about everything you could ask for. The produce? Fresh as can be, like it came straight outta the garden this morning. And the seafood? Well, you know they’ve got some top-notch, sustainable options—only the best here in Maine.

What I really like is they’ve got plenty of local stuff. You’ll find Maine-made goodies all over the store, from jams to craft beers. Makes you feel good knowing they’re supporting local folks.

The staff? Real friendly, always willing to help you find what you need or answer any questions. Feels like they actually care, which is hard to come by sometimes. The prepared foods section is a lifesaver, too—perfect for grabbing something quick but still healthy and tasty.

Parking’s easy, and even when it’s busy, they keep things moving along pretty well. If you’re in the area and need good food and great options, this Whole Foods is the real deal. Highly recommend!

Fresh as can be, like it came straight outta the garden this morning. And the seafood? Well, you know they’ve got some top-notch, sustainable options—only the best here in Maine.

What I really like is they’ve got plenty of local stuff. You’ll find Maine-made goodies all over the store, from jams to craft beers. Makes you feel good knowing they’re supporting local folks.

The staff? Real friendly, always willing to help you find what you need or answer any questions. Feels like they actually care, which is hard to come by sometimes. The prepared foods section is a lifesaver, too—perfect for grabbing something quick but still healthy and tasty.

Parking’s easy, and even when it’s busy, they keep things moving along pretty well. If you’re in the area and need good food and great options, this Whole Foods is the real deal. Highly recommend!

text.text:
I’m not really one to write reviews, but the experience of my last few visits here is worth calling out for other’s attention.

I can look past the occasional passive-aggressiveness in the tone at the “customer service” desk when I go around to ask when the coffee bar will open (when it is very often closed during its supposed operating hours).. but a couple of employees that work at the checkout counter make me not want to go to the store again. I actively try and avoid the counters that they run.

One employee must absolutely HATE working at the counter, because every item that they check out is done with rolled eyes and loud sighs, after which they get thrown across the belt. Items get taken out of the paper bags they are in, and are dealt with so forcefully that either the bags get torn, or the item is no longer in the bag. We chalked it off to someone having a bad day the first time, but she has done it every single time! I’m sorry you hate being there, but don’t take it out on my bagged vegetables.

Second employee ran all the items that we
placed on the belt, and then just let it stack up on the other side. When there wasn’t any more space to put the scanned stuff, she kept stacking them up to the point that items started rolling off. One of our sweet potatoes got to rest on the cold Whole Foods floor for a few seconds before it got PUT BACK ON TOP OF THAT PILE again. She showed no interest in bagging (which is fine, I can do it, but could you please communicate that politely?), and then just stared at us when we asked if she could scan the Amazon code on our phone. She proceeded to just watch us bag the 20-25 items we purchased and offered zero help. When she saw that we were done to our last 5 or so items, she decided to take the next customer in line. Not a word, not a hand to help us. Thanks for that!

I’m not asking for anything here besides requesting that the store talk to its employees. Meanwhile, I’ll keep avoiding these two, and I wish the people that end up in their counters the very best of luck.

Review for Denisse – Whole Foods Customer Service Superstar

I recently had the pleasure of visiting Whole Foods, where I was assisted by an extraordinary employee named Denisse. Her exceptional professionalism and attention to detail truly stood out during my shopping experience, making a significant impact on my overall enjoyment and satisfaction.

Her genuine approach to customer service set the tone for the rest of my visit. Denisse's ability to anticipate my needs and provide tailored assistance was akin to a seasoned professional, ensuring that my shopping experience was seamless and efficient. Her knowledge about the products was impressive, and she took the time to explain the benefits of the items, which was incredibly helpful.

Denisse's attention to detail was evident in everything she did. Whether it was recommending complementary products, or addressing any concerns I had, her meticulous approach left no room for error. I felt confident in her guidance and appreciated her thoroughness in ensuring that my questions were answered and my needs met.

While interacting with Denisse, it became clear to me that her skills are underutilized in her current position. She possesses a natural talent for leadership and an ability to inspire those around her. Her calm demeanor, coupled with exceptional organizational skills, would undoubtedly make her a valuable asset in a managerial role.

I couldn't help but compare her to another impressive employee I encountered at the 96th Street Branch, who ultimately turned out to be the store manager lol. Both share a remarkable commitment to excellence and customer service, yet Denisse brought an additional warmth and personalized touch that I believe would thrive in a leadership position. Her potential for growth within Whole Foods is undeniable, and it would be a tremendous loss not to recognize and develop her capabilities further.

Considering Denisse's outstanding capabilities and the positive impact she has on customers, I strongly recommend that she be considered for a promotion. Elevating her to a managerial role would not only harness her skills for a greater purpose but also enhance the overall shopping experience for all customers lucky enough to cross paths with her. Whole Foods has the opportunity to further cultivate an exceptional employee in Denisse, and I am confident she would excel and continue to exceed expectations in a leadership capacity.

In summary, Denisse is a customer service star who should not go unnoticed. Her professionalism, attention to detail, and potential for a managerial role make her an indispensable asset to Whole Foods. Her dedication to providing an outstanding shopping experience deserves recognition and reward, and I urge Whole Foods to consider her for well-deserved career advancement.

FOOD SAFETY ISSUE, BRUSHED OFF TWICE.

I’m genuinely glad there’s a new Whole Foods Daily Shop in the neighborhood. It’s well-maintained, convenient, and has a great selection. I’ve shopped there many times and wanted to see it succeed.

But today, I noticed the potatoes looked visibly green - even before checking out, I flagged it to a staff member. I was told “it’s edible” and brushed off.

When I got home and peeled both potatoes I purchased, I saw the green went deep under the skin, which, as anyone with basic food safety knowledge knows, can indicate high levels of solanine, a toxic compound. That’s not safe, especially if you’re serving this to kids, elderly family members, or anyone with health sensitivities.

I went back and raised the concern with the manager. He refused to apologize for the negligence, claimed he “wasn’t familiar with that fact” and needed to “check,” yet in the same breath offered to start covering the potatoes to reduce light exposure. That contradiction alone tells me he wasn’t being straight with me.

I also asked what the plan was for training staff, so they stop casually dismissing legitimate concerns by telling customers food is “edible” when it clearly may not be. He made it clear that staff training is his thing, and the tone implied I had no right to raise that question - even though the staff gave misinformation and clearly needs better guidance.

This isn’t about the $1.50. It’s about how both staff and management dismissed a clear food safety issue with zero accountability. I expected better - especially from a store that positions itself as a standard-bearer for quality. Very disappointed in how they handled this, and how little concern they showed for customer safety.

When I got home and peeled both potatoes I purchased, I saw the green went deep under the skin, which, as anyone with basic food safety knowledge knows, can indicate high levels of solanine, a toxic compound. That’s not safe, especially if you’re serving this to kids, elderly family members, or anyone with health sensitivities.

I went back and raised the concern with the manager. He refused to apologize for the negligence, claimed he “wasn’t familiar with that fact” and needed to “check,” yet in the same breath offered to start covering the potatoes to reduce light exposure. That contradiction alone tells me he wasn’t being straight with me.

I also asked what the plan was for training staff, so they stop casually dismissing legitimate concerns by telling customers food is “edible” when it clearly may not be. He made it clear that staff training is his thing, and the tone implied I had no right to raise that question - even though the staff gave misinformation and clearly needs better guidance.

This isn’t about the $1.50. It’s about how both staff and management dismissed a clear food safety issue with zero accountability. I expected better - especially from a store that positions itself as a standard-bearer for quality. Very disappointed in how they handled this, and how little concern they showed for customer safety.

text.text: This Whole Foods location in Glastonbury is the worst one in the area and possibly anywhere.  It feels that if you physically go there to shop, you're always competing against the Whole Food/Amazon workers filling the online orders.  There appears to be at least two to three of them running up and down every aisle almost all day.  This usually will result in many products not being available on the shelves as compared to the other stores. And this really annoy the walk in customers that take the time and effort to physcially go to the store! This store's location is too small (and with the aisles being too narrow) to accomodate these online orders!! If they really want to fill the online orders, do it offsite at  one of the many Whole Foods/Amazon warhouses that seems to be everywhere, not in the physical Whole Foods store!  Also, this location's prepared food section is very weak in terms of the offerings and variety and is somewhat lacking, especially the hot foods, as compared to the other locations such as Avon, South Windsor, etc. It goes to show that it appears that they don't put that much focus in this area probably because they're so focused on the online orders.  And you used to be able to eat in this beautful area where it has nice big windows with a coffee bar right the middle along with some other wonderful take out offerings but no more. Again this area was taken over by the need to fill the online orders with many fridges, freezers, etc. If this Glastonbury location really wants to be a "neighborhood" store, then move the online orders offsite to one the warehouses and bring back the beautiful and spacious eat in area.

text.text:
Whole Foods was founded in 1978 and has over 500 locations; its parent company is Amazon as of 2017 and it is headquartered in Texas. It is known for its organic selections and selling products free from preservatives, hydrogenated fats, artificial flavors, and colors.

This location in Avon is fairly new. It's located in the Avon Village Center. The parking lot is big but very busy. The store was large and organized. I purchased some cookies, a sushi roll, and some single serve beers. I found the beers at the end of an aisle and the prices ranged from .99 cents to $2.99. The prices were higher than other grocery stores because of their organic food model. It's not my usual grocery store I shop at because I am budget conscious; it's a once in a while place to shop for me. I do understand why people shop there weekly, because of the quality ingredients.

Make sure you watch the screen closely when you check out with a cashier. I deducted one star because she scanned an extra item. I normally would use self checkouts but I had some cookies from the bakery I wanted make sure was inputted correctly. Now I know to just use the self checkouts next time I go. Other that, it was a decent shopping experience.

text.text:
I would have given this store five stars since I have been coming to this one since I moved to the Simsbury area about 3 months ago.
I find the store vastly better than my old hometown Whole Foods Market which was in Milford.
But today my experience was much different and more difficult then I would have ever expected. I was actually really astounded. I am all for giving people chances for employment and if you're here legally then okay.
However, I needed something particular and didn't know where in the store to find it.
So I approached a woman sweeping the floor in produce and I said excuse me and she didn't look up, so I got a little closer and politely said pardon me, and she turns and looks at me and says "I no speak English"
I was a little put off by the fact that they had nobody there with her to help her with these type of instances, but I looked past it and went to find someone else.
I see a woman pushing a cart out of an aisle going into the double doors into the back so I stopped her. I asked her where I could find what I was looking for, and she looked at me like she didn't understand what I was saying. She beckons me to follow her and speaks in a foreign language to another guy who in turn asks me in broken English what I'm looking for. So I tell him and he just couldn't grasp what I'm asking for. So he then brings me to another person who is working putting stock away that amazingly understood English and told me where I needed to go to find what I was looking for.
I continue along my way and I go down towards the prepared food section and they normally have two different size boxes to put prepped food in, but I didn't see the smaller size boxes. There was a girl walking by me and I asked her if they have the smaller boxes and she looks at me and shrugs her shoulders and shakes her head. So I asked her again and again she shakes her head and this time tells me she doesn't understand english!!

I'm sorry, and maybe I am a jerk for this, but if you don't know how to speak the language and management is not willing to put somebody right next to these people until they know enough to get by, then you should not be hiring them.
I will probably continue going there because I just like Whole Foods products, but I was really put off by that today and it's really bothering me.

text.text:
This morning, when I was picking strawberries here, there were only three boxes of Sweetest Batch available, and one of them was in an employee’s hand. The box she had was larger and of better quality compared to the other two remaining boxes. I thought I would wait and see if she didn’t need it so I could purchase it. During this time, I noticed she was repeatedly trying to close the cardboard box. Why was she closing the box?

Did she open the box to pick out the largest strawberries and combine them into one box, leaving the less desirable ones behind? I love strawberries and buy them every day, but I never open the box to pick and choose. I only inspect the box from the outside to make sure there are no bad strawberries.

As a Whole Foods employee, they may have priority over regular customers, but if they are opening boxes to select the best strawberries and leaving behind the less desirable ones, isn’t that unfair to us regular shoppers? We are paying the same price, but the quality is different! This is something I find very hard to accept.

Does this mean that in the future, I can also open the fruit boxes and combine all the best ones into a single box? I don’t believe this should be acceptable, but if your employees are doing this, I wouldn’t mind doing it as well!

Dear Whole Foods Team,

On July 31st, I purchased a medium container of New English Seafood Cheddar Soup from your store. Upon tasting it for the first bite, I noticed a sour flavor. Initially, I assumed it might be due to the ingredients, perhaps an intentional use of vinegar, given Whole Foods’ strong reputation for quality.

However, I began experiencing stomach discomfort and diarrhea today as of Aug 1, 2025. While there has been no severe physical harm, I believe the quality of this soup does not align with the standards associated with your brand.

I have retained the receipt with the purchase date clearly visible and have taken a photo as proof of purchase. I hope this issue can be looked into and addressed appropriately.

Thank you for your attention

text.text: Been visiting this place for almost 8 to 10 years. The food quality in salad bar and pizza corner since 2022 has gone down the drain. The hygiene is extremely questionable with cooks in pizza place not even changing gloves between handling pizza and their phones or touching hair & face or wiping sweat. Several items in salad bar are stale. Twice in a row, I got bad stomach within minutes. Several items seem overnight or from previous day, not fresh. I tried to give feedback on WFM link on the receipt but it takes to some weird site. There are no considerations to change gloves when handling meats versus veggies for toppings. They use the same slicer to cut meats pizza and veggies pizza, making it unpalatable for vegetarians. Too much cross contamination. Lastly, in the past 2 years or so, the shopping experience looks like something similar to Walmart on Thanksgiving. Staff running around like headless chickens to pack orders without consideration for those who made the trip to the store. They rush in all directions looking at screens & lack basic manners of saying excuse me, please or even sorry when they bang into you. I have just not seen such pathetic environment and poor food quality at any place with such prices, least of all Whole Foods.

text.text: Ordered my wedding flowers from this location. We ordered bouquets and boutonnières. When discussing on the phone to place the order we agreed the bridesmaids bouquets would have 11 roses and the bridal bouquet would have 30. Not only did the bouquets not have the correct amount of flowers (bridesmaids had 7 roses, bridal had 12), but they also did not cut the stems at all. The full length stems were wrapped in ribbon. My bridesmaids had to spend time unwrapping each bouquet and cutting all the stems. The boutonnières were sad looking as well with almost dead flowers. The only saving grace here was that we only spent $180. So if you don’t care what your flowers look like / if they’re correct and are only looking to save money this is a good option.

Busch's in Pinckney is an absolute gem and easily my favorite grocery store in the area! Every time I visit, I'm impressed by the freshness of their produce and the quality of their meat and seafood departments. It truly feels like a step above your average supermarket.

The store is always clean, well-organized, and has a fantastic selection of both everyday essentials and unique specialty items. The staff members are consistently friendly and helpful, always willing to assist.
