This Meijer is CHEAPER than Walmart. They have a full bakery section, women’s health section, sushi, cheese, and a solid Halloween section. The store decor  is very drab grey and kind of depressing. They have unique items that you can find at Ross, for (instance skull butter dishes, chocolate,)
but at better quality and prices. There are a few problems with the store: Something I hate about shopping at Meijer, is the fact that I  need a PIN number to get into my online coupons and savings. Just let me type in my phone number please. It’s easier to remember. The other problem that several people have with the store is the lack of traffic lights in the parking lot. They should have some sort of halt signal in the cross section near the entrance of the parking lot. Those of us who take the bus get trapped there and can’t move forward. Also, when are they going to install a staircase next to the bus stops? It’s extremely hard for the elderly customers to walk up and down the steep hill out front and still make their buses. Other than that, this is a decent store.

text.text: If I could give this store a Hero to ZERO score I most certainly would. When Meijer Stevensville opened I was elated!! The store layout was nice and made sense ..they usually had all the items I shopped for like probably 98% of the time. Staff seemed happy and friendly and you used to see the same faces and it just felt like a nice neighborhood grocer. But over the years you could see the employees "light in their eyes" go out. You could see them trying to struggle to smile and then the familiar faces started to disappear one by one (I learned they were fired by new managements that would come and go). Gradually my items (normal stuff like orange juice, cheese, hair spray or cleaners) that were popular items started consistently not being in stock. But Wow..recently, like this past month with the new "refresh" it's HORRIBLE! They went from the manageable layout of produce down on a level where shorter ppl (like me) or older ppl or handicap ppl could reach to pick out such items like lettuce, radishes, etc are now unreachable on a top shelf. Whoever designed and decided to completely makeover the way produce is presented needs fired! The produce looks awful stacked and crammed in to these tiny spaces. Wilted and rotting. So, why I wrote this review is to say I would rather drive to Kalamazoo (Trader Joe's) and Portage (Sam's Club) to do my grocery shopping than continue at the Meijer in Stevensville. It's so sad to see a store decline such as this one but bad management decisions have really ruined this once nice store. NOT AN IMPROVEMENT. (I have been going to Martin's in Stevensville for my deli needs and other things, more over the past couple of years anyway as I quit buying from the deli area of Meijer bc of the quality as well.) Shame on the upper management for such bad decisions. Who puts radishes and lettuces so high up? Ridiculous...

text.text:
I recently started shopping at Meijer , I switched from my local Jewel & Walmart. Since shopping here, I have always enjoyed the friendliness of all the employees, the hands on efforts to assist with customers, the prices, the freshness of the produce & my favorite is the meat section.
Upon my last visit, I was greeted by the most rude cashier I think I have ever met. I’m a disabled senior, and shopping alone is quite a chore & quite exhausting.
In need of assistance, I went through a main register with a cashier. She checked out groceries, as they piled up on the end of the belt, they just kept piling, higher & higher and she never stopped to bag my groceries. So, to stop my bread, chips, produce from getting damaged, I went over and started trying to assist but I was having trouble keeping up. They just kept coming. My total was a bit over $200, she took my payment, and walked off from behind her register, not saying a word. I began rebagging alone. She came back with her coat in her hand and on a face time call with a gentleman. Laughing and watching me. While her light was still on above her aisle to accept more customers for checkout.
She was definitely a bad seed that has slipped into your fold of outstanding employees that I have met while shopping. She is definitely in the wrong line of work.
I Love Meijer, I just hope I never meet another employee like her, it’s reasons like this, I switched over to your store.
Happy Shopping !!

I had an excellent experience today thanks to the outstanding service from a cashier named Jen or Jeni (apologies, I don’t remember the exact spelling). After checking out, I accidentally left the onions I had purchased behind and headed out to the parking lot.

I tend to have a little fun by "cart surfing"—riding on the back bar of the shopping cart like a scooter—and I had picked up some good speed heading to my truck, which was parked about as far from the store as possible.

To my surprise, when I reached my vehicle, Jen was right behind me, having run all the way across the lot just to return my forgotten onions. I was genuinely impressed by her effort and kindness.

Thank you, Jen, for going above and beyond—this was some of the best customer service I’ve ever received, and I truly appreciate it.

text.text:
I didn't buy as much as I had planned because they were doing construction and they were low stock or out of many items. And also I don't know if they were Meijer employees or contractors but they were barging through and nearly knocked me over with his pallet because he didn't look to see if somebody was standing there before he started moving the pallet with the pallet jack.

Then there was the rude checkout employee. I don't know what her problem was but there was no divider thing on the far end of the conveyor belt and I could not reach the one that was close to her. But then she shoved this watermelon and other things that belong to the other customer in front of me into my items and knocked stuff over. I gave her a look and she said something like you're supposed to use a divider. I said I can't reach that one. She gave me a dirty look and finished checking out the other customer. She didn't even slide it down towards me or anything like that. She was very short with me for the rest of the transaction. And I did nothing at all to her to elicit such an awful response from her.

And then of course the Mperks didn't work. Or at least some of the items.

Customer service employee was also rude. I was supposed to get Mperks for certain items and she demanded I hand her my phone to prove that the digital coupons were clipped. I refused. Because I'm not going to just hand somebody my phone. So she yelled at me and loudly said she couldn't do anything about me not getting my discount. So I returned everything that was Mperks related that did not do the correct coupon.

Then she didn't say anything when she finished running the return and putting the funds back onto my credit card so I stood there a few seconds because I didn't know if she was done with me and I had to ask her if the transaction was now completed and she got huffy about that too.

When I got home, the Meijer branded milk that does not expire until August 22nd which was in over a week from when I purchased it was already bad. So I guess I could go back and return it and talk to the rude customer service lady again. But perhaps I won't.

Won't shop there again.

text.text:
Normally this is a very good store with excellent staff. However, after countless visits, we had a bad experience tonight. Employee Michael who was working self checkout on the west end of the store at approx. 8:45 PM was extremely rude to my pregnant wife after she asked for assistance using a coupon. Even though she was the only person in the area at that time, apparently helping customers was a hindrance to his time on his smartphone.

Besides her having to walk up to him and ask for assistance even after the “help” light was on,” he was instantly annoyed that he had to stop scrolling on his phone. Initially, he flat out refused to help her, telling her she can’t use the coupon and that she would have to use it next time. She then asked if he could void the transaction so she could rescan and apply it. At this point, he huffed out loud and was visibly mad. After finally taking the two seconds to help her, he put down her items roughly in the bagging area.

Overall, not a great experience. Usually Meijer employees are really good but this guy would rather scroll TikTok, Grindr or whatever than do his job. Lastly, when attempting to bring this up to a supervisor or manager at the customer service desk, they just laughed. Go to a different location.

I assume he wanted to go home and didn't want to do any extra work.

He's basically telling me to go do his job. It was very unpleasant, very agitating, and unprofessional. I guess that's what you call a good scam. Or maybe a good tip for the store.

Because had I not walked back there and took a picture of the sign, I would have had to pay way more. The one way was marked to be I was appalled.

text.text: Usually a loyal Meijer customer but this location seems to be doing downhill. I’ve had multiple occasions where I accidentally purchased out of date/moldy food. The produce is largely subpar. Most of the carts are broken and the straps aren’t large enough to go around my baby. I’ve also frequently ordered curbside pickup and found many items were “out of stock” but I was able to go straight inside and find them myself. My last strike was during my most recent order. I ordered shaving cream and the item I received (although correct) clearly had a clearance sticker that was peeled off (I was charged full price— about $8) and the product was open and looked dirty. My experiences have been very disappointing because I’ve always chosen Meijer but it will now be considered as a last resort.

Unfortunately there is no way to edit your cart or even communicate with the shopper but there is a spot to write a note  for every single item and also a place to choose a substitute should your item not be available.

Then when your order is ready to be picked up you get another text and or email.

When you drive to pick up your order all you have to do is pull into the marked "pick-up" parking spaces on the right side of the building and  there is a sign that tells  you what spot you are in.  Then you just text the number on the sign with your last name and  spot number.  Within 3-5 minutes some incredibly kind, hard working and friendly person will appear and  load your groceries into your car for you.  I am so impressed with the customer service these folks provide.

Also, recently they re-paved the entire parking lot.  It was a mess while it was happening but now it looks incredible and so tidy.    Top marks!  Thanks you guys!

This store has a deli with fully cooked turkey for slicing, a slicer, and employees behind the counter. That’s all for show. When I tried to purchase a pound of sliced turkey from the Wauwatosa Outpost deli, their employee told me to go get a package of pre-sliced turkey from a refrigerated case across the aisle from the deli. I had already looked at those and they had been sliced two days prior. I told the employee I wanted fresh-cut slices, and instead of fulfilling my order, he gave the excuse that the pre-sliced packs were good for four days. That is when it became clear that I would have to go to another store to purchase that item. This wasn’t the first time over many years that an employee at this store had been unhelpful to me, but it will be the last time I provide that opportunity.

Reply to Outpost’s response: I reported this to the person working the service desk and he just said sorry. He wasn’t that sorry. I did contact the store manager by phone at 5:30 p.m. on Sept. 21, 2025, about this incident just a few minutes after it happened. He was disinterested. All I got was a “sorry about that” and “will look into it.” This business either does not care or it is staffed by people who do not care. It shows.

I told the employee I wanted fresh-cut slices, and instead of fulfilling my order, he gave the excuse that the pre-sliced packs were good for four days. That is when it became clear that I would have to go to another store to purchase that item. This wasn’t the first time over many years that an employee at this store had been unhelpful to me, but it will be the last time I provide that opportunity.

Reply to Outpost’s response: I reported this to the person working the service desk and he just said sorry. He wasn’t that sorry. I did contact the store manager by phone at 5:30 p.m. on Sept. 21, 2025, about this incident just a few minutes after it happened. He was disinterested. All I got was a “sorry about that” and “will look into it.” This business either does not care or it is staffed by people who do not care. It shows.

text.text:
A Bar in a Grocery Store… of Course! 🛒
We live in Milwaukee, Wisconsin — and for a couple who doesn’t drink, we sure know how to find all the bars!

Today’s adventure took us to Whole Foods Market for the very first time, and wow… this place is full of surprises. Inside one grocery store, we discovered:
🥗 The Olive Bar – I picked the marinated mushrooms, while Bill went for the classic jumbo green olives.
🍲 The Soup Bar – warm and inviting.
🍕 The Pizza Bar – we shared a slice of mushroom and caramelized onion pizza with a creamy white sauce. Delicious!
🍣 The Sushi Bar – we picked an avocado roll topped with garlic, ginger, and a touch of green mustard — unique and surprisingly tasty.

We couldn’t resist the bakery, either. Fresh loaves of bread stacked and ready — we chose a sourdough loaf, and they happily sliced it for us on the spot. 🥖✨

One thing we loved: Whole Foods has banned over 300 preservatives, sweeteners, and other artificial ingredients. That made our little food adventure even sweeter.

💡 Bonus surprise: At checkout, they asked if we had an Amazon account. I opened mine and — ta-da! — we got a nice little discount.

And just like any good adventure, it started with a sample right at the entrance. That’s how you know it’s going to be a fun place to shop! After filling our cart (and our tummies), we headed to the food court to taste our finds. Definitely adventure dining!

On to our next foodie find… 🚗✨

#WholeFoodsAdventure #MilwaukeeEats #FoodieFun #AdventureDining #LocalExplorers #GroceryGoals

Dear Whole Foods Management,

I am writing to express my disappointment and frustration regarding an unpleasant experience I had at your Evanston location on Saturday, May 17th at around 2:00 PM, specifically at the meat department.

I asked a male and a female staff member if a particular cut of meat was available. Both of them responded with clear signs of irritation. The male employee replied with, “I don’t know,” in a dismissive tone, and the overall attitude from both was extremely unprofessional and rude. After briefly checking in the back, they simply said, “We don’t have it,” in a very curt manner. The whole interaction left me feeling disrespected and unwelcome.

This experience was particularly disappointing because I have always encountered kind and helpful staff at other Whole Foods locations. Unfortunately, this visit has made me decide that I will not be returning to the Evanston store. I strongly believe that these employees need to be retrained on how to communicate respectfully and professionally with customers.

text.text:
I have been a frequent shopper at Whole Foods since the store opened. However, this evening I had a terrible customer service experience.

I wasn’t making a purchase but was returning some items through the Amazon return kiosk. While I was actively completing the return, the security guard, Jonathan, approached me and told me I had to leave because the store was closed. I explained that I only had two items left, and asked for just a couple of minutes to finish. Instead of allowing me to complete the return, he told me, “We’re open tomorrow—next time, come earlier,” and continued to insist that I leave.

During this entire exchange, I could have easily finished my return, but was forced to stop instead. As a store manager myself, with years of retail experience, I know it is not good customer service to force a customer out while they are actively completing business at the front of the store.

If this is actual store policy, I strongly urge you to reconsider. Customers should not be treated this way, and certainly not turned away while in the middle of a transaction. This type of service does not encourage loyalty or return business.

I'm fairly certain that if I had been purchasing something that evening, I would not have been forced out of the store. That makes it seem as though the store values customers only when they are spending money, but not when they are completing returns. This sends the wrong message-returns are still part of doing business, and customers should be treated with the same respect regardless.

I faced completely unacceptable treatment as a Black woman when I attempted to exchange spoiled blueberries. Despite not having a receipt, I was only looking to replace them with fresh ones. When I requested to speak with the manager, Luis confronted me with unfounded accusations of shoplifting and falsely claimed to be the manager. I firmly demanded to speak with a genuine manager, leading to Eric, who identified himself as a manager, checking my credit card for my shopping history—over a simple exchange of rotten blueberries.

When I asked for the store manager, MK, her response was dismissive, insisting that they were just doing their job. I challenged this idea, asserting that harassing a customer who is only trying to make a straightforward exchange is entirely unacceptable.

I later found the receipt in my car. It is notably concerning that my white husband had no issues returning a jar of tomato sauce without a receipt just a week earlier. This raises serious questions about whether policies are enforced differently based on race. The discriminatory treatment I experienced is not only obvious but absolutely intolerable.

I spend an exorbitant amount of money weekly at Whole Foods. Like many aspects of the store facing a decline in quality, the hot bar is no exception. The variety is absolutely pathetic. At the very least then make sure the food is fresh and palatable.
I picked up some samosas last night and should have been warned by their slightly rancid odor that I was making a big mistake. (By the way the redesign of the samosas is awful - they used to be a lovely, flatter triangle shape with a delicious flaky crust and the perfect amount of filling.)
I brought these little abominations home and they were not only smelly but hard as a rock and completely inedible. They had to be sitting there since lunch time. Maybe even were brought out as leftovers from the previous day.
This is completely unacceptable at these prices and just another indication that Whole Foods is no longer the pinnacle of grocery shopping. Where yes, it was expensive, but you were paying for QUALITY and uniqueness. I will never purchase another hot bar item again for fear that I'll waste my money and go without dinner like I did yesterday evening.

text.text:
Stepping into Whole Foods, you’re greeted by an atmosphere that’s fresh, vibrant, and undeniably upscale. The hot bar is the crown jewel—an incredible spread that feels like a global culinary tour. From fragrant curries to perfectly roasted meats and colorful veggie dishes, every option is bursting with flavor and freshness. Even kale becomes crave-worthy here, and the presentation rivals a five-star restaurant. The bakery is just as spectacular, with the tres leches cake stealing the spotlight. It’s absolute fire—moist, creamy, and perfectly balanced, each bite a dreamy indulgence. Flaky croissants, chewy cookies, and artisanal breads make it hard to leave empty-handed.
Unfortunately, the Amazon return area is a major disappointment. For a store under Amazon’s umbrella, the setup is shockingly inadequate. The space is far too small, creating chaos as lines spill into the aisles during peak hours. Staff are friendly but visibly stretched thin, making returns more frustrating than they should be.
Despite this flaw, Whole Foods remains a food lover’s paradise. The hot bar and bakery—especially that tres leches—keep me coming back. If they could expand and streamline the return area, it’d be near flawless.

text.text:
Whole Foods customer service needs some serious improvement.
I went there for an Amazon return, not knowing where to go, as there aren't any signs directing you, like at Kohls.

I finally made my way to the counter, and as I was pulling up my return info on my phone, an older gentleman came to do the same thing. The employee behind the counter directed him to use the machine, and clearly he was uncomfortable using it. So he said I could go in front of him and he would watch. I said, "ok, but I've never done it either, so we'll be learning together. " We both laughed. But the machine was in the middle of a reboot and the employee was so annoyed with us cause we were laughing saying how we might need some help. You should have seen the look he gave us. He then says. "I'll just take you up here." Again, sounding super annoyed cause he had to do his job instead of the machine doing it for him. It literally took him 1 click of a button to scan my QR code and that was it. Done! Literally 3 seconds. Now was that so hard friend? And I just thought about it... he didnt give me a receipt or anything.
I'm sure the older gentleman's return was just as easy. He didn't say thank u, have a nice day no nothing. All he said was, to the other employee standing there, was something to the fact that the situation "was annoying" as he rolled his eyes and shook his head, with a dirty look on his face.
I'm sorry I made u do ur job, and that the machine was in the middle of a reboot so IT couldn't do it for u.
Because of him, I will NEVER set foot into Whole Foods again. And I was excited to do some shopping when I was done with my return. But instead, I walked straight out the door!!!

text.text:
This is an understandably popular place for healthy food.  It's a go-to for us.  My one complaint, and it's a major one, is that a place like this ought to be different from run of the mill grocery outlets when it comes to needing to be really careful.  You still need to pay close attention to the ingredients lists if you're looking to fight having chemicals in your food.

One example is rapeseed oil.  It's a cheap lubricant and somebody decided it would be great to add it to our food.  Problems?  Well, first the name, so they must have held a ceremony and renamed it to Canola oil.  Problem solved, right?  Ah... No.  It's toxic.  So, not to be deterred, they figured out a way to process it so they could get enough poison out to be able to feed it to us.  And good luck trying to find food without it. You can do it, but it takes a lot of work.

It would sure be nice to have an oasis of sorts where you didn't need to work so hard to avoid chemicals in your food.  You'd think this might be that sort of place, wouldn't you?  I'm hoping...

text.text:
Meijer is one of those rare big-box stores that truly delivers on being a one-stop shop without sacrificing quality, cleanliness, or customer service. From the moment you walk in, it’s clear the store is well-organized and maintained to a high standard—aisles are wide and uncluttered, shelves are stocked, and everything is easy to find whether you’re here for a quick grocery run or a full household restock.

The grocery section is excellent, with fresh produce that’s consistently crisp and flavorful, a wide variety of meats and seafood, and bakery items that rival specialty shops. Their organic and gluten-free selections are impressive, and the layout makes it easy to shop for specific dietary needs. Beyond groceries, Meijer’s home goods, clothing, electronics, seasonal décor, and garden sections are well-curated with competitive pricing that often beats specialty retailers.

What really sets Meijer apart is their balance between national brands and their own store brand, which often matches or exceeds the quality of name brands at a better price. Weekly sales, digital coupons, and MPerks rewards make it even more budget-friendly without feeling like you’re compromising.

The staff here consistently go above and beyond—whether it’s someone walking you directly to an item instead of just pointing, a cashier who takes the time to bag carefully, or employees in every department who are approachable and knowledgeable. The checkout process is fast, with plenty of lanes open during busy hours and well-maintained self-checkout options for speed.

Parking is abundant and well-lit, carts are always available, and the store feels safe and welcoming no matter the time of day. In short, Meijer makes errands easier, faster, and more pleasant while offering a huge selection at a great value. Whether you’re doing a big weekly haul, picking up a last-minute dinner ingredient, or browsing seasonal deals, Meijer consistently delivers a smooth and satisfying shopping experience.

text.text:
It sucks that this is the only coop near by.  This store is just trash now, and has been for a while.  If you go after 6pm on any given night, they are already taking down their hot bars.  So when I go at 7:30. I'm expecting them to already be down. But then you stand there to get service and the 4 different people that you see, "all doing something MORE IMPORTANT" don't help you.  The one guy that did acknowledge me says "Someone will be with you shortly. we're all doing closing something down."  Then he procedes to wipe his soup bar.  So I stood there a few more moments and was like. whatever, decided to leave.  You get up front. and the customer service person, is on her phone. The cashier is on her phone.  I was about to just take what i was buying, and not ring it up,  but I didn't.  I understand that the grocery business is a 1% business and hard to make good profits.  I go in this store multiple times / week and have for years.  But honestly it pisses me off everytime i do.  Should just start shopping elsewhere..  Watch your camera footage on 9/15/2025 at 7:45pm at deli, for a reall shitty time.

Oh and since, im in the mood.  Many years ago, i was going to get a membership there.. In there defense, it was 8:45pm at night, so they were ready to go home soon, but I asked how big of a deal is it to get a membership right now." and their answer was "right now?  It's a big deal." lol.  Are you kidding me.?  You fill out a form.  its take about a minute, and give them $100.

Now i have a Lakewinds membership but don't get to use it because I don't live by one.  Like i said, i shop here multiple times / week. I like some of the workers.  I talk to a few of the meat guys once in a while, and they are always good stuff.  But it's a terrible experience every time i go in there after 6pm.  for years now.  just had it tonight.  I spend thousands of dollars a year here for the last decade, and they can't stay off their phones. What a joke.  And the deli... every time.  Put a bell up to ring.  Or teach your people to help the customers.

The thought of having to go to lunds and byerlys sucks, and Kowalski's or lakewinds isnt near by.  ugh.  Disgruntled customer.   Might stop showing up. srsly.  get better.

First time here, had no agenda, looked throughout the store, especially the meat department, which had some very good looking cuts, and the fish looked fresh. I ventured over to the bakery and deli area and looked around. I was tempted upon finding a leek tart! - but decided to go back and get a very nice looking simple, well marbled chuck roast. Also picked up a couple of potatoes and sweet potatoes, apparently organic and locally sourced products. The picture speaks for itself.
For my first time there our grocery cart of items was out of the normal price range for our average shopping experience. It was over $200 -but I think the quality that I saw is also above average. Nice butcher shop!

text.text:
I’ve been shopping at this Whole Foods location every Saturday for the past three years. Typically, staff are restocking shelves from store opening (8:00 AM) until around 10:00 AM, which I understand — though in such a small store, it does make navigating the aisles more difficult.

However, today’s visit (10/18/25 between 8:25–9:00 AM) was an unusually negative experience. While walking through the ramen/chips aisle — which was especially crowded with 2–3 carts and three employees (two women and one man) — I heard the male employee comment, “I don’t know why you’re in this aisle,” as I tried to pass. I was between him and the two women workers at that moment.

I ignored the comment and continued trying to exit the aisle, but both female employees did not move or acknowledge my presence when I said “excuse me” and attempted to pass. I had to lift my cart to squeeze through.

As I was leaving, the male staff member began making strange noises and laughed loudly in an exaggerated way, running out of the aisle as though mocking the situation. It felt very unprofessional and disrespectful.

This is not the standard I’ve come to expect. Every other time I visit, staff are courteous, move out of the way when customers approach, and even offer assistance. But this interaction stood out for all the wrong reasons. It left me feeling uncomfortable and unwelcome in a store I’ve supported weekly for years.

The store always smells good and the warm and cold salad bar is always good and fresh. I’m an Amazon Prime member and it’s also nice to get occasional discounts and perks.

The dessert bakery is excellent and I have fun picking out all of their mini desserts.

Non food items such as vitamins, shampoos, etc are really nice too. Sorta spendy stuff but the quality speaks volumes.

One thing I miss is the Jamba Juice. Miss having that before or after my shopping.

Overall, I’ve been using this location for at least three years.  It is a good location that is close by and has convenient on site parking that is free.  It has a huge selection of great produce, protein, etc…

My issue is with customer service as of late.  I’ve never had an issue and they were always very friendly, helpful and kind.

However, in the last couple months, it has taken a sharp nosedive overall.  The main area I’ve had personal experiences that were horrible were at the deli that were fairly rude to not just me but other customers.  On one day, I was just straight up ignored for minutes before I just gave up and walked away.  If they had even acknowledged that I was there and said to give them a minute, that would have been something but they just straight-up pretended I wasn’t standing there and being a tall person, it’s not like I was hiding.

Overall, still it’s probably the physically nicest Whole Foods I’ve been too.  I wish they carried more unique or local stuff (like Down to Earth Organic), but it is still good.  And many of the folks working there are still great, just hope they shift direction with a lot of the newly hired folks.

text.text:
Unsanitary Practices During Refrigerated Food Replenishment

There are ongoing concerns regarding unsanitary practices observed during the replenishment of refrigerated food products at your store. Specifically, staff members have been seen stepping onto the lower deck of refrigerated displays—where food items are stored—instead of using appropriate equipment such as stepladders, step stools, or reacher tools.
This behavior poses significant hygiene and safety concerns, as employees are stepping directly onto food display surfaces with footwear that may be contaminated. There is no way to determine what substances or debris may be transferred from their shoes onto these surfaces, creating potential risks to food safety and public health.
During a visit to the store on October 6, 2025, I personally witnessed two female staff members standing on the top edge of a refrigerated unit while restocking soups. One employee had her cart blocking the display area while standing on the unit, and another (identified as Rhonda) was walking along the edge of the refrigerator, restocking the upper shelves. Despite customers being present and attempting to view products, the staff continued their task without acknowledging the obstruction or safety concern.
This incident raises questions about what other unsanitary or unsafe practices might be occurring in less visible areas of the store.
Store management on duty, Bob and Rhonda, were notified at the time of the incident.
Recommendation: It is strongly advised that management take immediate steps to address this issue by:
* Providing proper equipment such as stepladders or reach tools
* Implementing and enforcing hygiene and safety protocols
* Training staff on safe and sanitary product handling practices

text.text: Good produce and gourmet food selection if you go there to shop but a disappointing employer. I would caution to anyone considering employment here to get your job offer in writing, take time to decide if it's right for you, and don't put all your eggs in one basket by committing to a role until you've actually worked in it and know that you will be doing the work/position agreed upon. After reading the poor employment experiences online and hearing stories about past employees in the store (not a single positive or kind thing) and noticing that no other employees seemed to work there very long, I asked for my offer in writing and then I sat down with an attorney to go over it. I would encourage anyone else receiving an offer to do the same. There are no formal internal HR policies (no HR at all so employees have no advocacy), no hiring process (interview, onboarding, training/support, etc.), no rewards structure or career ladder, and no benefits. There's no disciplinary structure either, and no job protection of any kind--regardless of whether it's full-time salaried or part-time hourly--so you can gather why no employees seem to ever be there. It is good starting pay, but that's about it. If you get a job, leave yourself a way out, and absolutely don't depend on it for your livelihood. Stand up for yourself to get lunches, breaks, and days off and to not be overworked. Seriously expect to not have a job the next day, no matter how hard you work or how well you do. Be your own advocate. Read the other reviews on this business. It took the other girl a lot of courage to write her review and not take it down after being threatened.

I had the pleasure of discovering Juneau Natural, Southeast Alaska's only specialty organic grocery store, and I can't sing their praises enough. This gem of a business offers an exceptional shopping experience both in-store and online, making it incredibly convenient for locals and visitors alike.

One of the standout features is their commitment to serving the community by providing daily in-store and online shopping options. This means you can access their high-quality organic products whenever you need them, whether you're strolling through their welcoming store or shopping from the comfort of your home.

But what truly sets Juneau Natural apart is their innovative approach to shipping. Offering shipping on Alaska Seaplanes ensures that even those in remote areas can access their carefully curated selection of organic goods. It's a game-changer for anyone in Southeast Alaska looking to prioritize health-conscious living.

What's more, Juneau Natural's Reward Points and Membership Program are a real boon for savvy shoppers. The program not only offers great savings but also encourages sustainable, healthy choices every day. It's a win-win!

In conclusion, Juneau Natural is a shining example of a local small business that goes above and beyond to provide exceptional organic products and services. Their dedication to the community, convenient shopping options, and innovative shipping methods make them a true asset to Southeast Alaska. Don't miss out on the opportunity to shop with them and experience the difference for yourself!

text.text:
EarthFare has a wonderful selection of organic and heirloom produce and artesian everything as well as bulk foods (which are hard to find) and very pleasant employees. They also revitalized a derilict shopping center's anchor store and gave the whole strip new life--major props for good citizenship.

The meat department has many organic and free range choices. The deli has things I haven't tasted elsewhere. The cheese corner is a delight, as is the young lady who (wo)man's  it. They have an impressive selection of craft beers in the cooler. Their prepared foods are also extensive and look delicious. They have sushi you can eat without trepidation and the excellent pre-cooked whole chicken is $5 daily. There is also a fresh juice bar.

As a very experienced bread and pie  baker, who became gluten intolerant late in life, the bakery makes me want to weep for joy. You should go crazy and try every kind of bread EF makes, such is the impression of what I've seen and smelled. The crackle of the fresh loaves is not something you can get outside NYC. I haven't seen bread like this short of my own kitchen.

As groceries go, EF is a little pricey, but what you get for the price is amazing selection and very high quality food given to you by people who actually seem kinda okay with their world, not *forcibly* cheery over top of personal misery (like at the big W).

Some things are worth paying for.

text.text: Best Bulk Bins! They have liquids such as honey, olive oil, & vinegar in bulk. Some comments say this is like Whole Foods or Fresh Market - I DISAGREE! The quality is much higher. Today was my first time in; the butcher told me that ALL their meat meets non-GMO, antibiotic free, cruelty free standards. They also have a "Food Boot List"; they boot "dirty" foods with 108 ingredients that are banned from their stores including artificial preservatives, MSG, trans-fats, Sodium Hexametaphosphate, & High Fructose Corn Syrup . (I checked out their website for this.) Earth Fare fills a serious whole in the market for people who want REAL FOOD in their bulk bins and not just a bunch of junk food. If you're environmentally conscious and don't want to purchase food in tons of one-time use plastic, Earth Fare seems to be a much better choice as their staff is accommodating; you can bring your own bags or jars to fill and they will tare off the weight. Their bulk bins have just about everything you need: several types of rice, flours, beans & nuts galore; best bulk in the area (I live in VA Beach, so I'm considering all of Hampton Roads). In addition, their organic fresh food is much better than WF or FM because Earth Fare has a good amount of Organic that's not wrapped in needless plastic. Yes, there is some needless plastic, but definitely less than at other grocery stores. For people who want CLEAN FOOD, Earth Fare is definitely filling a niche! I'm super glad to have a choice finally!!!!

text.text: Truly disgusting customer service. Never in my life, I just moved to Virginia and I've been to this store a couple times and I've never experienced an employee get into a customer's face unprovoked. Over a WATERMELON. At 7:20 pm today 9/1/25  I went in today with my mother we're at self check out. We grab a watermelon a small one it said $4.49. Anyway it scanned $7.99 not a big deal I just asked the check out woman if it was just misplaced. She's repeating that's the price I said okay well then can we just remove It. She asks "WHY? It's just a watermelon it's not a big deal." I explain and show her the picture calmly I apologize for the confusion if it was my fault. She starts talking over me and says "YOURE NOT LISTENING TO ME ARE YOU HEARING ME" She was yelling directly in my face the entire time. I take a step back she turns to my mother who's bagging and says it's on sale when you have the giants card. She's now directly facing my mother who doesn't speak the language and she's aggressively asking her what the problem is. My mom gestures no and I once again ask her to remove the watermelon she continues asking why we don't use the card and if we don't have it to get it. I repeat again for the 3rd or 4th time to just remove the watermelon. She begins to yell at us causing a scene saying why its just a watermelon. I tell her she's speaking over me she scans a card it's now discounted I tell her I just don't want it anymore it wasn't the price now it's the service the disrespect her tone of voice we're uncomfortable. I just wanted to pay for my other items and leave. Prema I believe sighed loudly and said don't talk to me like that relax and we're calm again my mom and I just said we don't have the card just remove the watermelon please. My mom tries to just calm her down and says I'm sorry she yells give me the watermelon and snatches it directly from my hands. She voids it angrily and we paid got our receipt. I head to customer service ask to see a manager woman wouldn't provide her name at the self check out or provide me with anyone's information/ email a time I could speak to anyone or even the woman's name in self check out. Nothing no information just annoyed. Customer service woman repeats "my manager isn't here, they left for the night." That was it also rude and vague. Finally I beg her to write any information she writes the store number on a sticky note? My only real problem is with the self check out older woman employee that made a scene over a small watermelon. It escalated for absolutely no reason. It could've been a complete misunderstanding on my part but she wouldn't stop harassing us about the giants card wouldn't void the item didn't have to yell in my mothers face in front of everyone. As we went to customer service she ran right behind us to see what we said to the woman working that counter. My sole complaint is this older woman gray long hair always at self check out glasses. Name I believe is prema or prima. I will be looking into filing a formal complaint because everyones just unprofessional at this point. I felt unsafe, i never imagined one question leading up to her humiliating an elder woman. Honestly convinced she's racist.

Not just her, the other employees did not mention programs offered to shoppers and I had spent a lot of money there. My experience happened one weekend around 2001.  I had spent more than $450 in one visit. The next evening, I returned because I had forgotten to purchase a few additional items. I spent $75+ this day. While in line, I overheard this cashier speaking to an older caucasian male shopper about points you earn when you shop there to receive free items. No one ever mentioned this to me. So when this cashier processed my items, I kindly asked her about the points and if they could be added from the evening before because I had not heard of this. She replied, "uh, No". This cashier who so pleasantly described this program to the gentleman ahead of me suddenly became very rude. I was shocked and highly disappointed, but I simply and quietly said to her, I spent more than $450 here yesterday. No one mentioned this to me. I never returned to purchase anything else from this store. And now, after reading several reviews regarding discrimination against POC (people of color), over the past few years, I see this is their culture.

To sum it up I found a new store. We love this place.

text.text:
Mom's,
How do I love thee?
Let me count the ways!

Outside of the stellar customer service Mom's employees provide, what I love most about this organic market is that they are one of the few (if only) grocer in the DM(V) that sells Certified Humane meat from local farmers that go through a rigorous process to get the certification. I have become more conscious about the food I consume. While I'm no vegan, since I eat meat, I care about how the food I consume was handled and treated during it's incarnation (or lifetime).

Energy is energy. I don't care to consume anything from an animal that was not humanely treated. My temple deserves better. Mom's creates space in a competing market where we are flooded with food that is mishandled in various different ways with food that is handled humanely and with care and for that I am most grateful.

What I also love is how the store is always clean. I have never seen a spill in isle 9 that I had to notify management about. The produce is always beautifully presented. Everything is! It's a beautiful store to shop in and experience.

If you have questions about anything, an employee is always readily available to help. They don't go and send you to find whatever you're looking for yourself, they walk with you and oftentimes they will go get it themselves. That level of customer service anywhere is almost obsolete.

What I love most about Mom's is how they aren't just another business looking to exploit its customers with inflating prices for goods not worth their price tag, no. Mom's is an embedded member of the community and they act as such. Whether it's their recycling program or their pledge to their employees to provide a fair wage. They care and it is reflected in everything they do.

I really cannot say enough about Mom's. If I had to complain about anything, I'd say, I wish there were more of them. Do yourself a favor and shop Mom's today!

I start off by saying Carlos & Curtis!!! Ok... My experience? I was in South Beach for a few days. I was sleeping irregular & eating very unhealthy & I definitely felt dehydrated. My body told me, "to go to the Whole Foods". I called Uber & headed for the whole food on 11th & Alton South Beach. I was greeted by security & felt very welcome.... I headed to the produce section. There I was approached by Carlos. He made great suggestions... Watermelon & fresh lemonade ginger mint & garlic... For natural herbal tea. I headed to the prepared food section & a tall African associate informed me the menu had changed & apologized for the limited options... I picked a few items & headed to check out. After scanning most of my items a woman with a Caribbean accent accused me of stealing. I was feeling lethargic and weak... I began to cry... I called for security & another associate (I believe she was from India) she started to calm me when my accuser called Curtis and further accused me of theft. Her presence antagonized me... She continued to watch me even after two managers, an associate & security were consoling me. Just wanted to leave I was ashamed & embarrassed. Carlos came out of nowhere & hugged me. I burst into tears & felt relief. Curtis insisted I just pay for what was scanned. I called and Uber & was escorted out by Curtis who offered me a gift card& an apology. I felt loved. This was the greatest customer recovery I have ever experienced. I was angry, sad, insulted & disrespected. Carlos & Curtis made a 180° change to the situation & my emotional state. I left with a smoke & tears of joy.

A few days later I ordered from , "too good to go app". I called a head & requested Carlos to assist me. When I arrived to pick up my order Carlos was there greeting & assisting me & walked me out .... No!!! Carlos excorted me out to my awaiting Uber.

I wanted to complain but I had the greatest experience at this whole foods. I would describe it as a lifelong, positive & permanent memory.

CARLOS, THANK YOU MY BROTHER.

humbley, sincerely & most appreciated

BRANDON K. CARTER

text.text: Firstly,  I have to say that I visit Whole Foods at minimum once per week. This location in particular about once month since I go to that area for meetings. Today I was really disappointed and disgusted at the lack of professionalism and utter pettiness of the cashier and her supervisor. I picked up several items including a bottle of sparkling water and noticed there were two signs in that location. One states $1.79 and the other $2.99. Confused as to why several similar bottles were put in that location with 2 different amounts, I took a photo just in case there would be any discrepancy at checkout. I didn't get the name of the cashier, but she was a black lady with dark loose curls and with a Jamaican accent. She rang up the items and the water rang up for $2.50. I informed her that there were two signs with two different amounts where the water was located.She started speculating that one price maybe the Amazon Prime price. I told her it couldn't be because there was not a "sale" sign there.  I showed her the photo I took. She then left to allegedly verify what I had told her. When she came back,  she told me that one price was for mineral water and the other for the sparking water. I told her that if there was only an isolated bottle or two under the cheaper price, I could have understood that they may have been misplaced by customer(s); however, there seemed to be about an entire case of the same water in that section. The cashier decided to get her supervisor involved (short black lady with bleached hair). She was no better. Her overall demeanor was unprofessional and she refused to make eye contact with me. They both could have expeditiously resolved the situation, but they chose to drag it on for several minutes at the expense of myself and the other customers waiting in line. In the end, the supervisor decided to adjust the price to my favor. A few cents credit took a whole ordeal of back and forth and defensiveness from them. I have noticed a significant breakdown in customer service at Whole foods in general in the past year or so. I expect this type of attitude in lower end stores. Perhaps my expectations are too high and I should  I shouldn't be expecting more considering who owns it.

text.text:
I’ve always enjoyed Whole Foods for its friendly atmosphere and great selection, but my last visit really changed my perspective. My wife and I have been regulars every week, yet this time I saw something I couldn’t ignore—a woman I’d describe as a junkie left a baby in a stroller outside in 98-degree heat. I can’t understand why the store would allow this.

Panhandling is illegal in our county, and our community has programs in place to help those in need. This kind of behavior has never been part of our neighborhood, and I don’t think we should start accepting it now. When I took a photo, she flipped me off—that’s not the kind of scene I ever expected to encounter here.

In my opinion, Whole Foods should take responsibility for what happens on their sidewalk. We should be promoting our existing community support systems, not allowing unsafe or scam-like situations to take root. That’s how I feel, and since it is my personal opinion, it is beyond contestation.

text.text: The high quality and large variety of products is undeniable. However, they do everything in their power to squeeze the last penny out of you they can. For instance, a loaf of their challah bread is up to two dollars more expensive than the price in the kroger and fresh marker stores near by (the bread is done by the same miami onion company). Actually, it is not the very same bread since WF reduced the weigh of the loaf from 16oz to 15oz (none else has done this) so they can improve their margins by an additional 1/16... This is a good example of unjustified corporate greed. They will go as far as you let them!

text.text:
The atmosphere of this store was exemplary—everything one could hope for in a grocery shopping experience. Carts and baskets were readily available, the lighting was bright and welcoming, and the store layout was intuitive and easy to navigate. Each aisle was impeccably organized, with products neatly arranged and in their proper places.

At checkout, multiple lanes were open, with staff members actively greeting customers and directing them to available registers. The associate at my register was exceptionally friendly, engaging in a pleasant conversation about one of my purchases. Additionally, another staff member who was not assisting a customer stepped in to help with bagging, ensuring a smooth and efficient checkout process. Both employees were cheerful, professional, and seemed genuinely enthusiastic about their roles, which contributed to a truly positive and enjoyable experience.

text.text: Went in specifically for a goat mozzarella cheese.  Unfortunately, they don't carry it at this location,  but they were able to steer me towards a buffalo mozzarella that's also very tasty and lactose free. I picked up some farm raised salmon(skin on) because it looked pretty good.  Getting in to this shopping center was a bit of a pain,  but the Whole Foods parking lot is well designed and has plenty of parking.  Lots of other stores around it as well. They have a good variety of vegan, gluten free, dairy free, soy free options on the shleves as well as at the hot bar. They had plenty of cashiers when I visited, I didn't have to use the self checkout. Found Katz gluten free cinnamon buns and a few other items.  They have the seaside English cheddar that my wife loves.
